# Watch VexVoid play live.

AIVJ is VexVoid’s live channel: audio-visual sets mixed live in the browser. Watch the first three minutes without signing in. After that it’s 1p a minute from your bWalletX, straight to the artist.

## How it works

### Open and watch

Go to aivj.website/live. No account, no sign-in. Tap for sound.

### Carry on with bWalletX

After three minutes, pay 1p a minute to VexVoid. Pick a cap of 15, 30 or 60 minutes and approve once.

### Stop any time

Close the page and the meter stops.

Every penny goes to VexVoid, the artist.

Fans who hold 100 or more $VEXVOID pay 0.8p a minute.

When there’s no set on, the page shows the schedule.

[Open AIVJ Live](https://aivj.website/live)[VexVoid on bChatX](https://chat.bwalletx.com/u/vexvoid)[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

More from VexVoid: [the VexVoid artist page](https://bwalletx.com/artists/vexvoid). Thank them any time with a [tip](https://bwalletx.com/tips).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts.

# bWalletX for Android

The full bWalletX wallet on your Android phone or tablet. Your keys stay on your device.

[Download APK (beta) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-android-5.2.45.apk)

It isn't on Google Play yet, so install it by hand. (The store edition, bWallet, is in a Google Play internal test: see [/testers/bwallet/android](https://bwalletx.com/testers/bwallet/android).)

- Tap Download APK on your Android device.

- If Android asks, allow your browser to install unknown apps (Settings › Apps › your browser › Install unknown apps).

- Open `bwalletx-android-5.2.45.apk` and tap Install.

- Open bWalletX and create or restore your wallet.

Updating from an older version? Install over the top and your wallet stays. If Android says the app can't be updated, write down your 12 words first, then uninstall and reinstall.

Version 5.2.45 beta · 24.1 MB · Android 7+ · SHA-256 c539055522e144844711c0aea5af03601d6b00ca8ed77a7557e3ffeda6146b04

Also: [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension) · [Developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

# Ask

Ask b

[Ask b](https://web.bwalletx.com/ask-b)

Just ask.
b helps.

b lives inside bWalletX. Type a question in your own words, and b answers, or does it with you.

In the bWallet App Store / Google Play edition, b works with your own AI provider key only.

Send money. Tell b who and how much. b fills it in, and nothing goes until you say so.

Make a pot. A holiday, rent, a gift. b asks what it's for, how much and until when, and sets it up.

Explain things. What's this payment? What does locking do? Plain answers, no jargon.

Fix problems. Something not working? b looks into it with you and helps put it right.

Where to find b

- [web.bwalletx.com/ask-b](https://web.bwalletx.com/ask-b)

- [bchatx.com/ask-b](https://web.bwalletx.com/m/ask-b)

- In the bWalletX apps: tap b. [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get?from=ask-b)

b is us

Talking to b means talking to our team. b is the bWalletX team’s assistant: an AI model (Claude, from Anthropic) run by our server at The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd, answering on our behalf. When something breaks or confuses you, telling b is the quickest way for it to reach us. We read those conversations and fix things quickly. [Watch the film](https://bwalletx.com/talk-to-b).

Your chats with b. Chats with b aren’t secret from us, because b is us. They travel encrypted over HTTPS, and our team reads them so we can help you. Your keys and 12 words are different: they never leave your device.

What we keep. Your conversations with b, on our server, for up to 180 days. Only our team and our server can read them, and each message is also sent to our AI provider (Anthropic) to write b’s reply. We never sell conversations, and we don’t use them for advertising.

Improving b. We may use conversations, with personal details removed, to improve b. You can opt out: email [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=b%20opt-out) with the subject ‘b opt-out’ and we’ll exclude your chats.

Never type secrets to b. Not your 12 words, private keys, passwords, backup files or API keys. The wallet strips anything that looks like a recovery phrase or private key before it leaves your device, and our server strips secrets again before anything is kept, but please don’t rely on it. Nobody at bWalletX will ever ask for them. If you ever typed them, move your money to a new wallet.

Want them deleted? Email [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=Delete%20my%20b%20conversations) and we will delete your conversations with b.

Your own AI key? Then b’s replies come straight from the provider you chose (Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter), and your messages go to that provider under its own terms. Anything you report to b still comes to us.

What stays on your device, and what we see

Stays with you. Your keys and your 12 words stay on your device; we never hold them and can’t move your money. Sealed contracts on bChatX are encrypted to the people who sign them. A passkey backup of your 12 words is encrypted so only your passkey opens it.

We can see. Chats with b. Bug reports and ideas you send to b or on [/bugs](https://bwalletx.com/bugs). Room messages, which are stored on our server, and feed posts, which go on the public blockchain. Direct messages, which are stored on our server and are not end-to-end encrypted.

Talking to a person. Email [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com); that is ordinary email, read by us. To report a security problem, follow [b-Aware](https://bwalletx.com/b-aware). The full detail is in our [privacy policy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy#b).

Status, 25 Oct 2026

- Live: a consent sheet before your first message to b, naming where it goes.

- Live: the wallet refuses to send anything that looks like a recovery phrase or private key.

- Live: this section and “Conversations with b” in the [privacy policy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy#b).

- Live: deletion on request by email to support@bwalletx.com.

- ◻ Rolling out: server-side storage of b conversations for up to 180 days, with secrets stripped again on the server.

- ◻ Coming: plainer wording inside the wallet, so every Ask b screen says the same as this page.

- ◻ Coming: delete your b conversations yourself, in the app.

Help and support

Stuck, or something not working? Here is how to reach us.

- Ask b in the app. Tap b and describe the problem in your own words. b looks into it with you, and our team reads what you tell b, so nothing gets lost.

- Email us: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com). Never send your 12 words, password or backup file to anyone, including us.

- Report a bug: [bwalletx.com/bugs](https://bwalletx.com/bugs), or tap Report to b on any error in the app.

- Talk to other users: [the Lounge](https://bwalletx.com/lounge), the chat room every bWalletX user can join.

Quick answers

Lost or new phone? Install bWalletX and choose Restore, then use your 12 words or your encrypted backup file. [How restoring works](https://bwalletx.com/restore).

Can you get my money back? No. bWalletX is self-custody: your keys stay on your device and we never hold them, so we can’t see, move or recover your funds. Keep your 12 words safe and offline.

What does it cost? The app is free. Bitcoin SV network fees are usually a fraction of a penny per payment.

Does your team read my chats with b? Yes. b is us, and we read what you tell b so we can help. See [b is us](#b-is-us), our [privacy policy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy#b) and [terms](https://bwalletx.com/terms).

## Less noise. More life.

[Ask b](https://web.bwalletx.com/ask-b)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/b-aware

# b-Aware

Responsible disclosure and bug bounty for bWalletX and bWallet · Policy version 4 · 26 October 2026

bWallet and bWalletX are non-custodial. If you find a way to take or spend someone's money, read their keys or
recovery phrase, or make the wallet sign something its owner did not approve, tell us first. We fix it, we
credit you, and we pay for it in BSV.

[Report](#report) [Rewards](#rewards) [Scope](#scope)
[Safe harbour](#safe-harbour) [Known and accepted](#known)
[Advisories](#advisories) [Credits](#credits)

## How to report

-
Check [bwalletx.com/bugs](https://bwalletx.com/bugs) first. Known and already-fixed issues are listed there and earn
credit, not money. Still-unfixed security issues are not listed, for safety: if you found something serious
that is not there, report it privately as below.

-
Email [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=b-Aware) with the subject line
`b-Aware`. Put the report in the mail itself: the edition and version (Settings › About), the
steps, what happens, and why it matters. Steps we can run beat a video.

- If it lets an attacker move funds or read keys, say so in the subject so it is read first.

-
Do not open a public GitHub issue or a public bug report for a security finding. Ordinary bugs go to
[Bugs](https://bwalletx.com/bugs) (tell b in the app) or
[github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet/issues](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet/issues).

-
Never send us a recovery phrase, private key, password or key file. Use a throwaway wallet to demonstrate.

What you can expect from us: an acknowledgement within 2 working days, a severity and a fix plan within
7 days, and a note when the fix ships. Our machine-readable contact is at
[/.well-known/security.txt](https://bwalletx.com/.well-known/security.txt); the policy also lives in the repository as
[SECURITY.md](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## What we pay

Rewards are paid in BSV to an address you give us, within 30 days of the fix being live on every channel
(including the App Store and Chrome Web Store) or 60 days after we confirm your report, whichever is first. We
pay in one batch each month. Reports received before 25 October 2026 keep the earlier terms: 14 days from the
fix shipping or 30 days from triage.

Severity
What it looks like in bWallet
Reward

Critical
Steal or spend funds, extract keys or the recovery phrase, sign without the owner's approval
10 BSV

High
Bypass an approval or permission, forge a pairing or connection, drain through a dApp endpoint
3 BSV

Medium
Leak private data, defeat the safety filter, deny a user their own wallet
0.5 BSV

Low
Real but contained
Credit

### The rules that bound it

-
A pool, not an open tap. The reward pool is 20 BSV per calendar quarter. When it is spent, valid
reports still earn credit and are paid from the next quarter's pool, in the order they were triaged. We are a
small company and would rather say this than quietly stop paying. The pool balance and every payout are public on [/bounties](https://bwalletx.com/bounties).

-
First valid report wins. Duplicates, issues we already know about and anything listed under
[Known and accepted](#known) earn credit, not money.

-
Proof required. A working reproduction against a wallet you control. Scanner output or an AI-written
report with no reproduction is closed politely.

-
Severity is by impact on users' money and keys, not by CVSS alone. We set it and explain the reasoning
in writing; if you disagree, say so and we will look again.

- One reward per root cause, even where it shows up in several places.

-
We pay people we can name. Every payout is recorded: who, which address, how much, and the
transaction. Under 1 BSV, a stable handle and a paymail or address is enough. For 1 BSV or more (every High
and Critical), you need to verify your identity with Veriff in bWallet, and we pay only to an address of the
wallet that holds that verified identity; a typed name and country is no longer enough. The reward is held
for you, not lost, until you verify. To verify, open bWallet and go to Settings › Identity › Verify your
identity (or use the account page on bChatX); it takes about two minutes. We never see your ID documents:
Veriff holds them, and your wallet keeps only a signed certificate that says you are verified. This applies to
every unpaid reward of 1 BSV or more from 26 October 2026, including earlier reports. If you would rather stay
anonymous, you still get credit, but not a payment of 1 BSV or more.

## Scope

In scope (the code is open at
[github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet)):

- Key handling, signing and approvals: the background wallet, the approval sheets and the USB key flow.

- Storage, backup and the remote storage provider.

-
The BRC-100 dApp bridge: the injected provider, the content script, the extension side panel and in-page
sheet, the mobile dApp browser and its per-origin endpoints, pairing of computers and the CLI.

- Paymail, OpNS names, the Name Store, pots and subscriptions, agent accounts.

- The iOS and Android apps, the Chrome extension, and the web wallet.

Out of scope:

- The marketing sites and this page.

- Rate limiting, missing security headers, best-practice notes with no exploit.

-
Self-XSS, clickjacking on pages with nothing to click, anything that needs a rooted or jailbroken device or
physical access to an unlocked phone.

- Social engineering of our staff or users.

- Services we do not run: indexers, exchanges, HandCash, the Yours Wallet upstream.

## Safe harbour

Research done in good faith under this policy is authorised. We will not pursue, or support, legal action
against you for it, and if a third party does, we will say publicly that you acted under this policy. Good faith
means: you test against your own wallets and your own funds; you do not access, change or destroy anyone else's
data or money; you do not degrade the service for other people; and you give us a reasonable time to fix before
you publish. We will not ask you to sign anything to be paid.

## Known and accepted

Things we already know about. Reports of these earn credit only.

-
DNS rebinding of an app's own origin. In browser runtimes the wallet cannot pre-resolve DNS, so a site
could point its own hostname at a private address after we verify it. The fetch is still limited to that
site's HTTPS origin with no redirects; the same limitation is documented by the upstream reference wallet (see
the 20 October advisory below).

-
Connected wallets hold operating balances. A BRC-100 wallet signs what its owner approves; it cannot
judge intent. Keep savings in a wallet that is not connected to apps.

## Advisories and our responses

Published advisories that touch BRC-100 wallets, the BSV TypeScript stack or our dependencies, with what bWallet
does about each. Newest first.

### 20 October 2026 · SSRF hardening of BRC-100 manifest fetching (bsv-desktop)

Source: [bsv-blockchain/bsv-desktop#135](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/bsv-desktop/pull/135),
opened 20 October 2026, no CVE or GHSA id at the time of writing. Not affected

What it is. A BRC-100 wallet fetches `https://<app>/manifest.json` to show an app's
declared permissions in one grouped prompt. In the Electron reference wallet that fetch ran in the privileged
main process on a URL the renderer supplied, which is a server-side request forgery surface: a page could make
the wallet process reach localhost or a private network. The pull request requires HTTPS on the default port
with a `manifest.json` path, rejects localhost, private, reserved and non-public IP addresses
including DNS results, refuses redirects, caps the body at 1 MiB, restricts the IPC handler to the main frame
and removes the renderer's fallback to an unrestricted fetch.

bWallet's position. bWallet does not have the mechanism the fix addresses. There is no privileged
"fetch this URL" channel between a page and the wallet: the background never fetches a URL a page supplies.
The manifest fetch happens inside the wallet toolbox's permissions manager (we ship wallet-toolbox-client
2.14.5 and @bsv/sdk 2.8.11), which builds the URL from the originator rather than accepting one, goes through
the SDK's public-HTTPS fetch (HTTPS only, no credentials, pinned to that origin, IP literals must be public),
refuses redirects, caps the body at 256 KiB and times out after 10 seconds. The originator itself is not
chosen by the page: the extension rejects any message whose originator does not match the browser's
`sender.origin`, and the mobile app derives it from the verified origin of the per-site endpoint.
The only host a site can make the wallet contact is therefore its own.

Residual and shared. In browser runtimes the SDK cannot resolve DNS before the request, so a site could
rebind its own hostname to a private address; the reference wallet notes the same gap. Plain HTTP is used only
for an originator of `localhost`, for local development, as upstream does. We will adopt DNS and IP
checks in our toolbox fork if upstream lands them, and we track the fix.

Action for users: none.

### 23 September 2026 · Coordinated ts-stack trust-boundary advisory (GHSA-qp3j-h5xf-p2p7)

Source:
[ts-stack advisory, High. Patched: @bsv/sdk 2.8.0, wallet-toolbox and wallet-toolbox-client 2.13.2, @bsv/message-box-client
2.5.2, @bsv/templates 1.10.2 and others. Patched

A broad set of findings across the stack: storage-supplied output scripts not verified against the requested
outputs in createAction, action references not bound to the originator that was authorised, abort
refusals reported as success, negative signature verdicts treated as success, originator spoofing over the
wallet wire transport, and tenant isolation gaps in remote storage.

bWallet's position. bWallet ships @bsv/sdk 2.8.11, wallet-toolbox-client 2.14.5 and
@bsv/message-box-client 2.5.4, all past the patched versions. Separately from the stack fixes, the wallet
checks every message's originator against the browser-reported sender origin before any wallet call, verifies
the OpNS covenant locally before broadcast, and refuses to abort an action the network may already have.

Action for users: be on bWalletX 5.2.38 or later. The Chrome Web Store build is older (5.2.18) and does not have this fix yet; until it is updated, install the extension from bwalletx.com/download](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/security/advisories/GHSA-qp3j-h5xf-p2p7).

###
6 July 2026 · createAction output redirection with remote storage (GHSA-36f9-7rg5-cpf8 / CVE-2026-56744)

Source:
[ts-stack advisory, High. Affected wallet-toolbox, -client and -mobile; fixed in 2.13.2. Patched

A malicious or compromised remote storage server could return output scripts different from the ones the
caller asked for, redirecting a payment. bWallet ships wallet-toolbox-client 2.14.5, which verifies returned
outputs against the authorised request. The remote storage provider is a setting you can change in Settings ›
Wallet Backup.

## Credits

No reports yet. Yours could be the first name here.

## Changes to this policy

-
26 October 2026: version 4. Rewards of 1 BSV or more need identity verified with Veriff in bWallet and are
paid only to an address of the verified wallet; a typed name and country is no longer enough. This applies to
every unpaid reward of 1 BSV or more, including earlier reports. Rewards are paid when the programme's funding
arrives; the quarterly pool and order rules are unchanged.

-
25 October 2026: version 3. Check bwalletx.com/bugs](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/security/advisories/GHSA-36f9-7rg5-cpf8) before reporting (listed issues earn
credit, not money). Rewards are paid within 30 days of the fix being live on every channel or 60 days after we
confirm the report, in one monthly batch; earlier reports keep the version 2 timing.

-
24 October 2026: we briefly published lower rates and withdrew them the same day. The rates above stand;
anyone who reported on 24 October is paid at them.

-
20 October 2026: version 1. Policy, reward table, 20 BSV quarterly pool, safe harbour, first three advisory
responses.

The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd. Questions about the policy itself:
[support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com).

Made an app?

## Put it in the wallet.

If you've built something on BSV, add it to the Apps screen of bWallet and bWalletX. It's free, and a person reviews every app.

- One tap away. Your icon sits in Apps beside the other BSV apps.

- Sign-in built in. Apps open in the wallet's browser, connected over BRC-100. The user's identity key is the login.

- Paid in BSV. Ask for a payment and the user approves it on one sheet.

- What happens next. We review it, add it with your site's own name and icon, ship it in the next wallet release and email you.

[Add your app](https://bwalletx.com/apps/add)[Developer docs](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

# Your eBay store, on Bitcoin.

bMarketX.com gives your shop a second home. Store pages look the way your buyers already know, you move in in about a minute, and you sign in with bWalletX. If you like, you can mint the whole shop into your own wallet, so it belongs to you and not to us.

[Bring your shop](https://bmarketx.com/sell?from=bwalletx-b-market)[Visit bMarketX.com](https://bmarketx.com?from=bwalletx-b-market)

[Watch: b is for shopkeepersMabel moves 682 teapots before the kettle boils. 45 seconds, play it loud.](https://bwalletx.com/b-is-for-shopkeepers)

## A store page you already know

Every shop gets a page at `bmarketx.com/str/your-shop`, laid out the way eBay buyers and sellers are used to: your banner, your feedback, your listings in a grid, prices in US dollars. Nobody has to learn a new shop.

## Move from eBay in about a minute

Two ways in. Pick whichever is easier.

### Upload your listings file

In eBay Seller Hub, download the “All active listings” CSV and upload it on [bmarketx.com/sell](https://bmarketx.com/sell). Your listings come across in one go.

### Or paste your store link

Paste your eBay store link, then put the short code we give you into your eBay store description. That proves the store is yours, and it brings over your feedback score, items sold and followers too.

## Your wallet is your account

Sign in with [bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get). There is no password to choose, forget or leak. bMarketX uses the open BRC-100 wallet standard.

## Mint your whole shop, if you like

- Each listing becomes a BSV-21 token in your own bWalletX.

- Its photo is inscribed on chain as the token’s icon.

- The supply is your stock: ten teapots, ten tokens.

### About a tenth of a cent a listing

Minting costs about $0.001 per listing in network fees, so a 682-item store is around 75 cents. The wallet shows the exact price before you confirm. The tokens are yours, held in your wallet, not by bMarketX.

## Dollars on the tag, Bitcoin at the till

Prices show in US dollars. Buyers pay in BSV from bWalletX with Buy It Now. The payment goes straight to the seller’s wallet, and bMarketX takes no fee.

### What isn’t live yet

Bids and best offers come later. Promoting a listing with bAds is switched off for now.

## What’s finished

bmarketx.com, 28 Oct 2026.

- 26 Oct: store, item and search pages laid out like eBay; upload your eBay listings file; Mint my store (each listing a BSV-21 token, supply = stock).

- 27 Oct: Sign in with eBay to prove a store (read-only); import your listings from eBay; My bMarketX for your store; contact a seller by bMail; Buy It Now pays the seller’s wallet directly, with no fee; share cards.

- 27–28 Oct: cookie-free analytics, a privacy page and a public [stats page](https://bmarketx.com/stats).

- Next bWalletX release: link your eBay account from the wallet.

## Questions

### Do I have to leave eBay?

No. Bringing your shop over copies it; your eBay store keeps running as it is.

### Is bMarketX.com part of eBay?

No. bMarketX is not affiliated with or endorsed by eBay. We name eBay because that’s where most sellers are coming from.

### Who owns my minted listings?

You do. They sit in your own wallet, and your keys stay on your device. We can’t move them.

### Do I need to mint?

No. Minting is optional. Your store page works either way.

[Bring your shop](https://bmarketx.com/sell?from=bwalletx-b-market)

# b is on Twetch

b, the assistant inside bWalletX, now has its own Twetch account, [@bWalletX](https://twetch.com/u/220501). It posts bWalletX updates there and answers people who ask it questions.

## What b does on Twetch

### Posts bWalletX updates

New features and blog posts, each with a link to the page that explains it. Recent posts covered bAds, bTrust, rooms, NFT sending and the web home for bChatX rooms.

### Answers questions in replies

When someone mentions @bWalletX or replies to one of its posts, b writes a short, plain answer in the thread. It doesn't join other conversations.

### A person checks each reply

For now, someone on the bWalletX team reads every reply before it goes out.

“We want people to get a straight answer where they already are. On Twetch, that means asking b.”

The bWalletX team

## How to talk to b

- On Twetch: mention or reply to [@bWalletX](https://twetch.com/u/220501).

- In the wallet: open [Ask b](https://bwalletx.com/ask-b) in bWalletX.

## About bWalletX

bWalletX is a self-custody wallet for Bitcoin SV: your keys stay with you. It holds BSV, tokens and NFTs, and includes rooms, apps and b, its built-in assistant. bWalletX is made by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales (company number 16735102).

THE BITCOIN ACCELERATIONIST MOVEMENT

bAcc

# Make Bitcoin faster

bAcc is the Bitcoin accelerationist movement. We want Bitcoin to be fast enough and cheap enough to pay for anything, anywhere, all day. Our goal is 1 billion transactions per second (1b TPS). That is a goal, not what the network does today. The long-run version has a name: hyperbitcoinization, Bitcoin becoming the money people use every day.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Play the bAcc race](https://race.bwalletx.com/race?theme=bacc)

## BTC is slow. BSV is built to be fast.

Both are called Bitcoin. They run the same idea differently, and speed is where they differ most.

BTCBSV

Speed on the main chainAbout 3 to 7 transactions a secondNo fixed limit in the protocol; capacity grows with the hardware

Block sizeCapped by rule at a few megabytesBlocks can be as large as miners and nodes can handle

Fee for a small paymentRises when the network is busy, often too high for small paymentsA fraction of a penny

How it growsMoves small payments to other layersKeeps payments on the main chain and scales it up

Figures are approximate and change over time. Check a current source before you rely on them.

THE GOAL
### 1b TPS: one billion transactions per second

That is the target bAcc is working toward: a network that never makes anyone wait or pay much to send a payment. Today’s real-world volume is far lower, and we will not pretend otherwise. The speed has to be built, tested and shown.

## What bAcc means

### More payments

Every payment you send adds to Bitcoin’s volume. Tip, pay, split a bill, buy a track: the movement counts transactions, not speeches.

### Smaller payments

Here, Bitcoin payments cost a fraction of a penny, so a one-cent payment makes sense. Small and frequent is how volume grows.

### More people

A wallet that is easy to open and quick to use brings in people who have never held Bitcoin. That is why bWalletX exists.

## How to take part

### 1. Get a wallet

[bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) runs on your phone, in Chrome and on the web. You hold your own keys.

### 2. Pay in small amounts, often

Send a payment to a friend, tip someone whose work you like, pay for something in Bitcoin. Each one is a transaction.

### 3. Bring someone with you

The fastest way to raise volume is more people sending. Show one person how to open a wallet.

## The game

IN PROGRESS

### VexVoid Race

The bAcc game: jet-bike racing in black and yellow, free to play while it is in preview. Game engine by VexVoid. It is still being built: the bikes are being remodelled and the phone layout is not tested yet. Play what is there today.

[race.bwalletx.com →](https://race.bwalletx.com/race?theme=bacc)

## The Gas Run

The bAcc game mode we are building. Your bike runs on real Bitcoin transactions, and the aim is to keep them flowing without a break.

COMING
### 1. Fill the tank

Put a small amount of Bitcoin in the gas tank from your wallet, about one US dollar at most per run. What you do not use comes back to your wallet at the end.

COMING
### 2. Ride

Your bike burns gas by sending real, paid transactions: faster on boost, none when you stop. A crash, or an empty tank, ends the run.

COMING
### 3. Your score

The longest unbroken chain of your transactions that all get confirmed in a round. It is counted from the blockchain itself, so it cannot be faked.

COMING
### 4. Rounds

A round follows the blocks, about ten minutes. You see a live count as you ride, marked pending, and the final score when the round closes. Beat the last round’s best.

This mode is not built yet. There are no prizes: the first version is records and bragging rights. You pay normal network fees, nothing more, and every run is capped.

See the [bAcc theme](https://bwalletx.com/b/acc/store). Tell us what you want at [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com).

## What’s a bAd?

Our ads aren’t ads. They’re bAds. A bAd is made by b, the agent that lives in your bWalletX. You tell b about your business in a sentence. b makes the film, the logo or the whole brand, in your colours, not ours.

## Order a bAd

For a quick ad, b makes it on the spot with Grok Imagine. Square post, story or banner.

### 1. Describe your business

Your name, what you’re selling and, if you like, who it’s for and your colours.

### 2. b makes the ad

A clean layout, a short headline spelled right, your name on it. About a minute.

### 3. Pay in BSV

You see the price first. One pay sheet in your wallet, nothing else.

### 4. It’s yours, minted

Mint it in your name as a 1-sat NFT, or download it and post it anywhere.

[Order a bAd](https://web.bwalletx.com/m/bmint/mint/ad)
Live

### bAd film

A short animated film, about 45 seconds, with licensed music, a clear call to action, its own page and share image.

### Brand kit

Logo, colours, type, voice and rules, with a public brand page and a download pack.

### Logo

A mark and wordmark in SVG and PNG, with app-icon sizes.

### Share images

Cards that look right on X, iMessage and WhatsApp.

Our first client was us: [b is for business](https://bwalletx.com/b-is-for-business), [the bWalletX brand](https://bwalletx.com/brand) and [the b family](https://bwalletx.com/b-family) were all made this way.

No forms, no agency. Open b in your wallet and say what you need, or sign in at bAdvertisingX with bWalletX and send b a brief. b asks a question or two and gives you one fixed price in Bitcoin. Nothing is charged until the work has passed our quality check, and no money moves without your OK on the wallet’s pay sheet.

# bApps: apps that run inside bWalletX

bApps are Bitcoin apps from The Bitcoin Corporation. Open them from the Apps tab in bWalletX, or in any browser. You sign in with your wallet, not a password, and anything you pay comes from your wallet, after you approve it.

## How bApps work

### Sign in with your wallet Live

One tap on "Sign in with bWalletX". No account, no password, no email.

### Pay from your wallet Live

When an app asks for money, bWalletX shows you what it wants. Nothing leaves without your approval.

### One bar in every app Coming

Every bApp gets the same five buttons in the same place, each one about the app you have open:

WalletExchangebFeedChat

An app that doesn't use a button shows it greyed out, so the bar always looks the same. ☰ (your wallet menu) stays top left, with the app's icon next to it.

### Like = 1¢ to join the room Coming

Each app's Feed shows what's trending. A Like is a small buy, 1¢ by default (or one [PNEE](https://bwalletx.com/pnees)), of that thing's token. It funds the thing you liked, and the token is your key to its chat room. Daily cap of $1 by default; you can change both.

# bMovies, inside bWalletX

bMovies is a film feed on Bitcoin SV. Scroll it like Instagram, watch thousands of films, and back the ones you want more of. Sign in with bWalletX and it works like part of your wallet.

[Open bMovies](https://bmovies.app)[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## Live today Live

- A film feed syndicated from creators on X, with around 2,300 films you can play.

- BSV only: every payment is in Bitcoin SV, from your own wallet.

- Film tokens: each film can have its own token. Holding it shows you backed the film.

The bMovies sign-in screen on a phone.

# Bounties

The [b-Aware](https://bwalletx.com/b-aware) reward pool and every payout from it, in public.

### Pool

Loading…

Pool address: published soon

0BSV paid this quarter

0BSV paid all-time

0reports rewarded

0credit only

## Payouts

DateCreditSeverityBSVRecipientVerify

Loading…

Recipients are shown as a short fingerprint. The full address is visible in the transaction for anyone who checks it.

Report details stay private until the fix has shipped and the reward is paid.

## How the pool works

- There is a fixed pool each calendar quarter. The bar shows what is left, read live from the pool address on chain.

- The first valid report of an issue earns the reward. Duplicates earn credit.

- Rewards are paid after the fix ships.

- When a quarter's pool is spent, valid reports are paid from the next quarter's pool, in the order they were triaged.

The full policy, the reward table and the safe harbour are on [b-Aware](https://bwalletx.com/b-aware).

# bPhone. Get paid to take the call.

Calls in bWalletX are free. bPhone lets you charge for yours: a price per second, minute or hour, or a one-off price per call, in BSV, MNEE or a token. The caller sees the price before your phone rings, agrees a maximum, and their wallet pays yours every few seconds while you talk. For therapists, solicitors, accountants, tutors, coaches, developers: anyone whose time is the product.

Live since 5.1.87 bPhone is in bWalletX (not the store edition). It is new: start with small prices while we test it with real payments.

## What the caller sees

alice@bwalletx.com charges to receive calls

$2.00 / min, paid in BSV

Paid every 10 seconds from your wallet while you talk. You can hang up any time.

Max spend on this call

$30 ≈ 15 min$60 ≈ 30 min$120 ≈ 60 min

Nothing rings until the caller accepts. During the call both phones show the money: the caller sees what has gone out and a warning 30 seconds before their maximum, you see what has arrived and that the caller is paid up. When the call ends, both see the total.

## How it works

- Live since 5.1.87Your price. Chat › Calls › bPhone. Turn on “Charge to receive calls”, pick dollars paid in BSV, MNEE, or any BSV-21 token you hold (your own $NAME token included), and a price per second, minute, hour or call. Off by default: your calls stay free until you set a price.

- Live since 5.1.87Pay as you talk. The caller’s wallet pays yours one interval ahead: every 10 seconds in BSV, every 60 seconds in MNEE or a token. Each payment is an ordinary wallet-to-wallet transaction straight to your paymail or token address. There is no middleman, no platform balance and no refunds. A one-off price is paid once, when you answer.

- Live since 5.1.87Your phone enforces it. If the caller’s payments stop, your phone ends the call after a short grace period. If their maximum runs out, the call ends when the paid time does. A caller on an app without bPhone gets about 20 seconds and is cut off.

- Live since 5.1.87List yourself. A title, what you offer, a category, and your opening hours in your own time zone. People looking for a professional find you under Chat › Calls › Experts, see your rate and whether you are open now, and call or book. Listing is separate from charging: you can charge without being listed, or list a free consultation.

- Live since 5.1.87Bookings. Callers pick a 15, 30, 45 or 60 minute slot inside your hours; you confirm or decline. Both sides see the booking under bPhone, and from five minutes before the start a Call now button appears. The booked call is a normal bPhone call, quoted and paid the same way.

- Live since 5.1.87Dollars in, sats out. A BSV price is set in US dollars and paid in satoshis at the live rate at each payment, so you quote “$2 a minute” and the caller’s wallet does the conversion. MNEE and token prices are in those units.

## What a call costs

You chargePaid inPayment everyA 30-minute call

$2.00 / minBSV, at the live rate10 s ($0.34, then $0.33…)$60.00 in sats, over 180 payments

90 MNEE / hourMNEE60 s (1.50 MNEE)45 MNEE

1 BOB / secondyour BOB token60 s (60 BOB)1,800 BOB

$50 per callBSVonce, when you answer$50.00

Each BSV payment carries the normal network fee (about 25 sats) and is never smaller than 546 sats, so very low rates are better charged in MNEE or a token. Rounding is exact over the whole call: the caller pays what the rate says, never a cent more.

## Why in the wallet

Paid consultations usually mean a platform in the middle: it takes a cut, holds the money, decides who gets paid and when, and keeps the client list. bPhone has no middle. The price is published under your own identity key, the call runs over bWalletX’s own video server, and every payment goes from the caller’s wallet to yours while you are still talking. bWalletX takes 0%.

Your existing names work: callers reach you at your [$handle or paymail](https://bwalletx.com/handles), and your listing is tied to the same identity your [signature](https://bwalletx.com/identity) uses. If you have a [personal token](https://bwalletx.com/friends), you can charge in it, which gives your holders something to spend it on.

## Not in the store edition

bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition, keeps free voice and video calls and never shows a price. Charging for calls and the directory are bWalletX only, pending the store rules on person-to-person services.

## Your responsibilities

You are selling your time to people you may not know. Any licence, insurance, confidentiality or tax rule that applies to your profession applies here too; bPhone does not check qualifications, and the directory shows your own words next to your paymail. Calls are not recorded by bWalletX. Report and block work inside the call, as on every call.

More on the thinking in [blog post 030](https://bwalletx.com/blog/030-bphone). Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts.

Source: https://bwalletx.com/bpositive

# bPositive. Sponsor someone’s journey.

Back a person who is working towards something: a student, an athlete, someone getting sober, a developer learning a new stack, an artist finishing an album. You support them monthly, or pledge money to a milestone that witnesses confirm. It is built inside bWalletX, where the money, the proof and the people already are.

Live bPositive is in bWalletX 5.2.26: journeys, monthly support, milestone pledges, witnesses and thank-you NFTs.

## A gift, not an investment

Sponsoring is a gift. Sponsors get nothing back: no share of future earnings, no equity, no repayment and no token. Every screen, receipt and thank-you NFT says so. The only money a sponsor can ever get back is their own milestone pledge that was never released, after the deadline passes.

There is no bPositive token, and bPositive will never be combined with a launchpad coin on the same journey.

## How it works

- LiveJourney pages. The person starts a journey in bWalletX: a title, a short story, a category and, if they want, milestones such as “Pass the AWS Associate exam” or “90 days sober”. The journey is a signed record, so a milestone can’t be quietly changed after people pledge. Updates notify sponsors.

- LiveMonthly support from pots. “Support monthly” is a standing order from one of your [pots](https://bwalletx.com/pots) to the person’s paymail. Pause or cancel it any time with one tap. A gift is final, so payments already made aren’t refunded.

- LiveMilestone pledges. You pledge an amount to a milestone. It is paid when witnesses confirm the milestone: 2 of 3 by default, each with a verified identity. At first a pledge stays in a pot in your own wallet and is sent when the confirmations arrive, so it is labelled “Pledged”, not “Locked”.

- ComingRefund after the deadline. A later version locks the pledge on chain, so it can only go to the person once witnesses confirm, or back to you after the deadline. Until then, an unconfirmed pledge simply stays with you.

- LiveThank-you NFTs. Sponsors get a thank-you receipt NFT. It is a record, not a reward: it unlocks nothing in the app and has no promised value.

- LiveSponsors’ room. If the person turns it on, sponsors who hold a thank-you NFT can enter a room for the journey, in bWalletX.

## Witnesses

The person names witnesses for each milestone, and each witness has to accept. When the person says “I’ve done it” and attaches evidence, witnesses confirm or decline with a signed, on-chain seal. Witnesses are shown on the journey page with their identity strength, need a verified identity, can’t be the person’s other accounts or a sponsor of the same milestone, and are not paid for witnessing.

## The rules

- Live18+ only. Recipients, witnesses and milestone sponsors must be adults at launch.

- LiveGifts only. No perks for money beyond thank-you NFTs and updates. Offering services or content for money is selling, not bPositive.

- Live0% fee. The Bitcoin Corporation takes nothing from gifts. You pay the normal network fee.

- LiveSponsor count, not totals. Journey pages show how many people sponsor. Showing amounts is the person’s choice. No countdown timers and no leaderboards of totals.

- LiveReport and block. Journeys can be reported. Sponsors get no contact rights by sponsoring, and recipients can block a sponsor and return a gift.

Only give what you would give a friend. Gifts may have tax consequences where you live; bWalletX gives no tax advice.

## Not in the store edition

bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition, won’t have bPositive at first. Person-to-person payments and standing orders still work there. bPositive lives in bWalletX: web, extension, Android direct download and iPhone.

Why we built it this way: [029 bPositive: gifts, not investments](https://bwalletx.com/blog/029-bpositive).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Nothing here is investment, legal or tax advice. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# TheWalletXbrand

A gold b on black, a calm voice and a handful of rules that keep everything we make looking and sounding like us. Use our logo freely to point people to bWalletX. Please keep it as it is.

[Download the brand kit](https://bwalletx.com/brand/bwalletx-brand-kit.zip)[Read the full brand guide](https://docs.bwalletx.com/brand/)

[The idea](#idea)[Logo](#logo)[Versions](#versions)[Name](#name)[Misuse](#misuse)[Colour](#colour)[Type](#type)[Voice](#voice)[Imagery](#imagery)[Motion and sound](#motion)[Buttons](#buttons)[Family](#family)[Your brand](#services)[Press](#press)

## 01 · THE IDEAb is for Bitcoin.

The b is Bitcoin, made personal: your money, your keys, your name. Everything we make should feel calm and in control, never noisy or speculative.

Less noise.No hype, no charts shouting at you, no jargon. We say what something does, in everyday words.

More life.Money that gets out of the way, so people can get on with music, friends, work and the things they love.

Just b.Simple and confident. One gold letter is enough; we don’t need to explain ourselves twice.

## 02 · LOGOThe gold b.

Our logo is the letter b alone, drawn from two simple shapes: a stem with a 45° flag cut across the top, and a round bowl. There is no X in the mark; the X lives in the name.

- The stem is 18 units wide, cut at 45° across the top: the bCorp flag.

- The bowl is a circle (radius 33) with a round counter (radius 15).

- They meet cleanly. The stem ends exactly where the bowl’s edge is upright, so the left side runs in one unbroken line.

- The gold runs top to bottom across the whole letter: #FFE58A, #FFD24D, #C98F00.

xx

16 px min24 px34 px header80 px

Clear space: keep at least x clear all round, where x is the width of the counter (the hole). Minimum size: 16 px tall on screen, 6 mm in print.

# bShares.
Any company’s register, on chain.

A register of members, kept by the company. Shares issued as tokens, approved by your directors, and locked in each holder’s wallet so the company and the holder both have a say.

In testing bShares is a record-keeping tool for any company. It’s in testing; the first register is our own company, The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd. It isn’t open to other companies yet. Nothing on this page is an offer of shares, and no shares are sold here or to the public.

[Ask about bShares](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=bShares%20for%20my%20company)

Before a company: [Partnership shares](https://bwalletx.com/partnership-shares), for friends starting something together.

## For any company

bShares is a bApp in bWalletX for companies of any size. The same tools are being shaped so any company can keep its register, its directors and its members’ holdings here.

## The register is the record

The register of members is the legal title. bShares reads holdings from it, never from a list in the app. Certificate numbers are never reused.

## Directors approve every allotment

A board minute is drafted in the company’s own format, and a director approves it before any share is issued. An allotment that would go over the company’s authorised shares is refused.

## A share with two keys

Each holding is a token in the holder’s wallet, locked 2-of-2: one key for the director, one for the holder. Nobody can move it alone.

And holders never depend on us. After a set block height, the holder can move their token alone, from their own seed. No server, no director needed.

## Private placements

A company can invite people it already knows to buy shares privately, under its own rules and the law where it is registered; bShares only keeps the record. A member pays in BSV to a 2-of-3 company treasury, with director keys on separate devices. Pay too much and you choose: a refund within 14 days, or treat it as share premium.

## From a token to a company

Most things start small. bShares is one step on a longer path:

- Token
- Rooms
- [Partnership shares](https://bwalletx.com/partnership-shares)
- Company
- Private placements
- IPO

## What works today

- BuiltRegister of members, phase 1. A company’s register and its directors’ approvals, in private testing.

- BuiltTwo kinds of lock. The company’s money sits in a 2-of-3 treasury on its directors’ keys (for one director: phone, desktop and an offline backup). Each member’s shares are locked 2-of-2 to the company and the member, with a timed way out the member can use alone.

- BuiltIn the Vault. Holdings show in the Lock vault as Restricted, not for sale.

- BuiltExchange “Shares” filter. Holdings appear marked Restricted. There are no buy or sell buttons.

- ComingSet-up for any company. Your own name and ticker, import your register, add director keys, use your minute template.

- ComingPartnership shares stage. Friends start something together before there’s a company. See [Partnership shares](https://bwalletx.com/partnership-shares).

- Liveb drafts in partner chats. Ask b in the partners’ chat to draft an agreement or summarise the terms; every partner accepts before it counts.

- ComingIncorporate 1:1. Turn partnership shares into company shares, one for one.

## What bShares is not

It isn’t a place to buy shares. No shares are offered or sold on this site or in bWalletX, and bShares is left out of bWallet, the App Store and Google Play builds. It’s a tool for a company to keep its own records and lock its members’ holdings.

## Run a company?

If you’d like to keep your register this way once it opens, write to us.

[Ask about bShares](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=bShares%20for%20my%20company)

bShares is a record-keeping tool, not an offer of shares or investment advice. bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/bspaces

# bSpaces. Live Spaces for your token holders.

A bSpace is a live audio or video room inside a token room in bWalletX. The host is on stage, holders listen and watch, and anyone can raise a hand to be brought up. Hold the token and you’re in.

## What a Space is

- Live in bChatStage and audience. A host, speakers on stage and listeners. Camera is opt-in for people on stage. Runs on our own video server.

- Live in bChatRaise hand. Listeners raise a hand, the host sees the queue and brings people up to speak.

- Live in bChatToken-gated. A Space lives in a token room, so only holders get in. The server checks the holding, and the video server only lets in members who have joined.

- Live since 5.1.85Spaces in bWalletX. A “Live now” banner with Join in the room, “Start a bSpace” for the issuer or a room admin, and a full-screen Space view: the stage on top, the hand queue for the host, controls at the bottom, and the room chat sliding up from below.

## Paid Spaces

- Live since 5.1.91Paid tickets. Pay at the door: you pay the host and the host’s wallet sends you the ticket. Not in the store edition.

- ComingPaid speakers. Pay to come up on stage.

- Live since 5.1.95Per-minute charges. Paid listening: the host sets a price, you approve a spending cap, and your wallet pays the people on stage a minute at a time. Not in the store edition.

Any fee on a paid Space will be shown before you pay. Paid Spaces will need identity and age checks before they open.

## Why in the wallet

The token is the ticket, and the token is in your wallet. Putting the Space in the same place means no separate platform account and no card: you hold the token, you open the room, you join. It is the same room you already chat in.

One-way livestreams to token holders are on [Live](https://bwalletx.com/live).

## Not in the store edition

bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition, has no token rooms, so it has no Spaces in them, and no paid tickets or paid listening.

Free Spaces stay: in bWallet you can listen, ask to speak, speak and chat in the Lounge and other open rooms.

Creators are responsible for what they say and show, and must follow the law and our terms. Rooms can be reported. bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/btrust

# bTrust.
Hand down what matters.

A Lock with more than one key. Set money and your important papers aside, and share the keys with the people you trust, so the people you love are looked after.

Live bTrust is in bWalletX (web, Chrome, Android download; not the App Store or Google Play edition): open bApps › bTrust. It’s new, so start with small amounts. [What works today](#works).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## A Lock with more than one key

A [Lock](https://bwalletx.com/lock) keeps money aside until a date, and only you hold the key. A bTrust shares the keys. You choose who holds one, say your solicitor and two family members, and how many it takes to open it: any two of three, for example.

Nobody can move it alone. Not one of them, and not even you.

## Looked after in life

Lose your phone, and two of your key holders can help you back in. No company to call, no forms, no waiting.

## Looked after later

Choose who receives what, and when: on a date, or if you haven’t checked in for a while. Leave each of them a letter in your own words. When the moment comes, your key holders open it together and carry out your wishes.

## Your important papers

Keep the things your family will need alongside it: deeds, insurance, the letter you’d want found, and the backup words for wallets you keep elsewhere. Everything is encrypted on your device, and only opens for the people you’ve chosen, when the time comes.

## What works today

- LiveLocks. Set money aside until a date you choose. See [Locks](https://bwalletx.com/lock).

- LivePots. Money set aside for a purpose. See [Pots](https://bwalletx.com/pots).

- LiveYour wallet backup. Back up your words and restore on any device. See [Restore](https://bwalletx.com/restore).

- LiveRecovery slices. Split your backup into slices, 2 of 3 or any number you choose, as QR and text cards. Restore from enough slices on this device.

- LivePassing on. Name three heirs and build a plan. Fund its lock from your wallet with one approval. The coins stay yours and you can move them any time.

- LiveCheck in. Check in to push the date back. If you don’t, any two heirs can claim together; six months later the lead heir can claim alone.

- LiveHeirs claim. Heirs claim from their own bWalletX. When two claim together, the second checks every output, fee and lock total before co-signing.

- LiveFind your locks. Your recovery phrase alone finds your bTrust locks. No plan file, no server.

- LiveImportant papers. Seal a will, deeds or instructions with your slices, and open them with your slices.

- ComingHeir keys from a paymail. For now, you paste each heir’s public key.

- ComingPaper fingerprints on chain.

- ComingSolicitors as extra key holders.

- ComingLetters to each person.

bTrust is a way to arrange what you hold in your wallet. It isn’t a legal trust or a will; for those, talk to a solicitor. bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Known issues.

What’s broken, what we’re fixing, and what we fixed. Spotted something? Tell us below.

## Before you report: check this page

Everything below is a known or fixed issue. Reporting something already listed here earns credit, not money.

Security issues that are still being fixed are not listed, for your safety. If you found something that looks serious and it is not here, report it privately to [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=b-Aware) with the subject b-Aware. See [b-Aware](https://bwalletx.com/b-Aware) for how we reward reports.

## Report a bug

What happened?
Device and app version (for example iPhone 15, 5.2.45)
Email (optional, if you’d like a reply)

Leave this empty

Send report

In the app? Tap Report to b on any error screen instead.

## Known issues

-

### The b button misbehaves when b disappears
Investigating

We are working out where and when it happens. If you see it, tell us what you tapped and on which device.

Reported 22 Oct 2026

-

### Show my 12 words asked for a password you never set
Fixed in 5.2.45

If you made your wallet with a passkey, Show my 12 words now has Use my passkey, so you can see your words without a password.

Fixed 23 Oct 2026

Fixed 22 Oct 2026

The wallet showed an error about “identityAddress” instead of opening. It now opens normally.

Fixed 22 Oct 2026

-

### Balance stuck on “Still syncing” after a backup at sign-up
Fixed in 5.2.45

Making a backup during sign-up no longer stalls your balance, and encrypted backups save every time.

Fixed 22 Oct 2026

-

### Restoring a wallet could hang on Restoring…
Fixed in 5.2.38

Restoring or importing a wallet now finishes instead of spinning for good.

Fixed 20 Oct 2026

-

### Sends failed after spending from another device
Fixed in 5.2.36

Coins already spent elsewhere could inflate your balance and make sends fail on iPhone. The wallet now clears them when you unlock, and if a send still hits one, it says “tap Send again”.

Fixed 19 Oct 2026

Fixed in 5.2.36

The Feed opens normally on Desktop.

Fixed 19 Oct 2026

## Security fixes

Found by researchers under [b-Aware](https://bwalletx.com/b-Aware) and reported privately. We describe a security fix here only once it is live everywhere you can get bWalletX, so more will appear as releases reach every store. Keep your wallet up to date.

-

### A stranger could knock a paired computer offline
Fixed

Someone who only knew a pairing’s channel could take over the phone’s side of the link and cut off your paired computer. No money could move. Our pairing server now refuses this. The fix is on our server, so every edition has it.

Fixed 24 Oct 2026 · Security fix, reported privately under b-Aware

bRand  Business agents

# Your shop’s agent, paid in sats, in chat.

Don’t be bland. Get bRanded.

Paste your website. b drafts an agent that knows your products, prices and FAQs. It answers customers and takes payment right in the chat, on Bitcoin, with a receipt anyone can check.

Chat agents that take money today mostly hand off to a card checkout. bRand doesn’t: the agent works from a capped account with a daily limit and a Stop button, and the payment settles on chain.

[How it works](#how)[What’s live](#status)

b
YourshopAgent · bRanded

Got the gold sticker pack?

Yes: gold sticker pack, 12,000 sats. Ships today. Want it?

Yes please.

Pay Yourshop
12,000 satsNetwork fee under 1p · from your walletAllow

Paid · receipt on chain ↗

01 / 05  How it works

## Paste a link. b drafts your shop. Take sats in chat.

Step 1

### Paste a link

Give b your website. It reads your products, prices and FAQs.

Step 2

### b drafts your shop

You check the agent, edit anything, then put it in your bChatX room or your branded bWallet.

Step 3

### Take sats in chat

Customers tap Allow on their own approval sheet. No cards, no forms.

02 / 05  Card rails vs bRand

## Same chat. Different money.

Card railsbRand

FeesA percentage of each sale, often plus a fixed chargeBitcoin network fee, usually well under 1p

SettlementTypically days to reach your bankOn chain in seconds, in your wallet

Who holds the moneyThe processor, until it pays outYou. Your keys, your wallet

ChargebacksCan be reversed weeks laterFinal once paid; refunds are yours to give

ReceiptA private record at the processorA public transaction anyone can check

Agent spendingUsually a card or API key with wide accessA capped account with a daily limit and Stop

Card fees vary by provider and country. Sat prices move with the BSV price; the sheet shows the amount before you allow it.

03 / 05  Kept on a short leash

## You stay in charge of the money.

- 01The agent has its own capped account with a daily limit you set. It never touches your main wallet.

- 02A Stop button pauses it at once.

- 03Every sale gets a receipt on chain, so you and your customer have the same record.

- 04Refunds come from your own wallet, by you.

- 05Customers approve every payment themselves. The agent can ask; it can’t take.

04 / 05  Price

## Included with Branded editions.

Business agents come with a [Branded edition](https://bwalletx.com/themes/custom) (from $999). The Theme edition is $99 a year. Ask us if you want to be one of the first businesses to try it.

[See editions](https://bwalletx.com/themes/custom)[Message us on bChatX](https://chat.bwalletx.com/u/bwalletx)

# Buy BSV in bWalletX

Open the wallet and the gold Buy BSV card is right at the top, with today’s price. Tap it to buy with a card or bank, or to receive BSV from an exchange or a friend.

Buy BSVLoading price…

BSV price from WhatsOnChain, the same source the wallet uses.

In the wallet, the card’s price updates every minute. You’ll also find the card under the BSV price chart, and a Get BSV button on your BSV row while it’s empty.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## How it works

### Tap Buy BSV

The gold card at the top of your wallet opens the Get BSV sheet.

### Pick how

Pay with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or bank. Or receive from an exchange, another wallet or a friend.

### It lands in your wallet

Your BSV shows up in your wallet, in dollars. Ready to send, mint or trade.

## Ways to get BSV

### From an exchange or another wallet

bWalletX shows your BSV address and QR code. Send from wherever your BSV is now.

### From a friend

Share your $name or paymail. They send to it and it arrives in seconds.

### With a card or bank

Pick a provider in the sheet. It opens in the wallet’s browser. Copy your address from Receive and paste it there.

The card providers in the sheet today:

- ChangeNOW · card, many currencies

- Alchemy Pay · card, Apple Pay, Google Pay

These open the provider’s own website. Whether you can buy depends on where you live: from the UK on 18 October 2026, Alchemy Pay said it isn’t available to UK users, and ChangeNOW’s page didn’t give a dollar price for BSV. Receiving BSV from an exchange or a friend works everywhere.

## Status

- ✓ Live · receive BSV from an exchange, another wallet or a friend

- ✓ Live · Buy BSV card with today’s price, opening the Get BSV sheet

- ◻ Coming · buy with card, Apple Pay or bank inside the app with Ramp, your address filled in. Waiting for Ramp to approve us

- ◻ Coming · card buying that works in every country we serve, including the UK

### Good to know

These providers are independent companies, not bWalletX. They check your ID and set their own fees and limits. bWalletX never holds your money: you pay the provider, and the BSV goes straight to your own wallet.

# bWeb: ask b to build your website Planned

You tell b what you need: a page for your band, a site for your café, a small shop. You get one fixed price in BSV and approve it once. An agent builds it and shows you previews in the chat. When you're happy, the site is published on bitcoin, and the code is yours. This isn't open yet. We're running one real paid pilot first, and this page says exactly what works today.

[Tell b you're interested](https://bwalletx.com/ask-b)[Be a pilot (email us)](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=bWeb%20pilot)

## How it will work

### 1. Ask b

Say what you want in bWalletX. b asks a few questions and writes a one-page brief for you to check.

### 2. One fixed price

A tier and a price in dollars, paid in BSV at the rate of the moment. One approval in your wallet. No meter running.

### 3. b builds it

An agent builds your site in a walled-off sandbox. You see progress and screenshots in your chat with b.

### 4. Preview and tweak

You get a private preview link. Small changes are included. Bigger ones get a new price before any work starts.

### 5. Launch on chain

The files are published on BSV. You get a permanent link, and the site sits in your own wallet, so only you can update it. A shop takes payments through your bWalletX Store.

### 6. Upkeep, if you want it

A small monthly plan for edits and re-publishing. Stop any time: the site stays up because it's on chain.

## What you could ask for

- “A one-page site for my band: photo, next gigs, a link to our music, and a way to tip us.”

- “Five pages for my café: menu, opening hours, a map link, and a contact button that messages my $name.”

- “A small shop for my prints, 20 products, paid in BSV to my Store.”

## Yours, on chain

Your site is written to bitcoin as a set of files, and served from there by gateways such as ORDFS. Nobody can take it down by closing an account, and you hold the piece that controls updates. Each update is a new version; old versions stay readable. You can point your own domain at it.

What that means in practice: sites are pages, styles, scripts and pictures, with no server behind them. Forms, sign-ins and payments go through bWalletX on the page. Anything published stays public for good, so we never put secrets or other people's personal details in a site.

## Planned prices

These are a draft and may change after the pilot. Paid in BSV at the rate when you get your quote.

TierPlanned priceIncludes

One page$49One page, your words and photos, a contact button, one round of small changes

Site$149Up to 5 pages, up to 25 photos, two rounds of small changes, help with your own domain

Site + shop$299The Site tier plus up to 30 products paid through your bWalletX Store

Upkeep$9 a monthUp to 3 small edits a month and re-publishing

Publishing on chain costs a few cents or less for most sites, shown before you approve. If we can't build what your brief says, you get your BSV back.

## Status

- Live b in chat inside bWalletX ([Ask b](https://bwalletx.com/ask-b))

- Live bWalletX [Store](https://bwalletx.com/store)

- Live On-chain web pages served by ORDFS (ordfs.network), which bWeb will use

- Live bWeb settings in bWalletX: choose your dock and Feed bApps, what b can see, Ask b add-ons

- Coming b writes your brief

- Coming Fixed quote in BSV with one approval

- Coming Agent builds your site, with progress in chat

- Coming Private preview link and small changes

- Coming Launch on chain, site held in your wallet

- Coming Your own domain pointing at your site

- Coming Shops paid through your bWalletX Store

- Coming Upkeep plan

- Coming First paid pilot

## Safety

- We never ask for passwords or keys. The building agent can't reach your wallet.

- You pay only through your wallet, once, after you've seen the price.

- No fakes. We don't build sites that pretend to be other people or brands, or that trick people.

# Contracts in chat

Agree terms where you already talk. b drafts the agreement in your chat. You sign it with your hand and your wallet key. A fingerprint goes on Bitcoin, and each of you keeps a copy.

## How it works

-
1 · Draft

### Ask b to draft Live

In a partnership room, tap Ask b. b writes a full agreement, or sums up the terms so far, from what the room has said. Anything still open shows as [TO BE AGREED], highlighted so nobody misses it.

-
2 · Agree

### Everyone accepts Live

b's draft is only a proposal. Every member accepts it with their own wallet before it counts. Nothing is accepted for you.

-
3 · Document

### A `.nds.html` contract Live

On bChatX, contracts are `.nds.html` files: one web page with a box for each person who signs.

-
4 · Sign

### Your hand and your key Live

Draw your signature into your box. bWalletX then signs a record of what you signed with your wallet's identity key.

-
5 · Seal

### A fingerprint on Bitcoin Live

You approve a seal from your wallet. Only hashes go on chain, never the contract or your signature. You pay the network fee.

-
6 · Keep

### Each party holds a copy Live

A sealed contract on bChatX is encrypted to the people who signed it. Agreements sent by bMail are encrypted to each party and land in their own Agreements box.

-
7 · Resolve

### b helps with disputes Coming

Not built yet. Today b drafts and sums up terms. It doesn't mediate disagreements after signing.

b's drafts are labelled “Draft by b, not legal advice; review before signing”. b drafts in partnership rooms only, not in token rooms or one-to-one chats.

## What a `.nds.html` file is

It's a normal HTML page. Anyone can open it in a browser and read it. Inside sits a small, hidden manifest that lists the signature boxes: who signs, in what role, for which party, and where on the page the box goes.

<script type="application/npg-sig-manifest+json">
{ "signatureFields": [
{ "id": "a", "party": "founder", "role": "Partner", "signerHandle": "alice" },
{ "id": "b", "party": "founder", "role": "Partner", "signerHandle": "bob" } ],
"token": { "symbol": "ACME", "supply": 1000000000,
"distribution": [ { "to": "a", "pct": 60 }, { "to": "b", "pct": 40 } ] } }
</script>

A simplified example, not a real contract.

### Token allocations

A contract can carry token terms: the token's name and supply, and how the supply splits between the people who sign. bChatX checks the split before it builds the contract. bWalletX doesn't show token terms itself yet.

### Signed in place

Each drawn signature lands exactly on its own box, so the signed file looks like the paper version would.

### What goes on chain

Hashes only: a fingerprint of the contract and of the signatures. The text and your drawing never go on chain.

## Two places to sign

### On bChatX

Open the contract on bChatX and choose Sign and seal with bWalletX. Approve in the Chrome extension, or pair your phone with a QR code. Today that's two approvals: one to sign, one to pay the fee. [More on Sign and seal](https://bwalletx.com/sign).

### In bMail, inside bWalletX

bMail › Agreements sends a document (text, HTML or a small PDF) to the other party. Each of you signs with your card signature and identity key, then anyone who signed can seal it. Folders show what needs you, what's waiting, and what's sealed. bWalletX only.

## Privacy

### Your drawn signature

It's stored on your device only. It goes into a contract only when you sign one. [How it's kept](https://bwalletx.com/sign).

### A sealed contract on bChatX

Once everyone has signed, the finished contract is encrypted to the signers' keys. By default it's also wrapped to an offline recovery key, so it can be recovered. An author can choose a private contract with no recovery copy. While a contract is still being signed, it stays readable so the next person can sign it.

### When it isn't encrypted

If someone signs by an email link, they have no key to encrypt to, so the contract is stored readable. Share certificates are stored readable on purpose, because they exist to be shown.

### Agreements by bMail

The document travels inside a bMail letter, encrypted to each party. Only the parties can open it.

### On chain

Nothing readable. The chain holds fingerprints, so anyone with a copy can check it hasn't changed. Without a copy, the fingerprint tells nobody anything.

## Status

- Live
b drafts in partnership rooms. A full agreement or a terms summary, with open points marked [TO BE AGREED].

- Live
Every member accepts b's draft with their own wallet.

- Live
`.nds.html` contracts on bChatX, with signature boxes and optional token terms.

- Live
Card signature. Sign the back of your wallet card with your finger. In bWalletX and bWallet.

- Live
Sign and seal with bWalletX on bChatX. Hashes only on chain; you pay the network fee.

- Live
Sealed contracts encrypted to the signers on bChatX, when every signer has a bChatX account.

- Live
bMail › Agreements. Send, sign, seal and keep agreements in your wallet. bWalletX only.

- Coming
One-tap sign and seal. bWalletX shows one screen with the document, your box, your signature and the cost, then signs and pays together.

- Coming
Token terms shown in bWalletX. See a contract's token split in the wallet before you sign.

- Coming
b helps resolve disputes. b as a mediator between the parties after signing.

The contract text is never put on chain, encrypted or not. Encryption protects the stored copies.

## Store edition

bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition, has the card signature. bMail Agreements and partnership shares are in bWalletX only. Get bWalletX for the full set.

# Credits. Prepaid, per service.

Credits are prepaid credit that a service issues for its own service. Any service can issue its own credits and choose what it accepts: BSV, MNEE or PNEEs. bWalletX holds them and spends them for you.

Credits are in testing. bCredits for b come first. Nobody can buy or spend credits yet.

## bCredits, for b

The first issuer is The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd. Its credits, bCredits, pay for b, the agent in bWalletX. These terms are decided:

- You buy bCredits with BSV. 1 bCredit = 1p.

- b charges its running cost × 1.35 for each reply.

- Top up as little as you like, up to £20 at a time.

- bCredits don’t expire.

- They’re non-refundable, except where the law says otherwise.

- They can’t be transferred or cashed out. They’re only for b.

- Your unspent BSV stays in your own wallet. Only what you top up sits with the issuer.

## For services

Any service can issue its own credits. For example, a compute service like [Mandala](https://mandala.computer) could issue credits for its compute.

### Issue credits

Credits for your service, under your name and your terms.

### Set your price

Choose the rate, and what you accept: BSV, MNEE or PNEEs.

### Users top up

From bWalletX, in a tap.

### Charge per use

Debit per request, per minute or per job. No card processor. No monthly billing.

Want to issue credits for your service? Email [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=Issuing%20credits).

## In the wallet

- Each balance has its own card.

- The card being spent comes to the front and ticks down as you use it, with a chip like b · 2 bCredits/reply.

- Tap a card to flip it. The back shows the contract: who issued it, what it’s for, the rate and what you’ve spent so far.

- Stop ends payment and ends the service.

- Contact the issuer is on the back of every card.

## Built and coming

### Built IN TESTING

- The wallet’s credits row, history and top-up screens.

- The ledger server, with debits that can’t be charged twice.

- The balance cards: swipe is in the release app since 5.2.23; flip to the contract is still a prototype.

Top-ups are not open to users yet: they switch on when the treasury address is set on the server. Until then the wallet shows bCredits as coming.

### Coming NOT LIVE

- bCredits for b, going live.

- Credits from other issuers.

Related: [Streaming payments](https://bwalletx.com/streaming-payments), [Ask b](https://bwalletx.com/ask-b).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Culture, made on BSV.

A token isn’t just a ticker. Anything people make can gather around it: a game, pictures, films, songs, a room to talk in and a stage to go live on. In bWalletX all of that sits in one wallet, on a chain that keeps the fees tiny and the content itself on chain.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Launch your own coin](https://bwalletx.com/launchpad)

## One token, many kinds of media

Take $FROGGER Example. It’s a made-up coin for this page, not a real token. Here’s what its people could do with it today:

- A gameGames run inside bWalletX as bApps, so a Frogger game can sit right next to its token. [bApps](https://bwalletx.com/bapps)

- PicturesMint frog art from your phone with bPics, so it’s yours on chain, and share it or keep it. [Mint](https://bwalletx.com/mint)

- FilmsPost a Frogger film to the bMovies feed; each film can have its own token that backers hold. [bMovies](https://bwalletx.com/bapps/bmovies)

- MusicAn album on bMusic, where listeners pay the artist directly, a sat a second. [Artists](https://bwalletx.com/artists)

- A roomHold $FROGGER and its chat room appears in your list. Sell it and the room goes. [Token rooms](https://bwalletx.com/chat)

- A stageGo live in a Space for holders: speakers, raise-hand, and anyone can listen. [bSpaces](https://bwalletx.com/bspaces)

Each piece gives people another reason to find the token, hold it and back the people making things for it.

## Pay the people who make it

Wherever there’s someone to thank there’s a Tip button: artists, NFT creators, rooms, people in chat and speakers in Spaces. All of it goes to them. On bMusic, listening is paying the artist. [Tips](https://bwalletx.com/tips)

## How a culture grows

- Launch a coin
- Open its room
- Make things
- Go live
- Tip the makers

Launch a coin from the [Launchpad](https://bwalletx.com/launchpad), give it something people can use, and its room is there for holders. The wallet won’t sign a token description that promises returns: describe the room and the things you make instead.

## Why BSV

- Tiny fees. A photo costs a fraction of a cent to put on chain; a song can be paid for a sat a second.

- Scale. Bitcoin SV is built for large blocks, so lots of small payments and posts fit.

- The content itself is on chain. Pictures, music and video can be stored on chain, not just a link to somewhere else.

## Your keys, your culture

bWalletX is non-custodial: the tokens, the art and the tips are held by your own keys. Spaces, bMovies and the Launchpad are not in bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

$FROGGER is an example made up for this page. Tokens can lose all their value. No returns are promised. Nothing here is investment advice. bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

A story about Partnership shares

# Digital Ice-Cream

Three friends, one van, real ice cream paid for in digital cash, and a token called $ICECREAM. Every cone splits the money fairly. Nobody runs off with the freezer.

A story about what’s coming: automatic splits by share and 3-key partner locks are not built yet. See [Partnership shares](https://bwalletx.com/partnership-shares) for what works today.

## The story, in eight scoops

How a stall becomes a partnership, and a partnership one day becomes a company.

1Meet Fred, Joe and You.Three friends. One dream. Ice cream.

2They make a token: $ICECREAM.Fred 30, Joe 30, You 40. You drive the van and put in more, so you hold more.

3Every cone splits itself.Each sale pays out 30/30/40 (then 27/27/36/10 when Max joins), straight into each friend’s wallet. No spreadsheet. No arguments.

4Locked together.Their shares are locked, so nobody can sell without the others agreeing. Three keys, one lock.

5Max fixes the freezers.Everyone agrees Max should join for 10%. The others scale down a little, and the split updates itself.

6b keeps the peace.b sits in their private partners’ chat, drafts the agreement and helps them agree. Each partner signs with their own wallet.

7Business booms.More vans, more flavours, more cones. Every sale still splits itself, to the penny.

8One day: Digital Ice-Cream Inc.They incorporate. Partnership shares convert 1:1 into company shares. Private placements bring in backers. Maybe, one day, a regulated IPO.

## The recipe, in three scoops

### Split

The token says who owns what. Money in splits by holding, automatically.

### Lock

Partnership shares stay locked until the partners agree to move them.

### Agree

b drafts the paperwork in your partners’ chat. Everyone signs with their own wallet.

[How Partnership shares work →](https://bwalletx.com/partnership-shares)
[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

Partnership shares are for partners, never sold to the public. Until you incorporate you’re a partnership: profits are shared and each partner is personally liable. b drafts, you decide — b isn’t a lawyer.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)
