BWALLET DIRECT

Direct

# Sign in straight from your own wallet

bWallet Direct is a bWalletX wallet you open with a passkey, and the way a website lets you in with it. No account to make, no password to invent, no middleman holding your login. Your wallet proves it is you; the site checks it.

[Make a wallet with a passkey](https://web.bwalletx.com)
[Add it to your site](https://bwalletx.com/connect)

## For customers

### 1. Make your wallet with a passkey

Face ID, a fingerprint or your device PIN opens it. Nothing to write down first. [How passkey sign-in works](https://bwalletx.com/direct).

### 2. Press “Sign in with bWalletX” on a site

Your wallet is found in your browser, in the app, or by scanning a QR code with your phone, and it asks you to approve.

### 3. You are in

The site gets a signature from your wallet’s identity key, nothing else: no email, name or password.

## For businesses

One script tag and two routes on your server. There is no API key, no client ID and no account with us: your server checks the signature itself. The same wallet gives the same ID every time they come back.

[Read the guide](https://bwalletx.com/connect)
[Plain-text version](https://bwalletx.com/connect.md)

## What works today

LIVE
### Sign in with bWalletX

Chrome extension, the app’s browser, and phone or web wallet by QR code.

LIVE
### Passkey wallets

Web, Chrome extension and the Android download.

PRIVATE
### Passkeys on iPhone

In the private build for now.

COMING
### Pay from the same button

Not packaged yet. Today the button signs people in only.

COMING
### Passkeys in the App Store and Google Play editions

Not in the store editions yet.

COMING
### Sign in to HandCash with bWalletX

Not built.

## Good to know

### Passkeys stay in your Apple or Google account

A passkey saved to iCloud cannot open a wallet on an Android phone, and the other way round. Keep your recovery file or 12 words as well.

### Not the same as the Android “direct” download

That is the bWalletX Android app you download from this site instead of Google Play. bWallet Direct is the sign-in service.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX for Chrome and Brave

The full bWalletX wallet in Chrome's side panel, and a wallet websites like TokenBlaster can connect to. Your keys stay in the extension.

[Add to Chrome →](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/choopkcgggoaehffickjojkohmpbladd)

From the Chrome Web Store. Works in Brave too. Updates itself.

## Latest build, direct (experimental)

The newest version before the Web Store has reviewed it. You install it by hand and update it by hand.

[Download the latest build (.zip) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-extension-5.2.45.zip)

Two separate wallets. The Web Store version and the direct build are different installs, and each keeps its own wallet. If you switch, write down your recovery words first and restore them in the new one. Never click Remove on the old one until you have: removing an extension deletes its wallet's records.

Updating the direct build? Use the ↻ reload button on `chrome://extensions`, or replace the files in the same folder.

To install the direct build:

- Unzip `bwalletx-extension-5.2.45.zip`.

- Open `chrome://extensions` in Chrome.

- Turn on Developer mode (top right).

- Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.

- Pin bWalletX, click it, and create or restore your wallet.

## Brave

Same extension, same file. Brave runs Chrome extensions, so:

- Unzip `bwalletx-extension-5.2.45.zip`.

- Open `brave://extensions` in Brave.

- Turn on Developer mode (top right).

- Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.

- Pin bWalletX from the puzzle-piece menu, click it, and create or restore your wallet.

# bWalletX features

One non-custodial BSV wallet: send and receive by name, message and call people, hold and make tokens, and connect to apps. Your keys never leave your device.

[Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[iPhone · web app](https://bwalletx.com/iphone)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[Desktop](https://bwalletx.com/desktop)
[Web](https://web.bwalletx.com)

bWalletX only in bWalletX (web, Chrome extension, Desktop, direct Android download). Cards without the tag are also in [bWallet](https://www.bwallet.space) from the App Store and Google Play. Coming means not shipped yet.

[Wallet](#wallet)[Identity](#you)[Exchange](#exchange)[Social](#social)[Creators](#create)[Build](#build)

## 💰Wallet

### Money

### Pay a name

Send to a $handle or a paymail like `name@bwalletx.com` instead of a long address. Send stops and asks if a name you paid before now points somewhere new.

### Dollars first

Balances, sends and every approval show the amount in dollars, with sats underneath. Live BSV price chart.

### Receive

Two tabs, Money and NFTs & names, each with its own address and QR, so nothing lands in the wrong place.

### Buy BSVbWalletX

Buy with a card from inside the wallet, sent straight to your address. [How](https://bwalletx.com/buy).

### History and exports

Every transaction for any date range, with CSV and PDF statements. Find a missing payment by its transaction ID. [More](https://bwalletx.com/history).

### Pots and standing orders

Set money aside in a pot and pay regular amounts from it. Pause or cancel any time. [More](https://bwalletx.com/pots).

### App subscriptionsbWalletX

Subscribe to an app from your wallet and manage it in the Subscriptions tab. [How](https://bwalletx.com/subscriptions).

### Lock BSV

Lock until a date, or pay yourself out over time on a curve, with optional public receipts. A lock never opens early. [More](https://bwalletx.com/lock).

### Several accounts

Keep separate accounts, each with its own name, under one master password.

### On every device

### Push notifications

DMs always reach you; set each room to All, Mentions or Off. Previews off by default, plus quiet hours. On phone, web and Chrome. [More](https://bwalletx.com/push-notifications).

### Edit home

Add, remove and reorder modules on your home screen.

### Desktop

The whole wallet on a big screen at desktop.bwalletx.com, or as a signed Mac app. [Download](https://bwalletx.com/desktop).

### Security and recovery

### Non-custodial

Keys are created and stored on your device. We never see them.

### Approve every request

Nothing is signed or paid without your tap, and outside apps can't use the wallet's own keys. Set a one-tap limit for small payments.

### Passkey sign-inbWalletX

Face ID or fingerprint on the web wallet and the direct Android download; the extension signs in through the web. Not in the store editions yet. [More](https://bwalletx.com/seedless-login).

### Face ID and fingerprint

Unlock with biometrics on your phone.

### Restore from anywhere

12 words, a private key or a backup file. Import from Yours, Panda, RelayX or Twetch. [How](https://bwalletx.com/restore).

### Encrypted backups

Your backup is encrypted and restored and checked first when you set up a new device.

### Sweep another wallet

Pull funds in from any 12/24-word wallet. Recover RelayX NFT collections too. [How](https://bwalletx.com/recover-relayx).

### Troubleshooting

Resync coins and recover payments from Settings, with plain-English results.

### Passwords

One master password, with a strength check. Changing it needs your current password, biometrics or your 12 words.

### bTrustbWalletX

Co-sign payments with other people; every payment and fee is shown before you sign. [More](https://bwalletx.com/btrust).

### Open source

The wallet code is public. [What is open, and under which licence](https://bwalletx.com/open-source).

### Delete your account

Remove your paymail, profile and messages from our servers whenever you like.

## 🪪Identity

### Names

### Your name

Claim a $handle and `yourname@bwalletx.com`, and get paid and messaged at it. Add extra names in Settings › Identity. [More](https://bwalletx.com/handles).

### Signed by you

Your name is signed by your own wallet, so nobody (us included) can quietly point it elsewhere. Every change goes in a public log, and a name only moves to another wallet when that wallet accepts. [More](https://bwalletx.com/name-bindings).

### Name StorebWalletX

Search, buy, sell or give names. Price depends on length. [More](https://bwalletx.com/names).

### Look-alike protection

Brand, provider and very short names are reserved, and names that imitate someone (a 1 for an l) are flagged in bMail and chat.

### Identity

### Link your accountsbWalletX

Link X and Google (and more as they arrive) in Settings › Identity. Each link is proved by the provider and signed by your wallet; your email is never shown. [More](https://bwalletx.com/identity).

### Linked walletsbWalletX

Prove you own an ETH, BNB, SOL or TRX address by signing with MetaMask, Phantom or TronLink. Identity only; no funds move.

### Identity map

See your identity key, the keys grown from it and every name that points at them, with a warning if something is mixed up. [More](https://bwalletx.com/identity-map).

### Profile and bAvatar

A display name and bAvatar that follow you into chat and the exchange. Tap it to flip to your pay code. [More](https://bwalletx.com/bavatars).

### Sign-in alerts

Get told when your handle signs in somewhere new, with a Recent sign-ins list.

### Verified identity (optional)

An ID check and certificate, only when something needs it. [More](https://bwalletx.com/identity#verify).

### Share one factComing

Prove one thing from your verified identity without sharing the rest.

## 📈Exchange

### Trade

### ExchangebWalletX

Browse, buy and sell tokens and NFTs wallet to wallet at prices you set. Token IDs, verified badges and look-alike warnings. Nobody holds your coins for you. [More](https://bwalletx.com/exchange).

### MemepoolbWalletX

Buy or sell TX Blaster Memepool coins from the wallet, up to 1 BSV a trade.

### Safety filterbWalletX

An always-on filter for unsafe content in the exchange.

### Tokens and NFTs

Hold, send and receive BSV-21 tokens, 1Sat Ordinals and MNEE. Swipe the wallet card to see each balance.

### Token locking

Lock tokens until a date: swipe a token row and tap Lock. [More](https://bwalletx.com/token-locking).

### Launch a coinbWalletX

Name, ticker, icon and one approval, with a published launch curve and a holders' room. The wallet won't sign a token sold with a promise of profit. [More](https://bwalletx.com/launchpad).

### Receive and shop

### Airdrops inbox

Tokens, NFTs and BSV sent to you wait in an inbox with Keep and Hide, and warnings for address-poisoning tricks. [More](https://bwalletx.com/airdrops).

### Store and themes

Shops with themes and packs, paid in BSV with one approval. Theme the whole app and your card. [Store](https://bwalletx.com/store) · [Themes](https://bwalletx.com/themes).

## 💬Social

### Messages and calls

### Friends

Your address book: message, call or pay anyone, and see their token and room. Import and export contacts.

### Chat

Direct messages and rooms, with swipe to pin, mute or archive. Chat is also on the web at [bchatx.com](https://www.bchatx.com); sign in with bWalletX. [More](https://bwalletx.com/chat).

### bMail

Mail between wallets, with sent copies kept and newest first. Send signed notes and agreements, sealed on chain. [More](https://bwalletx.com/bmail).

### Voice and video calls

Recents, contacts and a keypad. Flip camera mid-call; share your screen from the web, Desktop or the extension.

### Token roomsbWalletX

Every token gets a chat room; hold the token to join. The owner sets the rules, and can charge per message. [More](https://bwalletx.com/b-creative).

### bPhone: paid callsbWalletX

Set a rate to receive calls, paid wallet to wallet while you talk, and take bookings. [More](https://bwalletx.com/bphone).

### Contracts in chat

Ask b to draft an agreement in a room, sign it with your wallet, and seal a fingerprint on Bitcoin. [More](https://bwalletx.com/contracts).

### Tickets and bountiesbWalletX

Send a ticket token to invite someone into your room, or post a paid task and pay out when it's done.

### Tips

Tip the person behind a post, track or room in one tap, with an optional message. [More](https://bwalletx.com/tips).

### Spaces and feed

### bSpacesbWalletX

Live audio and video Spaces: a stage, speakers, raise-hand and invite links. Anyone can listen on the web. [More](https://bwalletx.com/bspaces).

### bWallet Lounge

The community room: ask questions, meet other users, talk to the team. [Join](https://www.bchatx.com/chat?room=LOUNGE).

### One feed for BSV social

Twetch, Treechat, bChatX, CoinGeek, Hodlocker and RelayX in one timeline, with sorting, favourites and a leaderboard. [More](https://bwalletx.com/social).

### Lock to like

Back a post by time-locking your own BSV against it. The coins stay yours.

### Media player

Play music and video NFTs you own, with a mini player and lock-screen playback. Publish your own release with a cover.

- Fixed bugs appear on [Known issues](https://bwalletx.com/bugs). Suggestions appear on [Ideas](https://bwalletx.com/ideas).

- Security reports are never published before the fix ships.

- We never publish your email or personal details. A review shows only your first name, and only if you tick the box.

## How it works

### 1. Download your data

Ask X or YouTube (Google Takeout) for your archive. They email you a zip. It is your data, and in the UK and EU you have a right to it.

### 2. Drop the zip on bMintX

The zip is read in your browser, and nothing is sent anywhere. You see what is inside and what it costs to mint, at cost price, before anything happens. For YouTube you pick which videos to mint.

### 3. Sign with bWalletX

Your wallet signs each piece and it is written to Bitcoin, keeping its original date. Your X posts land on bChatX. Your YouTube videos land on bVideoX. Your keys never leave your device.

## What is live today

LIVE
### X → bChatX

Your posts, follows and history, with a cost check in seconds.
[Flick off X →](https://bmintx.com/flick-off/x)

LIVE
### YouTube → bVideoX

Every video with its title, description and original upload date. See the cost of each one and pick.
[Flick off YouTube on bVideoX →](https://bvideox.com)

If you can download it, it can be flicked. Tell us which one you want next at [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com).

## The rules

### Your own content only

FLICK OFF mints what you posted. Other people's posts are not copied. A reply to someone else links to the original.

### Private messages stay private

Direct messages are counted so you know they exist. They are never minted publicly.

### Cost price, shown first

You see the mint cost before you sign. It pays the Bitcoin network fee, nothing more. What you mint is a permanent public record, so check it before you sign.

[bchatx.com →](https://chat.bwalletx.com)

# bGigs.

Every artist gets a Space with a link that never changes. Go live on camera and mic from your phone or the web, invite guests up on stage, and chat with the room while you play.

## Tickets at the door

Set a door price and fans pay once to come in. Or charge by the minute, so they pay only for what they listen to, and stop whenever they like. Either way, the money goes straight to you.

## Cards you make with b

Tell b who it’s for and what they love. b makes the card for $0.50 in BSV. You mint it as your own NFT, send it by bMail, and they keep it in their wallet or wear it as their bAvatar on bChatX.

## How it works

### 1. Make it with b

Describe the card in a sentence. b generates the picture with AI image generation. Birthday is picked for you.

### 2. Mint it

The card goes on Bitcoin SV as an NFT in your name, from the Mint in bWalletX. One tap, no files to juggle.

### 3. Send it by bMail

Pick a $name and the card arrives in their bMail, ready to open.

### 4. Keep it or wear it

It sits in their wallet as theirs. If they love it, they set it as their round bAvatar on bChatX and in their wallet.

## What it costs

You pay in BSV, from your wallet, and you see the total before you confirm. It has three parts:

- The generation. Making a picture with AI costs us real money, so you pay for it, plus a small premium on top.

- The minting fee. The Bitcoin SV network fee to put the card on chain, plus the usual bWalletX fee. See [Mint with bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/mint) for how minting is priced.

- The stamp. Sending by [bMail](https://bwalletx.com/bmail) works like the penny post.

Making a card is $0.50 in BSV today, shown in the card maker before you pay. Nothing is charged without your OK on the wallet’s pay sheet.

## Send to any public key Coming

Send a card to any public key — even Satoshi’s. Your card goes to the key’s address with a note only that key can open. We’re building this in the wallet now.

## Start from a photo or a post Coming

Drop in a photo, or paste the link to a post on X, and b turns it into a birthday card you can mint. This isn’t live yet: today you describe the card in words. We’ll tick it off here when it works.

## Bigger than birthdays

Cards are the first thing we’re building on Generation-as-a-Service: we run the AI on our servers, you pay per generation in BSV, and what you make is yours to mint. Thank-you cards, invitations, wedding cards and more kinds of generation will follow for everyone with bWalletX.

## Where we are

- LiveMint a picture as your own NFT from the Mint button in bWalletX

- LiveSend an NFT to someone’s $name from your wallet

- LivebMail inbox in bWalletX, with tokens and NFTs from new senders held in Quarantine

- LiveYour own generated bAvatar on bChatX, which you can mint

- LiveTalk to b in your wallet

- LiveMake a birthday card in the card maker (Mint › Greeting card in the bWalletX web wallet)

- LivePay $0.50 in BSV for each card, in the wallet’s pay sheet

- LiveMint the card as your own NFT from the card maker

- ComingSend a card to any public key, even Satoshi’s, with a note only that key can open

- ComingStart a card from a photo you drop in or a link to a post on X

- ComingSend a card by bMail, with the card shown as the letter

- ComingWear a card you were sent as your bAvatar on bChatX and in your wallet

- ComingMore generations: thank-yous, invitations and other kinds of picture

[Mint a birthday card $0.50](https://web.bwalletx.com/m/bmint/mint/card)
[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Tell b who it’s for](https://web.bwalletx.com/m/ask-b?ask=I%27d%20like%20to%20make%20a%20birthday%20card%20for%20someone.%20It%27s%20for%3A%20)

The card in the animation is our own drawing. The card maker is in the bWalletX web wallet and the bWalletX apps, not the bWallet store edition. # History. Where your money went.

Every transaction your account has made, read from the chain. Pick a date range, see what came in and went out, and export it in a form your accountant can use.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## What it does today

- LiveFull on-chain history. Every transaction that touched the account’s addresses, not just ones made on this device.

- LiveDate ranges. 7 days, 30 days, this year, all time, or your own dates.

- LiveSummary. In, out, fees and net for the range.

- LiveLabels. Tips, likes, pot payments and agent spend are named where the wallet can tell.

- LiveCSV export. A spreadsheet of the range, one row per transaction.

- LivePDF statement. A printable statement of the range. On a phone, open it and use Print › Save as PDF.

- LiveTokens and NFTs. Buys, sells, listings, cancels, transfers and mints, each showing the token or NFT and the amount. Since 5.1.82.

- LiveGames, subscriptions and apps. Payments to games, pots and subscriptions, and apps you connected, each with its own label. Since 5.1.82.

- LiveCategory filters. All, Payments, Tokens, NFTs, Games, Subscriptions, Apps, Social. Exports include the category, asset and app. Since 5.1.82.

- Live since 5.1.85Correct amounts. Transactions your wallet funded for an app or token trade now show the right amount.

- LiveConnections log. Which apps used the wallet, when, what you allowed them, what each spent, and a button to revoke access. Recorded on each device from 5.1.82.

- LiveGains and losses. A Gains tab with realised gains and losses per tax year: UK HMRC share-pooling rules in pounds by default, FIFO in dollars elsewhere, BSV tracked as an asset, and a disposals CSV for your accountant. Since 5.1.85. Gains is in beta: figures may be incomplete, so check them against your own records.

Open it from the wallet: tap History on the account card. Payments from a pot show there too; see [Subscriptions and Pots](https://bwalletx.com/subscriptions).

History and its exports are records, not tax advice. Check with an accountant before you file.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

[On b](https://bwalletx.com/on-b) · Using Hodlocker with bWalletX

Hodlocker+

# Hodlocker on b

Hodlocker made locking popular: you back a post by time-locking your own BSV against it. The site has gone, but the idea lives on in bWalletX, written in the same on-chain format.

## What you can do

### Lock behind any post

In the Feed, tap Lock on a post. Pick an amount and a time: a day, a week, a month, or your own (up to about ten years). One approval and it’s done.

### Your BSV stays yours

The coins never leave your wallet. They sit in a lock only your key can open, show on the Wallet’s Locks row, and unlock on the date shown.

### Same format Hodlocker used

Each lock is the same lockup contract plus a like for the post, the shape Hodlocker wrote and read. Locks on a post are counted from the chain.

### Most locked

A board of the most locked people and posts over a day, a week, a month or all time. It counts the posts bWalletX has loaded, and says so.

## Status

What works in bWalletX today, and what doesn’t yet.

- ✓ LiveLock BSV behind a post, 1 day to about 10 years

- ✓ LiveSame lockup contract and like format as Hodlocker

- ✓ LiveLocks show on the Wallet’s Locks row and unlock on the date

- ✓ LiveLock totals for a post, read from the chain

- ✓ LiveMost locked board: people and posts, 1D / 7D / 1M / All

- ○ Not yetLock totals across the whole network (no live lock indexer since Hodlocker closed)

- ○ Not yetLocks made on Twetch counted on the board

- ○ Not yetChecked: finding locks you made on Hodlocker with another wallet

## Your keys. Your device. Your call.

# You’re invited to bWalletX.

bWalletX is your own Bitcoin wallet and account in one: your money, your name and your posts, held by you.

[ChromeBrowser extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[Webweb.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com)

## Share this invite

Your X handle (optional), so friends see who invited them

Copy link

[Post to X](#)

## Inviting people into a Space? The token is the ticket.

Each Space invite carries a small amount of the room’s token, and holding it is what lets them in. [About Spaces](https://bwalletx.com/bspaces)

There are two kinds of invite. They do different jobs.

## Open Drops

A link holding some of a token. The first person to open it claims it. Good for a post or a group chat, where you don’t know exactly who will come.

- Make a dropPut some of the room’s token into a link.

- Share itPost it anywhere.

- First to open claims itThey sign in with X or HandCash, get bWalletX, and the token lands in their wallet.

## Named Invites

An invite for one person. Only the X account you name can claim it, and the token is sent to them automatically when they do.

- Pick peopleChoose X accounts, from the people you follow, your HandCash friends or a pasted list.

- Attach a tokenEach invite carries some of the room’s token. That token is their ticket into the Space.

- They sign inThe named person signs in with that X account, gets bWalletX, and the token arrives. They’re let into the room’s chat.

## Friends find each other

Planned: as the people in your contacts join, they’ll be matched to their paymails and show up as friends. You won’t have to look anyone up.

## Keep it safe

- An Open Drop link carries the token. Whoever opens it first claims it, so share it only where you mean to.

- A Named Invite works only for the X account it names. Someone else holding the link can’t claim it.

- We never hold the tokens. They go from the host’s wallet to yours.

## Where this stands

- ✓ LiveAddress book import (CSV, contact cards, JSON, pasted lists) and export to CSV: in the app (5.2.45). Each paymail is looked up as you import.

- ✓ LiveSign in with HandCash on bchatx.com: switched on; first real sign-in being tested.

- ✓ LiveHandCash friends into your address book: the server side is live; the wallet button is coming.

- LiveOpen Drops: live in bWalletX 5.2.26 (first run pending). Each link is made for an @handle and pre-funded with the room token; whoever opens it first gets the token, and room entry is tied to that X account.

- ComingNamed Invites: the token delivered automatically to the X account you name. Planned; depends on pre-signed payments.

- ComingImport the people you follow on X: planned.

- ComingContacts auto-match to paymails as friends join: not in the app yet. Today the import looks up each paymail once.

Related: [bSpaces](https://bwalletx.com/bspaces) · [bMail](https://bwalletx.com/bmail) · [Airdrops](https://bwalletx.com/airdrops) · [Friends](https://bwalletx.com/friends) · [Sign in with X](https://bwalletx.com/x)

# bWalletX on iPhone

Apple only allows App Store apps on iPhone, and the App Store edition (bWallet) can’t trade. Until there’s a better route, bWalletX on iPhone is a web app: the full wallet, installed from Safari onto your Home Screen. Read [where your keys are](#keys) before you use it.

Open in Safari→Share→Add to Home Screen

## Install it (one minute)

- On your iPhone, open [web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com) in Safari.

- Tap the Share button (the square with an arrow).

- Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen, then Add.

- Open bWalletX from your Home Screen, and create or restore your wallet there.

## Where your keys are, honestly

### On your phone, not on our servers

The web app is the same non-custodial wallet: your keys are created on the phone, encrypted with your password, and kept in the app’s own storage on the device. We never see them.

### But web storage is more fragile than a real app

iPhone can clear a website’s storage. The installed Home Screen app is much safer than a Safari tab: it has its own storage, the app asks iOS to keep it, and the “7 days unused” rule only counts days you open it. It can still be lost if you delete the Home Screen icon, clear website data in Settings, or don’t open it for a long time. A Safari tab is cleared much sooner, so always use the icon.

### So: it makes you back up first

Before you can receive money, the web app makes you back up. Either save an encrypted backup file (locked with your wallet password) to Files or email it to yourself, or write down your recovery phrase on paper and confirm three of the words. Keep the password with the file; with either backup you can restore the wallet in any bWallet or bWalletX, on any device. Every month it checks you still have it.

It’s still a beta: keep small amounts in it.

## What’s different from Android

### The same wallet

Tokens, the Exchange and Strategies, names, chat rooms, agent accounts and the b agent all work, and the same recovery phrase works in every edition.

### A few phone features are limited

The web app unlocks with your password. A wallet made with a passkey signs in with Face ID on web.bwalletx.com in Safari: see [passkey sign-in](https://bwalletx.com/seedless-signin). Pairing the [CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) works while the app is open on screen.

## The native app: join the TestFlight beta

bWallet is our native iPhone app, the App Store edition: send, receive, tokens, names, chat and calls. It has no Market or Exchange; trading is only in bWalletX. You can run it today through Apple’s TestFlight beta.

[Join the iPhone beta on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/1TTnQNKm)

- Install TestFlight from the App Store if you don’t have it.

- Open the link above on your iPhone and tap Accept, then Install.

- New versions arrive through TestFlight automatically. Beta builds expire after 90 days; the next one replaces them.

It hasn’t been submitted to the App Store itself yet: that waits on converting our Apple developer account to an organisation account. [Join the waitlist](https://www.bwallet.space/#waitlist) to hear when it’s out.

[Open web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com)
[Other devices](https://bwalletx.com/get)

Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Jobs

Paid work on bWalletX. The code is open source; the pay is in BSV; every payout is public on [/bounties](https://bwalletx.com/bounties).

Sign up now. Payouts open soon. You can sign in with bWalletX, fill in your profile and submit work today. Payouts start once identity checks with Veriff are live, which is coming soon. Work you submit now is paid once you are verified.

## Open contracts

### Security testing (b-Aware)
Live

Critical 10 BSV · High 3 BSV · Medium 0.5 BSV · Low: credit

Paid from a 20 BSV pool each quarter.

Read the code and try the apps. Find a way to take funds, read keys, or get past an approval in bWalletX, bWallet or bChatX.

- Test only your own wallets and accounts. No real users' funds or data.
- First valid report of an issue is paid. Duplicates earn credit.
- Rewards are paid after the fix ships.
- Keep it private until it is fixed. Full policy and safe harbour on b-Aware.
- Anyone can report by email. To receive a reward you sign in with bWalletX on this page and verify your identity with Veriff.

How to submit: Email support@bwalletx.com with the subject b-Aware. Not the form below.

[Read the b-Aware policy and rates →](https://bwalletx.com/b-aware)

### Paid Android testing
Live

1 BSV per tester

0.25 BSV after the first open from Google Play, 0.75 BSV after 12 of 14 daily check-ins. New testers are paid once identity checks (Veriff) are live.

Install bWallet from the Google Play test and use it every day for 14 days: send a little, receive, try the features, and tell us what breaks.

- Apply with Google on /testers first. Testers are approved by hand.
- Use the Google account on your Android phone.
- One tester per person. The app checks in once a day when you open it.
- Sign in with bWalletX below to send test reports and notes.
- Payouts need a bWalletX sign-in and a Veriff check, like all paid work.

Set per contract

## How it works

- Sign in with bWalletX. Your wallet signs a one-time message. Nothing is spent.

- Verify your identity with Veriff, our KYC provider. Coming

- Submit your work: a test report, a fix, a finding.

- b checks it. b looks for duplicates and checks the work against the code.

- The team approves. b proposes a payout; a person on the team approves it.

- You are paid in BSV to your bWalletX paymail, and the payout is listed in public on [/bounties](https://bwalletx.com/bounties).

## Getting paid

To take paid work you sign in with bWalletX and verify your identity with Veriff (our KYC provider). We pay to your bWalletX paymail.

- No anonymous contractors. Every contractor has a bWalletX sign-in, a legal name, a country, at least one linked account (X, GitHub or Google) and a Veriff check. Veriff also does the sanctions check.

- Paid only to your own paymail, `yourname@bwalletx.com`. We never pay to an address pasted into a form or a message.

- Verify with Veriff: coming. Until it is live you can sign in, fill in your profile and submit work. Payouts start once you are verified.

- Security reports stay open to anyone by email. A reward for one needs sign-in and Veriff too.

This is paid work, not an investment. Amounts are set per job and only paid after approval.

- Signed in with bWalletX Live

- Contractor profile (legal name, country, linked account) Live

- Verify with Veriff Coming

- Payouts to your paymail After Veriff

Move to bWalletX

# Bring everything home.

Coins, NFTs, tokens, names and your posts. bWalletX sweeps them in from the wallet you used before, right on your own device. Moving is free; you only pay the normal network fee, usually a cent or less.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)[Get the app](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Pick your wallet](#wallets)[From a social network](#services)

On your deviceYour phrase or key is typed into bWalletX and held in memory for the sweep only. It is never stored or sent to us.

Nothing burnedAnything that looks like a token but can’t be read is listed, not swept, so it can’t be lost by accident.

See it firstEvery sweep shows what it found, in dollars, before you tap. Tick only what you want.

## From another wallet

Find your old wallet below. Live routes work in bWalletX today. Coming ones aren’t built yet: don’t paste their keys anywhere in the meantime.

[Yours / Panda](#yours)[RelayX](#relayx)[Twetch](#twetch)[SimplyCash](#simplycash)[Money Button](#moneybutton)[Paper key / WIF](#wif)[Other phrase](#other)[HandCash](#handcash)[Electrum SV](#electrum)[Metanet / Babbage](#metanet)

### Yours / Panda Wallet
Live

What movesBSV, 1Sat NFTs, BSV-21 tokens, from the payment, ordinals and identity keys (and the older Yours payment key).
You needYour 12-word Yours recovery phrase.

- In bWalletX, open Settings › Account data › Sweep into this account.
- Paste your Yours phrase. All the Yours keys are tried for you.
- Check what it found, tick it, tap Sweep.

New to bWalletX? Restoring with your Yours phrase opens the same wallet directly, since bWalletX uses the same keys.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)

### RelayX
Live

What movesBSV, RelayX NFT collections (Run jigs) and 1Sat ordinals from your RelayX keys. Listed items can be cancelled first.
You needYour 12-word RelayX recovery phrase.

- Open Restore › RelayX, or the sweep screen in Settings.
- Paste your RelayX phrase. bWalletX scans RelayX’s payment and ordinals paths.
- Review coins and NFTs, then sweep them home.

RelayX itself is offline. Recovery reads the chain directly, so it still works.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)[Full RelayX guide](https://bwalletx.com/recover-relayx)

### Twetch wallet
Live

What movesBSV on your Twetch payment key, plus anything on the shared Yours-style keys.
You needYour Twetch 12-word recovery phrase.

- Open Restore › Twetch, or Sweep into this account.
- Paste the phrase. The Twetch path is tried automatically.
- Confirm the amount and sweep.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)

### SimplyCash
Live

What movesBSV, NFTs and tokens on SimplyCash’s path `m/44'/145'/0'`, receive and change.
You needYour 12 words, or the full SimplyCash recovery string (words:path:passphrase).

- Open Restore › SimplyCash or the sweep screen.
- Paste the words or recovery string.
- bWalletX walks the addresses until 20 in a row are unused, then shows the total.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)[Full SimplyCash guide](https://bwalletx.com/sweep-simplycash)

### Money Button
Live

What movesBSV on Money Button’s path `m/44'/0'/0'`. Old Money Button “assets” (SFP tokens) are shown but can’t move: they needed Fabriik’s server, which is gone.
You needYour Money Button 12-word phrase (and passphrase, if you set one).

- Open Sweep into this account.
- Paste your phrase. The Money Button path is in the standard scan.
- Sweep the BSV. SFP tokens are kept out of the sweep so they aren’t spent as plain coins.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)

Live

What movesEverything on that one address: BSV, NFTs and BSV-21 tokens. An xprv works too.
You needThe private key, usually starting with `5`, `K` or `L`.

- Open Sweep into this account and paste the key.
- Or open Restore › Restore with private key to use it as an account.
- Sweep. Treat the paper key as spent afterwards.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)

Live

What movesBSV, NFTs and tokens on the common BSV layouts: BIP44 coin types 236’ and 0’, or a custom path you type.
You needThe 12 or 24 words and, if your old wallet used one, its derivation path.

- Open Sweep into this account.
- Paste the phrase. If the chosen path is empty, the other common paths are tried.
- Still nothing? Use Custom path.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)

## Tokens, ordinals and names

They ride along with any live wallet route above. Here’s how each kind is treated.

### 1Sat ordinals (NFTs)
Live

Swept as NFTs once their origin is confirmed as a real inscription. Images, music, collectibles and bAvatars all count.

### BSV-21 tokens
Live

Found by balance and swept one token at a time, so each lands intact in your bWalletX tokens list.

### BSV-20 and unreadable items
Listed

Anything that might be a token but can’t be confirmed is shown with a warning and never swept, because spending it as a plain NFT could burn it.

### OpNS names
Live

OpNS names are 1Sat ordinals, so they move with your NFTs. After moving, set one as your name in bWalletX.

[About names](https://bwalletx.com/handles)

## Stay safe while you move

- Never share your phrase or key. Not with b, not with support, not in any chat or form. We will never ask for it.

- Type it only into bWalletX, on your own device. Only public addresses are looked up online to find your coins.

- Check the address bar. bWalletX on the web is only ever `web.bwalletx.com`.

- Test with a little first. For larger amounts, bWalletX offers a small test sweep before the rest.

- Afterwards, treat the old phrase as retired. Your coins are now protected by your bWalletX backup, so make that backup now.

## Questions

Does it cost anything?
No fee from us. Each sweep pays the normal Bitcoin SV network fee, a fraction of a cent for most moves.

It found nothing.
Check every word and add the passphrase if you used one. Then try Custom path. You can also ask b in the app, without ever sharing your phrase.

Is it in the App Store and Play versions?
Yes. Sweep is in every bWalletX and bWallet build, and on [web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com).

My wallet isn’t listed.
If it gave you 12 or 24 words, try the [Any other BIP39 phrase](#other) route. Otherwise email [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com) with the wallet’s name (never the phrase) and we’ll look at adding it.

# Names you can check. Even against us.

Your bWalletX name is signed by your own wallet. Every wallet checks that signature before it pays. And every change to who a name points to goes in a public log that anyone can read, including changes we make ourselves.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Read the name log →](https://pay.bwallet.space/api/paymail/name-log)

## What a name is

A bWalletX name is `alice@bwalletx.com`, or `$alice` for short. It points to one wallet’s identity key. When someone pays `$alice`, their wallet asks our name server which key the name points to, then pays that key directly.

We never hold your keys or your coins. Payments go wallet to wallet. But the name itself is a row in our database.

## The risk, plainly

Whoever controls the name directory could point a name at a different key. Payments already made are safe. But future payments to that name would go to the new key. That is a real power, and we hold it. On 17 October 2026 we used it: at the owner’s request we moved two of his own names between his own two wallets by editing the database directly. Nobody lost anything. But it showed how easy it was, and that nobody else could have seen it. So we built limits, and we made every use of the power public. The story is in [blog 058](https://bwalletx.com/blog/058-signed-names).

## Three layers

### 1. Signed bindings

The wallet that owns a name signs a short statement: “this name points to my key, version N”. Our name server hands that signature out with the key. We can’t make that signature for a key we don’t hold. Before every payment to a bWalletX name, the paying wallet checks it and shows one of three things:

- Signed by its owner. The key’s holder put this name on this key.

- Not signed by its owner yet. A grey note. The payment still works. Wallets sign their names when they next open, so this fades out.

- Bad signature. The signature doesn’t match. The payment is blocked.

### 2. A public name log

Every change of who a name points to is written to a log. Each entry includes the hash of the one before, so entries can’t be quietly changed or removed. A database trigger writes the entries, so a direct database edit by us is logged too, marked `admin`. The first three entries are exactly that: our own edits on 17 October.

Each entry says who made the change: `owner` (the name’s owner signed it), `server` (our server made it for a request the owner signed) or `admin` (anything else, which means us).

### 3. On chain (coming)

Next, the log’s latest hash goes into a Bitcoin transaction once a day, so the log can’t be rewritten after the fact. And for names that must never depend on us at all, there are [OpNS names](https://bwalletx.com/names): names held on chain, in your own wallet.

## Standing on others’ work

We did not invent signed names. Others got there first, and we are building toward their work:

- [BRC-169](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/BRCs/blob/master/peer-to-peer/0169.md) binds a handle to a key with a certificate signed by the host, and tells wallets to warn before paying when a name’s key changes. Ours is signed by the owner instead, and fits inside ordinary paymail. Our wallet now has that key-change warning too.

- [BRC-174](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/BRCs/blob/master/tokens/0174.md) is the formal spec for on-chain names (OpNS) bound to a key. That is where bWalletX names are headed.

- The [paymail standard](https://tsc.bsvblockchain.org/standards/paymail/) already names this risk: “Alias Reassignment (server & database access)”.

- [Certificate Transparency](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162) showed how public, append-only logs keep operators honest. Our log is a simple version of that idea.

What we add is small: the owner’s signature inside the paymail answer that wallets already fetch, and a log that records our own database edits.

## Check a name yourself

You don’t need our app. Ask the name server for a name’s key and binding:

``curl https://pay.bwallet.space/api/paymail/id/npg@bwalletx.com``

The answer has `pubkey` and, once the owner’s wallet has signed, a `binding` with `alias`, `seq`, `timestamp` and `signature`. Read the log, whole or for one name:

``curl https://pay.bwallet.space/api/paymail/name-log
curl "https://pay.bwallet.space/api/paymail/name-log?alias=npg"``

Then check the signature with `@bsv/sdk`. The signed message is these fields, in this order:

``bwallet-paymail|v1|bind|alias=<alias>|identityKey=<key>|seq=<n>|timestamp=<ms>``
``import { ProtoWallet, Utils } from '@bsv/sdk';

const r = await fetch('https://pay.bwallet.space/api/paymail/id/npg@bwalletx.com').then((x) => x.json());
const b = r.binding; // undefined = not signed by its owner yet
const msg = `bwallet-paymail|v1|bind|alias=${b.alias}|identityKey=${r.pubkey}|seq=${b.seq}|timestamp=${b.timestamp}`;
const { valid } = await new ProtoWallet('anyone').verifySignature({
data: Utils.toArray(msg, 'utf8'),
signature: Utils.toArray(b.signature, 'hex'),
protocolID: [2, 'bwallet paymail'],
keyID: '1',
counterparty: r.pubkey,
});
console.log(valid ? 'Signed by its owner' : 'Bad signature');``

The log’s hash rule: `entry_hash = sha256(prev_hash|alias|identity_key|prev_identity_key|action|actor|seq|signature|note|created_at)`, with empty strings for missing fields and `created_at` in UTC as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`. The first entry’s `prev_hash` is 64 zeros. The full write-up is in our [draft standard](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet/blob/main/docs/brc-draft-paymail-name-bindings.md).

## The limits

- We still serve the bindings and the log. We could hold back a binding. The name would then show “not signed”, which you can see.

- We could serve an older genuine binding. Its version number would be lower than the one in the log, which you can see.

- The log is in our database until it is anchored on chain. The hash chain shows edits to past entries, but only once someone has kept a copy to compare. Keep one if you like.

- A name with no binding yet can’t be checked by signature, only by the log.

Only layer 3 takes us out of the picture. We will say so on this page until it ships.

## Status, 17 Oct 2026

- ✓ LiveSigned bindings. Wallets sign their own names and check names before paying.

- ✓ LiveBad signatures block payment.

- ✓ LivePublic name log. Hash-chained, append-only, every change logged by the database itself, including ours.

- ✓ LiveOur 17 Oct edits in the log as its first three entries, marked `admin`.

- ✓ LiveHandovers need both wallets. A name moves only when its owner releases it and the new wallet accepts. No one, us included, can move it any other way.

- ✓ LiveNo back door for lost keys. A name stays with its key. Recovery is yours, set up in advance.

- ✓ LiveKey-change warning. If a name you’ve paid before points somewhere new without a handover, Send stops.

- ✓ LiveProposed to the BRC authors in [BRCs issue #329](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/BRCs/issues/329).

- ◻ ComingDaily on-chain anchor of the log’s latest hash.

- ◻ ComingOpNS names in the wallet as the name that never depends on us.

## Questions

### Are you custodial?

No. Your keys are made on your device and never reach us. We can’t spend your coins or sign for you. The name directory is the one thing we control, and this page is about limiting it.

### Can you change my name?

Technically, yes. Anyone who runs a name directory can. What we can’t do is make your wallet’s signature for a different key, or change past log entries without it showing to anyone who kept a copy. Once the daily anchor ships, it will show to everyone.

### What happens if you do?

Payers’ wallets stop showing “Signed by its owner” for that name, because the new key has no signature from you. A forged signature blocks payment. And the change appears in the public log, with who made it.

### How does a name move to a new wallet properly?

The old owner releases it, then the new wallet signs its own binding for the name. Both steps are in the log.

### Why not just use OpNS?

We will, for names that matter most. OpNS names are held on chain in your wallet, so they don’t depend on us at all. But a paymail like `alice@bwalletx.com` works with every paymail wallet today, and it’s free and instant to claim. Signed bindings make that kind of name checkable while OpNS grows.

Related: [Names](https://bwalletx.com/names) · [Handles](https://bwalletx.com/handles) · [Identity](https://bwalletx.com/identity) · [058 We could move your name](https://bwalletx.com/blog/058-signed-names)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Partnership shares.

Start something with friends. Share it fairly. Incorporate when you’re ready.

## The path

Most things stay small, and that’s fine. Each step is optional. You only take the next one when you want to.

Token→Rooms→Partnership shares→Company→Private placements→One day: IPO

### Token

Launch a token for your idea. People who like it can hold it.

### Rooms

The token works as a ticket to your chat rooms. Your community gathers there.

### Partnership shares

When a few of you start working on it together, record who owns what.

### Company

Incorporate. Partnership shares become company shares, one for one.

### Private placements

Raise money from people you choose, under the company’s own rules.

### One day: IPO

A regulated public offering. Only then can shares trade in public.

## An ice-cream story

How it will work. Locked partner shares and splits by set shares are not built yet. See Coming below.

Fred, Joe and you decide to sell ice cream, paid for in digital cash. You set up Partnership shares: Fred 30%, Joe 30%, you 40%.

Fred 27

Joe 27

You 36

Max 10

After Max joins: everyone gives up a tenth, so 30/30/40 becomes 27/27/36, plus Max 10.

- Locked together. The shares will be locked, so nobody can sell theirs without the others agreeing.

- Max joins. Max has freezers. The three of you agree to admit him for 10%.

- Every sale splits itself. Money from each sale will go straight to each partner by their share. No spreadsheet.

- Incorporate later. When the business grows, you form a company. Each partnership share becomes one company share.

## b drafts it with you

The partners get a shared chat that only they are in. b, the bWalletX assistant, is in it too.

b drafts your partnership agreement, and any change to it. b explains each term in plain words. Anything still open is marked [TO BE AGREED], so you can settle it point by point. Each of you accepts with your own wallet. Help with disputes after signing is coming; see [Contracts in chat](https://bwalletx.com/contracts).

When you all agree, each partner signs with their own wallet. Nobody signs for anyone else.

b is not a lawyer. Drafts are for the partners to read and agree. For bigger stakes, take advice from a solicitor or accountant.

## Know what a partnership is

Until you incorporate, you are a partnership. Profits are shared. Each partner is personally liable for the business’s debts. Each partner pays tax on their own share.

Partnership shares are never offered to the public. Public trading comes only after a regulated offering.

## Built working

These pieces are in bWalletX today, or in testing where marked.

- Token launch. Launch a token for your idea.

- Token-gated rooms. A token works as a ticket to a chat room.

- Multisig locks (in testing). Shares locked so more than one person has to agree to move them. Today only on The Bitcoin Corporation’s own register; partner locks are being built.

- Automatic splits. Paid Spaces split each payment equally between the speakers on stage. Splits by set shares between partners are not built yet.

- Ask b. The built-in assistant, in the wallet and in chat.

- b in partner chats. In a partnership room, ask b to draft an agreement or sum up the terms. Every member accepts a draft agreement with their own wallet.

- bShares register. A register of members for any company, [in testing](https://bwalletx.com/bshares); the first register is our own company.

## Coming planned

These are plans. They are not built yet.

- Partner locks and splits by set shares. Shares locked between the partners, and each payment split by share.

- Partnership shares set-up. Name the partners, set the split, and get a generated agreement.

- Admit a partner. Bring someone in with everyone’s agreement, and the split updates.

- Incorporate. Convert partnership shares to company shares, one for one.

- bShares for many companies. Any company can keep its register in bShares.

## Start with the wallet

Everything here lives in bWalletX.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Peck on b

Peck posts are plain Bitcoin Schema on chain, so bWalletX can read them. Use Peck as you do, and follow it from the same place you keep your coins.

## What you can do

### Read Peck in the Feed

Open Feed and pick the Peck chip. Posts come from Peck’s public overlay, current to the latest block. Tap a name to see that author’s posts; tap Open to see a post on peck.to.

### Tip signed authors

When a post’s signature checks out, the tip goes to the address that signed it. If it can’t be tied to the author, the tip button says so instead of guessing.

### Like, reply and lock

Lock BSV behind a post you rate; it stays yours. Likes and replies you make here are written on chain as bChat posts.

## Status

What works in bWalletX today, and what doesn’t yet.

- ✓ LivePeck posts in the Feed, from its public overlay

- ✓ LiveA Peck author’s posts on one page

- ✓ LiveTip authors whose signature checks out

- ✓ LiveLock, like and reply from bWalletX (written as bChat)

- ○ Not yetYour bWalletX posts showing in the Peck app

- ○ Not yetImport who you follow on Peck

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get?from=peck-on-b)

Your keys stay with you: bWalletX is self-custody. Peck is a separate service; bWalletX is not affiliated with it. Logos belong to their owners. [More apps on b](https://bwalletx.com/on-b).

Linked sign-ins show how many accounts this person has connected. It is not identity verification.

# Push notifications

Never miss a message. Push notifications are live since version 5.1.70 and reach you even with the app closed: on your phone, the web wallet and the Chrome extension. They run through our own push server, push.bwalletx.com.

LiveiPhoneAndroidWebChrome extension

## Where it works

### iPhone

Apple Push Notifications.

### Android

Firebase Cloud Messaging.

### Web wallet and Chrome extension

Web Push, so your browser can tell you even when the tab isn't open.

## Turning it on

Go to Settings › Notifications › Push notifications. In the phone apps the switch starts on. In the web wallet and the Chrome extension it starts off: turn it on there and your browser asks for permission. The switch is per device; previews and quiet hours belong to your account and follow you to every device.

## What notifies you

- Direct messages from friends, always.

- Group chats: each group has a bell with All, Mentions or Off. Groups start on Mentions, so busy rooms don't buzz you all day.

- Mentions of your `$name`.

- Photos, voice and video messages sent to a room you're in.

- $b answers to your `/b` questions.

- Requests to sign or witness a document.

Tapping a notification opens the room or screen it's about. Several messages in quick succession are collapsed into one.

## Privacy

By default a notification says who messaged you, not what they wrote, so nothing private shows on your lock screen. If you want message previews, turn on Show message previews. Quiet hours silence notifications overnight or whenever you choose. No message text is stored on our push server.

You can turn notifications off per group with the bell, or entirely in Settings › Notifications. Your keys never leave your device; notifications don't need them.

## bWalletX and bWallet

Notifications work the same in both editions: bWalletX here, and bWallet, the App Store and Google Play version.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

# Your RelayX NFTs are still yours.

RelayX has closed, but the NFTs you bought or minted there are still on chain, held by the keys in your RelayX 12 words. bWalletX finds them and shows you your whole collection again, picture by picture. Your words stay on your phone, and finding them moves nothing.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Read the guide →](https://docs.bwalletx.com/recover-relayx-collections/)

RECOVER

## Recover RelayX collections

A screen in bWalletX made for one job: finding the NFTs your RelayX words still hold.

RelayX and its logo belong to their owners, shown here to identify the wallet. bWalletX is not affiliated with RelayX.

## How to find them

- Open bWalletX and scroll to the bottom of your wallet.

- Under Bring in old assets, tap Recover RelayX collections.

- Enter your RelayX 12 words. Paste them however you saved them: spaces, commas or a numbered list all work.

- Tap Find my NFTs. bWalletX reads the chain for each of your RelayX addresses and counts up what it finds.

- Your NFTs appear as a gallery, grouped by collection.

- Tap one to see it large: its number, collection, and the address that holds it.

### Or keep them in bWalletX

- Add your RelayX wallet to bWalletX: Restore, choose RelayX, and enter your 12 words.

- A blue Your RelayX collection card appears at the top of that account. Tap it once to find your NFTs; no words to type again.

- From then on they are in your wallet’s NFTs tab: choose Run (or All) to see them next to your other NFTs.

- If your old RelayX addresses still hold BSV, tap Move it into this account.

Your words stay on your phone.
Your NFTs appear as they are found.

## Ninja Punk Girls

Ninja Punk Girls was one of the largest collections on RelayX. Every one of them is now identified:

- Series 2: all 3,333 NFTs, each matched to her card number and shown with NPG’s card art. RelayX stored the pictures encrypted (they can’t be shown from the chain), so most were matched by the exact size of each minted file, and the rest by mint order between those matches.

- Series 1: all 25 NFTs, identified by name (13 girls).

- Single-girl collections such as KAZUYO and AIKA are named from the collection itself.

### Optional, NPG only: melt a girl into her element cards

Each NPG is built from layered element cards: hair, face, outfit, weapon and more. If you hold one, you can melt her into those cards for the NPG games, plus her round avatar badge, which only someone who melted an original can hold.

What melting really does: your RelayX NFT is a Run token, a format almost no wallet reads any more. Melting destroys that Run token on chain (it can’t be undone) and mints each of her parts fresh as a 1Sat Ordinal, the NFT standard bWalletX and today’s BSV wallets and markets use. You see every part, and the fees, before you allow it.

Melt: see every part before you allow it.
Done: her parts are now 1Sat Ordinals.

- One approval. A single sheet shows her, the cards she becomes, and the fees.

- Fees at cost. About 1¢ for the network and minting. No melt fee.

- The old NFT is burned on chain, in a way anyone can check. That is what makes the new cards hers and nobody else’s.

- Series 1 melts into the redrawn element set for that girl: the same girl, redrawn as parts, not the original artwork.

## Safety

- Your words never leave your phone. bWalletX reads public chain data only. Nothing about your keys is sent to us or to anyone.

- Finding is read-only. The scan moves nothing.

- Nothing moves unless you choose. The only action today is the optional NPG melt: one deliberate tap on one NFT.

- RelayX NFTs are never swept. bWalletX recognises them before anything else and won’t spend them as coins.

## Status, 18 Oct 2026

- ✓ 5.2.30NPG Series 2 identified by card number (matched by mint order), shown with NPG's card art; the on-chain image is encrypted. Series 1 and single-girl collections by name.

- ✓ 5.2.30Optional for NPG holders: melt a girl into her element cards and avatar badge.

- ✓ 5.2.37Keep them in bWalletX: restore your RelayX wallet and your RelayX NFTs show in the wallet’s NFTs tab under Run, kept as they are.

- ✓ 5.2.37BSV left on old RelayX addresses moved into your account in one tap.

- ✓ 5.2.32NFTs that were listed for sale on RelayX when it closed are found too, and one tap [cancels the listing](https://bwalletx.com/releases#v5.2.32) back to your own address.

- ◻ ComingOther Run collections shown with their pictures, not only their names.

## For developers

How RelayX NFTs are traced and identified, including the encrypted pictures: [Identifying RelayX NFTs](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/relayx-recovery/). How an NPG is built from her element cards: [Stack recipes](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/stack-recipes/).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# RelayX on b

RelayX has closed, but what you held there is still on chain, under the keys in your RelayX 12 words. bWalletX reads the chain for those keys and gives it back to you.

## What you can do

### Find your NFTs

Wallet › Bring in old assets › Recover RelayX collections. Enter your 12 words and tap Find my NFTs. Your NFTs appear as a gallery, grouped by collection. Finding is read-only: nothing moves.

### Keep them in bWalletX

Add account › Restore › RelayX. A Your RelayX collection card appears at the top of that account; one tap finds your NFTs again, and they sit in the NFTs tab under Run.

### Move leftover BSV

If your old RelayX addresses still hold BSV, one tap moves it into your account. RelayX NFTs are recognised first and never spent as coins.

### Cancel old listings

NFTs still listed for sale on RelayX when it closed are found too. The cancel is built and signed on your phone and shown before you allow it; one tap brings the NFT back to your own address.

### Read the old RelayX club posts

Feed › RelayX. The posts people wrote in RelayX clubs are on chain, so you can read them again, reply, like and lock behind them. RelayX itself is gone, so there is no “open original” link.

The full walk-through, with screenshots: [Recover RelayX collections](https://bwalletx.com/recover-relayx).

## Status

What works in bWalletX today, and what doesn’t yet.

- ✓ LiveFind RelayX NFTs from your 12 words, read-only

- ✓ LiveRestore a RelayX wallet and keep its NFTs in the NFTs tab (Run)

- ✓ LiveMove BSV left on old RelayX addresses in one tap

- ✓ LiveCancel a listing still open on RelayX, back to your address

- ✓ LiveOptional for Ninja Punk Girls holders: melt into element cards

- ✓ LiveRelayX club posts in the Feed, under the RelayX chip

- ○ Not yetOther Run collections shown with their pictures, not only names

- ○ Not yetTrading Run NFTs as Run NFTs in bWalletX

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get?from=relayx-on-b)

Your keys stay with you: bWalletX is self-custody. RelayX is a separate service; bWalletX is not affiliated with it. Logos belong to their owners. [More apps on b](https://bwalletx.com/on-b).

## 5.2.45 2026-10-29

- Paying a site from the wallet, such as TERRORNODE, now gives a plain reason when something goes wrong, and coin lookups keep working when a service is slow.
- Every failed BSV send now tells you why, and a message that did not arrive is sent again once.
- Your names sit in one tidy row each with a … menu, and Unlink and Remove explain what they do before you confirm.
- Turn your phone sideways for a landscape layout: a dock on the left and a two-column wallet home.
- Look-alike and brand names are flagged, and site sign-in asks in one clear sentence.
- The iPhone App Store build of this version is coming soon. Android, Chrome and web have it now.

## 5.2.44 2026-10-26

- Minting is private by default: your pictures and posts are minted encrypted, only you can see them, and “Make public now” is one tap away. Imports from X mint privately too.
- Feed now pulls in CoinGeek, Hodlocker and RelayX, with an All / sort / Favourites / Leaderboard row and a tidy grid of sources.
- The red DON’T PANIC! button on Home is now a calm green REFRESH WALLET.
- TERRORNODE has a Home tile: earn its coin by playing, and the room and shop open the game.
- Posting to bChatX from the wallet works again, and Make main carries on when bChatX already has that name as your handle.
- The iPhone App Store build of this version is coming soon. Android, Chrome and web have it now.

## 5.2.42 2026-10-25

- Talk to b any time: b answers in chat, and a one-time note explains that our team reads these chats so we can fix things fast.
- Exchange has a Memepool tab: see the coins on TX Blaster’s Memepool and buy or sell them from the wallet, up to 1 BSV a trade. New TokenBlaster coins each get a room and a store.
- The Store has a TokenBlaster shop with two $1 theme packs, and game rooms now dress themselves in the game’s own colours.
- A name you receive as an NFT explains itself and has an “Add to my Names” button.
- bApps now show two to a row on colour tiles, bVideoX plays full screen, and the main wallet card shows $b as its unit.
- Fewer approval prompts in everyday use, and a connected site’s theme shows correctly even if it was approved before.

## 5.2.41 2026-10-25

- Every approval and payment sheet now shows the amount in dollars first, with sats small underneath.
- After you disconnect a site, or a day away from it, the site’s next request asks “Reconnect to <site>?”. It never interrupts you in the middle of a session.
- Chrome extension: a connected game opens to its chat room with a short balance card, and a connected site’s theme now covers the whole wallet view.
- The account strip, account switcher and account chip show your full paymail, and Create lets you link your X account back and offers your X handle as your $name.
- Pausing spending now also stops pot standing orders and subscription charges, and restoring from a backup refuses if it would leave out accounts the backup doesn’t hold.
- More security fixes from our b-Aware reporters: each phone pairing’s permissions stay bound to that pairing, sign-in sheets never store a monthly allowance, and paymail payments are checked against the payee’s key before you sign.

## 5.2.40 2026-10-23

- A new bApps screen in tiers: our own b…X apps first, then commercial apps (NPG, VexVoid, Zero Dice), an 18+ group behind a check (never in the App Store or Play editions), and community apps that meet the bApp standard (a token, a bChatX room, a wallet theme and in-wallet payments). Others fold away under “Not yet bApp-ready”. In the Chrome extension a bApp opens in its own full tab.
- Every token you mint or launch now gets a launch curve: 1 billion tokens, the first one costs 1¢, and you choose how far the price climbs: Standard (to 19¢), Big (to $1.99) or Huge (to $19.99). The first 1% is a fair-launch early tier, $10 at most per person. The curve is written on chain when you mint, can’t be changed, and has a fingerprint anyone can check. You can choose to burn unsold tokens after 6 or 12 months, or never.
- Token market: list tokens for sale from the token row, straight after you mint, or from the token page, priced in dollars with the curve price shown. Buy is one tap, and the wallet checks the listing is still there first; if it’s gone, you’re offered the next one.
- A page for every token: its launch curve chart, price against the 1¢ start, holder count and top holders, and a link to its room. Tokens held in escrow, claim pools or quarantine can’t be listed.
- Chrome extension: a site you connect to can show the wallet in its own theme while its tab is open. Only themes built into the wallet are used, and your own theme comes back when you leave. Nothing is saved to your account.
- Wallets made with a passkey: Show my 12 words now has Use my passkey, and Chrome, Edge and Android offer to save the wallet’s password in your password manager as a second way back in. Coming to rooms: commissions paid in tokens, held in escrow until the work is accepted. Swap: unchanged in the downloads, extension and web; the App Store edition leaves swap out.
- Greeting cards and AI pictures in Mint, with a new card-making screen that shows your card as it’s made. In the bWalletX editions only, not the App Store or Google Play ones.
- A site you connect to now shows its own colours and logo on the approval sheets, with the wallet’s strip showing the true site address.
- If coins were spent from another device, sending now clears them and tries once more instead of failing.
- bChatX rooms work again: the wallet falls back to chat.bwalletx.com while bchatx.com is on hold.
- Safer by default: recovery phrases are caught in reports and Ask b before they leave your device, pausing or cancelling a subscription always sticks, wiping the wallet now removes phone pairings too, and more security fixes from our b-Aware reporters.

## 5.2.39 2026-10-22

- Fixes a crash (“reading ‘identityAddress’”) when opening the wallet after signing out and back in.
- Making a backup during sign-up no longer leaves your balance stuck on “Still syncing”, and encrypted backups save every time, not just the first.
- Chrome extension: Continue with a passkey opens web.bwalletx.com straight away. Use your passkey there and type the six digits it shows into the extension. New here? “No passkey wallet yet? Create a new one” makes one on the same page.

- Lock BSV-21 tokens until a date and find the locks again from your recovery phrase; links such as web.bwalletx.com/restore and /lock open again on the web and Desktop; and name prices are now $10, $50, $100 or $500 depending on length.

The App Store and Play editions don’t include it yet.

# Restore. Bring your coins home.

Have an old BSV wallet? Its 12 words still work. bWalletX can open it as an account, or move what’s in it into one of yours.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## Restore or sweep?

Restore opens the old wallet as an account in bWalletX. The keys are the same, so nothing moves on chain. Use it when bWalletX knows the wallet’s layout.

Sweep moves the coins and tokens out of the old wallet into an account you already have, in new transactions. Use it for wallets that spread coins across many addresses, or when you just want everything in one place. Sweeping pays a small network fee.

## Wallets you can bring in

WalletHowYou needDerivation pathWhat comes across

`m/44'/236'/0'/0/0` swept onceEverything on those keys, plus your RelayX NFTs (Run) via [Your RelayX collection](#relayx).

LiveRestore as an account12 words`m/0/0` paymentEverything on that key.

LiveNew wallet, then sweep12 words, or SimplyCash’s recovery string (words:path:passphrase)`m/44'/145'/0'`, receive and change chains, gap limit 20. Early SimplyCash wallets’ older derivation is tried too.BSV, ordinals, BSV-21 tokens. SimplyCash spreads coins over many addresses, so it can’t be one account; it is swept instead.

## RelayX wallets

RelayX has closed, but everything your RelayX words hold is still on chain. bWalletX brings it back in two ways:

- Restore it as an account. On the welcome screen (or Add account), choose Restore, pick RelayX and enter your 12 words. Your BSV and 1Sat ordinals come across straight away.

- Your RelayX NFTs. RelayX NFTs are Run tokens, which spread across many addresses. On the restored account a blue Your RelayX collection card appears at the top: tap it once and bWalletX finds them all. They then show in the NFTs tab under Run, kept exactly as they are.

- BSV on older RelayX addresses. If the search finds coins outside the account’s main address, tap Move it into this account.

- Just want to look first? [Recover RelayX collections](https://bwalletx.com/recover-relayx) finds and shows your NFTs from your words without adding an account. Nothing moves.

## What stays behind, and why

- Names, BSV-20 tokens and locked coins are not swept. The sweep screen tells you how many it found. Restore the wallet as an account instead to keep them.

- Money Button tokens (SFP). Each one can only be spent with a signature from Money Button’s token server, which shut down with Money Button in 2022. Nobody can move or burn them alone. bWalletX keeps them out of the BSV sweep so they are not destroyed by accident, and lists them for you.

- HandCash, Centbee, ElectrumSV and others aren’t listed by name. If you have their 12 or 24 words, try a sweep: bWalletX tries every path above. If it finds nothing, tell us.

## How to restore

- On the welcome screen, choose to restore a wallet.

- Pick the wallet: bWalletX (also Yours and Panda), RelayX, Twetch, SimplyCash (phone app), Restore with private key, Restore from master backup, or Other.

- Type your words (or key) and set a password. For Other, turn on Use custom derivations to enter your own paths.

## How to sweep

- Open Settings › Account data › Sweep into this account.

- Paste the recovery phrase, private key (WIF) or xprv. Add the passphrase only if the old wallet had one, and a custom path if you know it.

- bWalletX scans every known layout and shows what it found. Check it, then sweep. You get a link to each transaction.

## Stay safe

- Never type your words into a website, a chat or a form. Only into the wallet app itself.

- bWalletX derives every key on your device. Your words are never sent anywhere and are not stored after a sweep.

- A sweep moves funds in new transactions. Once they’re in, the old words no longer hold anything you swept.

## Don’t see your wallet?

[Tell us](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=Restore%20from%20another%20wallet) which one, and we’ll look at adding it.

The story behind this page: [022 Bring your coins home](https://bwalletx.com/blog/022-bring-your-coins-home).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Live

# No seed phrase to manage. Just your face.

Start a wallet with a passkey: Face ID, Touch ID or your device PIN. Nothing to write down on day one. Full details and where it works: [Seedless sign-in](https://bwalletx.com/seedless-signin).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[See the status →](#status)

## How it works

### 1. Continue with a passkey

Tap Continue with a passkey on the welcome screen. No password to invent, no words to copy down.

### 2. What locks it

A passkey made on your device locks the wallet. You unlock with your face, your finger or your PIN.

### 3. Your 12 words, kept safe

Your wallet still has its 12 words underneath. An encrypted copy is saved that only your passkey can open. You can show the words any time.

You can link X, Google, GitHub, LinkedIn or HandCash later, under Link your accounts. They only show who you are. They never touch your keys.

## Same wallet on phone and computer

Passkeys sync with your Apple or Google account, so the same passkey opens the same wallet on your other devices. On a computer, you can also scan a code with your phone to open it.

## The classic way stays

A password and 12 words are still there, side by side. Pick whichever suits you. Restoring with your 12 words or a backup file works exactly as it does today.

## We never hold your keys

Your keys are made on your device. The encrypted copy of your 12 words can only be opened by your passkey, and the passkey never leaves your device or your Apple or Google account. We can’t open your wallet, and we can’t move your money. If we disappeared, your 12 words would still restore your wallet in any compatible app.

## Status, 23 Oct 2026

- LiveCreate a wallet with a passkey (Face ID, Touch ID or device PIN). No password to invent.

- LiveOpen your wallet with your passkey.

- LiveEncrypted copy of your 12 words that only your passkey can open.

- LiveRestore on a new device with the same passkey.

- LiveScan-to-open on a computer with your phone.

- LiveWhere: the web, the Chrome extension and the Android download. iPhone is in the private build.

- ◻ ComingIn the phone apps (bWallet on the App Store and Google Play).

Already true today, and unchanged by this: password and 12 words, “Show recovery phrase” in Settings, restore from 12 words or a backup file.

## Questions

### What if I lose my phone?

Your passkey lives in your Apple or Google account, not only on the phone. Sign in on a new phone, use the same passkey, and your wallet comes back. Your 12 words still work too. For larger amounts we’ll suggest you write them down as well.

### Can bWalletX open my wallet?

No. Only your passkey can open the encrypted copy of your words, and we never see your keys.

### Do my old wallets still work?

Yes, unchanged. Your password, your 12 words and your backups keep working exactly as before.

Related: [Seedless sign-in](https://bwalletx.com/seedless-signin) · [Restore](https://bwalletx.com/restore) · [Identity](https://bwalletx.com/identity) · [Handles](https://bwalletx.com/handles) · [bTrust](https://bwalletx.com/btrust)

SEEDLESS SIGN-IN

Passkey

# Open your wallet with your face or fingerprint

Create a bWalletX wallet with a passkey. Your phone or computer’s own lock (Face ID, fingerprint or PIN) opens it. There is no password to invent and no 12-word phrase to write down before you start. Your 12 words are sealed with the passkey and saved as a locked recovery file you keep.

[Try it on the web](https://web.bwalletx.com)
[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## This is the sign-in screen

On a phone
In a browser, with the QR code to open your phone wallet here

## How it works

### 1. Tap Continue with a passkey

You are not asked to make a password or to copy down words.

### 2. Confirm with your device lock

Your phone or computer asks for Face ID, a fingerprint or its PIN. That is your device checking it is you. bWalletX never sees it.

### 3. Keep your recovery file

Your 12 words are sealed with your passkey and saved as a file only that passkey opens. A locked copy is also kept for you, so the same passkey can bring the wallet back on a new device.

## Where it works today

LIVE
### Web

web.bwalletx.com, in Chrome, Safari and Android browsers.

LIVE
### Chrome extension

Sign in through web.bwalletx.com with your passkey; the wallet comes back into the extension.

LIVE
### Android download

The direct download from bwalletx.com.

PRIVATE
### iPhone

In the private build for now.

COMING
### App Store and Google Play

Not in the store editions yet.

## Good to know

### Passkeys stay in your Apple or Google account

A passkey saved to iCloud cannot open a wallet on an Android phone, and the other way round. On a different kind of device, use your recovery file or your 12 words, or add a passkey there.

### We never hold your keys

Your 12 words are locked with your passkey before they leave your device. What we store is the locked copy, which only your passkey can open.

### You can still use a password and 12 words

It is the other button on the sign-in screen.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)
