# Sign in with HandCash. Bring your name with you.

Already have a HandCash account? You can use it to sign in to bChatX. The best way in is with bWalletX; HandCash works too. You keep your name and your friends, and you get your own bWalletX address.

[Open bChatX](https://chat.bwalletx.com)[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## How it works

- Tap More waysOn bchatx.com, under the gold bWalletX button.

- Approve in HandCashHandCash confirms it’s really you. We use your verified account, never a name you type.

- You’re inYour account is linked to that HandCash id, and you get first claim on the same name at bwalletx.com.

## What you get

- First claim on your name. If you’re $alice on HandCash, alice@bwalletx.com is held for you first.

- A new bWalletX address. It’s your own wallet, not a forward to HandCash. Payments to name@bwalletx.com land in bWalletX.

- Your HandCash friends. Bring them into your bWalletX address book, so the people you already know are there from day one.

## Keep it safe

- Your HandCash login stays on your phone. The token is kept in the phone’s secure storage.

- It expires. When it does, you simply sign in with HandCash again.

- We never see your HandCash password. HandCash checks who you are; we only get the verified id.

## Where this stands

- In testingSign in with HandCash on bchatx.com, under “More ways” below the gold bWalletX button. Uses your verified HandCash account, not a typed name. Built; not yet tried end to end.

- In testingHandCash friends into your bWalletX address book: in the bWalletX phone apps since 5.2.26; not yet tried end to end.

- In testingSign in with HandCash inside the bWalletX app: phone apps only (Android download and iPhone beta), Settings › Identity › Link your accounts › HandCash, since 5.2.26. Not in the web wallet or the Chrome extension. Not yet tried end to end.

- ComingThe store edition (bWallet on the App Store and Google Play): planned, once Sign in with Apple is added.

Related: [Invites](https://bwalletx.com/invite) · [057 Sign in with HandCash and invites](https://bwalletx.com/blog/057-handcash-and-invites) · [Sign in with X](https://bwalletx.com/x) · [Handles](https://bwalletx.com/handles) · [Friends](https://bwalletx.com/friends)

SMS In build

# Bitcoin by text.

Send money to any phone number. They tap a link to claim it. If they don’t, it comes back to you.

This is in build and not live yet. The list at the bottom shows where it stands.

[How it works](#how)[What’s live](#status)

Text message

Sam sent you £5 with bWalletX. Tap to claim: bwalletx.com/c/…

Claimed, thanks!

01 / 04  How it works

## Phone number in, money out.

Step 1

### Verify your number

- We text you a code
- Your number links to your wallet as a private fingerprint, not stored in plain text

Step 2

### Send by text

- Pick any phone number and an amount
- They get a text with a claim link

Step 3

### They claim, or it comes back

- Tap the link and claim into a wallet
- Unclaimed funds return to you
- We never hold the money

02 / 04  For businesses

## Customers can text your agent.

A [business agent](https://bwalletx.com/business-agents) can answer by text too: customers ask questions and pay without installing anything first.

03 / 04  Privacy

## Your number stays yours.

- 01Your number is stored as a private fingerprint, never shown to other users.

- 02We only text people you choose to send to.

- 03Reply STOP to any of our texts to opt out.

- 04You can unlink your number from the wallet at any time.

04 / 04  What’s live

## Where things stand.

- ComingVerify your phone number (in build)

- ComingSend by text with a claim link

- ComingUnclaimed funds return to you

- ComingText a business’s agent

- ComingSTOP to opt out

# Your shop.
Inside everyone’s wallet.

A bWalletX store is a shop front that lives inside the wallet itself. Your banner, your logo, your things for sale, one tap away for everyone who opens the Store. People pay you in BSV with one approval, and what they buy is theirs to keep.

[Start your store](#start)
[See what a store looks like](#look)

Free to start. Shops open after b has had a look. [What’s live today](#status)

Selling themes, art or files? [bStoreX](https://bstorex.com) is the Store’s home on the web. Keeping files and recordings? That’s [bDriveX](https://bdrivex.com). →

‹ Store

Ninja Punk GirlsThemes and art from the NPG universe

ThemesNFTsGamesArt

Card themeFrom your NFT

NPG Racer carGame item

Mock-up of a shop in the Store. Only the NPG theme is on sale today.

## What a bWalletX store is

Think of the Store as a small shopping centre inside the wallet. Every shop has its own front. Every item also sits in a department, so people can browse by shop (“Ninja Punk Girls”) or by kind of thing (“Themes”).

It’s where your buyers already are.
No new app to download and no account to make. People who use bWalletX open Exchange › Store and your shop is there, next to the others.

Paying takes one tap.
A buyer sees one sheet with the price and taps Allow. No card numbers and no checkout form. The money is BSV, straight from their wallet.

What they buy stays with them.
A theme stays theirs to switch on whenever they like. An NFT sits in their wallet’s NFTs tab. Each sale also comes with a signed receipt.

## What a store looks like

Every shop is built the same way, so buyers always know where to look. You fill in five things and the Store does the rest.

‹ Store

1

2
Ninja Punk GirlsThemes and art from the NPG universe
3

ThemesNFTsGames4

NPG theme$1

NPG cardNFT5

- Banner. The wide picture across the top, 1500 × 500. Your art, your scene, your mood.

- Logo. A square, 512 × 512. It also shows on your shop’s tile in the Store and on your buyers’ receipts.

- Shop name and a line about you. Up to 40 characters for the name, a sentence or two for the rest.

- Departments. Themes, NFTs, game items, art, music and more. Your items show under your shop and in the matching department.

- Items. Each one has a picture, a title, a short description and a price in dollars. Buyers pay the same value in BSV.

Your shop also gets its own web address, `bwalletx.com/shop/your-name`. You pick the name when you start.

### In the Store, your shop sits with the others

## Who it’s for

- NFT collections. You already have the art and the fans. Give them somewhere to buy, and something to do with what they own.

- Artists and illustrators. Sell your pictures, and themes made from them, so fans carry your work on their phone.

- Musicians and film makers. Tracks, albums, clips, and a look for the wallet to match.

- Game makers. Sell the cars, skins and extras for your game where your players keep their money.

- Brands and communities. One place for your members to pick up the official look and the good stuff.

## What you can sell

◻ Coming

### Your NFTs

List the NFTs in your wallet and sell them from your shop. That includes old RelayX (Run) NFTs: bWalletX can already find them from your 12 words and keep them in your wallet under NFTs › Run. Selling them from a shop is next.

◻ Coming

### Themes made from your NFTs

Your art becomes a theme: the app’s colours and a card with your picture on it. Your customers switch it on and their whole wallet wears your look. It’s the simplest way for fans to carry what they love on the phone they use every day.

◻ Coming

### Your own racing game

[bRacer](https://bwalletx.com/games) is our anti-gravity racer. A collection can have its own branded version made from it, the way we’re making NPG Racer for Ninja Punk Girls, or enter its own team in bRacer. Your shop then sells the race cars, in your colours, to the people who play.

✓ Live

### Themes, today

The Store already sells themes: NPG, NPGX and VexVoid, $1 each, paid in BSV with one approval. Every shop will use that same checkout.

The other departments open later: subscriptions, stickers and emoji, art and editions, music and video, courses and books, rooms and memberships, and services.

Worked example

## The Ninja Punk Girls store

Ninja Punk Girls is our own collection, so its store is being built first, one step at a time. Any collection’s pieces fit together the same way.

- 1

## How the money works

Buyertaps Allow on one sheet

80% to youpaid to your shop’s own bWalletX

20% to the Storekeeps the Store running

- You set prices in dollars. The buyer pays the same value in BSV at the rate on the day.

- Your share goes to the wallet your shop belongs to: the one you signed in with. We don’t hold it for you.

- Every buyer gets a signed receipt with your shop’s logo on it.

- Starting a shop is free, with no monthly fee.

Payouts to sellers start when the first outside shops open. Today the Store sells only our own shops’ themes.

## Questions

What does it cost to start?
Nothing. When you sell something, 80% goes to you and 20% to the Store.
Do I need a bWalletX?
Yes. Your shop belongs to your wallet, and that’s where your money arrives. [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) for the web, Chrome, Android or iPhone. It’s free.
Who can see my draft?
Only you, signed in with the same wallet. Nobody else sees it until your shop opens.
Why does b review shops?
So buyers can trust what they find: real makers, no fakes, nothing pretending to be someone it isn’t.
Is a theme mine for good?
Yes. Pay once and it’s yours to keep. Switch between it and the free themes whenever you like.
Why can’t I see the Store in bWallet?
The Store is in bWalletX: web, Chrome extension, Android and iPhone. It isn’t in the App Store and Google Play edition, bWallet.

# Pay as you listen. Stop any time.

Some things are worth a little, for as long as they last. In bWalletX you pay by the second or the minute for a Space, a call or a song. You set a limit once. The money goes straight to the people you hear.

## How it works

### See the price

The rate is shown before you start: per second, per minute or per hour.

### Set your limit

Approve once, with the most you’ll spend. No popup for each payment.

### Stop when you like

Leave, hang up or tap Stop. Payments end there.

## Paid Spaces

A host can ask listeners to pay for a live Space. They set the price per second, minute or hour, in BSV (priced in dollars) or in a token.

- The money is split between the people on stage, or paid to the token’s issuer, as the host chooses.

- The first minute is usually free, so you can hear it first.

- You choose “Most I’ll spend this session”. Or take just the free minute.

- Your wallet pays each minute directly to the speakers. bChatX takes nothing.

- It stops at your limit, or when you leave.

See [bSpaces](https://bwalletx.com/bspaces).

## Paid calls

With bPhone, people can charge to take a call: a coach, a tutor, an adviser. They set a rate per second, minute, hour or per call, in BSV, MNEE or a token.

- You see the rate and your most you’ll spend before the call rings.

- You pay as you talk, wallet to wallet. In BSV, a small payment goes every 10 seconds.

- Hang up and the payments stop.

See [bPhone](https://bwalletx.com/bphone).

## Music by the second

On VexVoid’s album Echoes in the Abyss, the headline track is free. Pay-to-play tracks cost 1 sat a second to the artist, plus the network fee.

- One approval sets a budget. After that, every second is its own small payment, with no popups.

- You see what’s gone to the artist, the network fees and the budget left.

- Tap Stop, leave, or hide the page for a minute, and what’s left comes back to your wallet.

See [Artists](https://bwalletx.com/artists).

## Your money, your limit

You never pay more than the limit you set.

Each payment is made out to the speakers, the person you’re calling, or the artist.

## Where to find it

- bWalletX: on the web at [web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com), [Desktop](https://web.bwalletx.com), the [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension) and the [Android download](https://bwalletx.com/android).

- Not in bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition. Free Spaces and free calls are there.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Restore

# Bring your SimplyCash coins home.

Had a SimplyCash wallet? bWalletX can find what’s in it from your recovery phrase and sweep it into your own bWalletX account. A few taps, on your own phone.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[How it works](#steps)

## Four steps

- 1

### Open the sweep screen

In bWalletX go to Settings › Account data › Sweep into this account. Setting up a new wallet? Restore › SimplyCash starts the same thing.

- 2

### Paste your SimplyCash backup

Your 12-word recovery phrase, or SimplyCash’s full recovery string (words, path and passphrase joined by colons). A private key (WIF) or an xprv works too. Add a passphrase if you set one.

- 3

### Let it look

bWalletX walks SimplyCash’s path `m/44'/145'/0'` and the other common Bitcoin SV layouts, receive and change addresses, until 20 in a row are unused. It also tries the older derivation early SimplyCash wallets used, automatically. It shows the coins, NFTs and tokens it finds, in dollars.

- 4

### Sweep it home

Tick what to bring over and tap sweep. Your coins move into your bWalletX account in a few transactions (BSV, NFTs, then each token), paying the normal small network fee. The old phrase isn’t kept: from then on, your coins are protected by your bWalletX words.

## Where’s my SimplyCash phrase?

Look for the backup you made when you set up SimplyCash: your 12-word recovery phrase or recovery string from your SimplyCash backup. People often wrote it on paper, saved it in a password manager or kept a screenshot. If you still have the SimplyCash app, its backup or settings area may show it again.

## Stay safe

- Never share your phrase. Not with b, not in any chat, not with support. We will never ask for it.

- Type it only into the sweep screen, on your own device. The phrase stays on your phone and is cleared when you leave the screen; only public addresses are looked up online to find your coins.

- Unsure? Test first. For larger amounts (over about £500) bWalletX offers to sweep a small test amount first. Check it arrived, then scan again to sweep the rest.

## Questions

It says nothing was found.
Check every word, and add your passphrase if your SimplyCash wallet had one (or paste the full recovery string, which carries it). The older SimplyCash derivation is tried automatically. You can also try a custom path under Advanced, or ask b in the app.

Does bWalletX keep my SimplyCash phrase?
No. It is held in memory only for the scan and the sweep, never stored and never sent to our servers.

Can I sweep other wallets?
Yes. The same screen takes recovery phrases from other Bitcoin SV wallets, private keys (WIF) and xprvs.

Is it in the App Store and Play versions?
Yes. Sweep from another wallet is in every bWalletX and bWallet build.

## What works today

- LiveSimplyCash 12-word phrase sweep (path m/44'/145'/0').

- LiveSimplyCash recovery string (words:path:passphrase).

- LiveOlder SimplyCash derivation, tried automatically.

- LiveCoins, NFTs and tokens found and swept.

- LiveOther BSV wallets: BIP44 phrases (coin types 236 and 0), private keys (WIF), xprvs and custom paths.

- LiveTest sweep for amounts over about £500.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Restore a bWalletX backup](https://bwalletx.com/restore)

SimplyCash is named only to describe compatibility; bWalletX isn’t affiliated with it. bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Terms of Service

bWalletX (Beta) · Effective 28 October 2026

Please read these terms before using bWalletX. The short version: it's your wallet and your 12 words. We can't
see them, recover them or move your money. Keep your words safe, start with small amounts while we're in beta,
and remember that coin prices go up and down.

## 1. Who we are

bWalletX is published by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales (company number
16735102), registered office Flat 6, 315 Barking Road, London, E13 8EE ("we", "us"). These terms cover bWalletX (the web
wallet at `web.bwalletx.com`, the Chrome extension and the phone apps), bWallet (the edition on the App
Store and Google Play), and this website, together "bWalletX".

By using bWalletX you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use it. Our
[Privacy Policy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy) explains what data we handle and why.

## 2. Who can use it

You must be at least 18, or the age of majority where you live if that is higher, and able to make a binding
contract. You must not use bWalletX if you are subject to sanctions, or where using a Bitcoin wallet, swapping
coins or any feature you use is against the law where you are. You are responsible for following the laws that
apply to you, including on tax.

## 3. Self-custody: your keys, your responsibility

bWalletX is non-custodial. Your wallet is created on your device from a recovery phrase (your 12 words). Your
private keys and 12 words stay on your device; we never receive or hold them, and we can't move, freeze or
reverse your coins, tokens or NFTs.

-
Lost words can't be recovered. If you lose your 12 words and your device, or forget your password
without your 12 words, we cannot get your wallet back for you. Nobody can.

-
Never share your 12 words. Anyone who has them controls your money. We will never ask for them.

-
Transactions are final. Payments on the blockchain can't be cancelled or reversed once sent. Check the
address, handle and amount before you approve.

-
Your device is your vault. You are responsible for keeping your device, password and backups secure.

## 4. What bWalletX does

bWalletX lets you hold and send Bitcoin SV (BSV), tokens and 1Sat Ordinal NFTs; use a paymail handle such as
`name@bwalletx.com`; connect to apps through the open BRC-100 wallet interface; chat; buy digital
items in the Store; send and receive bMail (letters that can carry a paid stamp or payment); join and host live
audio Spaces; list and buy tokens and NFTs wallet to wallet; time-lock coins; launch your own token; run agent
accounts with their own spending limits; ask our AI assistant, b; and swap other coins into BSV through a
third-party partner. bWalletX also runs as a desktop app and in your browser. Related sites such as bchatx.com,
bmailx.com, bcalx.com, bradiox.com, bjobsx.com, bnewsx.com, bstorex.com and bdrivex.com are part of bWalletX and covered by these terms.
bWalletX is software. We are not a bank, an exchange, a broker or a payment service, and we don't hold money for
you.

## 5. Handles and names

A handle (for example `$name`, which is `name@bwalletx.com` and also
`name@bmailx.com`) lets people pay you. You must
not claim a handle that impersonates someone else, infringes a trademark or is offensive. We may refuse, reserve,
suspend or reassign a handle that breaks these terms or that a rights holder can show belongs to them. Because
the paymail service is run by us, a handle depends on that service: it isn't the same as owning your keys, and
your money stays in your wallet whatever happens to a handle.

Reserved handles. Some handles are kept for The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd and can't be claimed:
every one- and two-character handle (including the numbers `0` to `99`), which we keep
for The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd; the names of our products and of b, our AI assistant; and the names of
identity providers and major platforms (for example `gmail`, `github` or
`linkedin`). Using any handle, display name, bot name or letter to pose as bCorp, a member of our
staff, b or our support team is impersonation under these terms, and we may suspend or reassign that handle.
A short name never means someone works for us: bCorp and its staff are identified only by the Verified · The Bitcoin Corporation badge. We will never ask for your 12 words or your password, in bMail or anywhere else. Handles registered before 28
October 2026 that are now reserved stay with their holders unless they are used to impersonate.

## 6. No financial advice

Nothing in bWalletX, on this website or from b (our AI assistant) is financial, investment, legal or tax advice,
or a recommendation to buy, sell or hold anything. Prices, rates and balances shown are for information and may
be delayed or wrong. Cryptoassets are high risk: their value can fall to zero, and they are not protected by
the Financial Services Compensation Scheme or the Financial Ombudsman Service. Only use money you can afford to
lose.

b is an AI. It can make mistakes, and it can't approve or send a payment for you: you always approve
transactions yourself. Check anything important before you rely on it.

## 7. Third-party services

Some features are provided by other companies, under their own terms and privacy policies, which you accept
with them when you use those features. We don't control them and aren't responsible for them.

-
Swaps (ChangeNOW). Swaps into BSV inside bWalletX are run by ChangeNOW, not by us. ChangeNOW is the
exchange: it quotes the rate, receives your deposit, sends the BSV to your wallet and carries out its own
AML/KYC checks. It may pause a swap, ask you for information, or refund or decline it. Rates float, and the
amount shown is an estimate until your deposit arrives. Questions about a swap's status, refunds or checks are
handled by ChangeNOW. See ChangeNOW's
[terms of use](https://changenow.io/terms-of-use),
[AML/KYC policy](https://changenow.io/aml-kyc-policy) and
[privacy policy](https://changenow.io/privacy-policy). We will help you
find a swap's details where we can.

-
Blockchain and wallet services such as 1Sat indexers and wallet storage, WhatsOnChain and price feeds.

- Identity checks through our identity service and Veriff, if you choose to verify.

- AI providers (for example Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter) when you use b.

-
Apps and websites you open from bWalletX, including bApps and anything you connect your wallet to. Only
approve requests you understand.

We may be paid a share of fees by partners such as ChangeNOW. Where that applies, it is included in the rate you see.

## 8. Fees

bWalletX is free to download and use. When you send a transaction you pay the BSV network fee, shown before you
approve. Swaps include the partner's fees, and may include a fee for us, within the estimate shown. Paid
features, such as Store items or pay-per-message use of b, show their price before you pay. We may change
prices for the future; a change never affects something you have already paid for.

## 9. Store purchases and refunds

The Store sells digital items, such as themes, paid in BSV from your wallet. The price is shown before you
approve the payment. Each item is a licence to use it in bWalletX for your own, non-commercial use; it doesn't
give you any ownership of the design or our intellectual property unless the item's page says otherwise (for
example an NFT sent to your wallet, which you own and can transfer).

Because items are digital and delivered straight away, when you buy you ask us to deliver immediately and
accept that you lose the usual 14-day right to cancel once delivery starts. This doesn't affect your legal
rights: if an item is faulty, not as described or not delivered, contact us and we will repair or replace it or
give you a refund in BSV to your wallet. Items bought through the App Store or Google Play are handled under
Apple's or Google's refund rules.

## 9A. Payments, locks, tokens and agents

- bMail stamps and payments. A stamp or payment on a letter is a payment to the person you write to.
Once sent it is theirs; we can't refund it. Setting a price to reach you is your choice; letters below it go to
your Requests.

- Paid Spaces. If a host charges to listen or to book a slot, you pay the people on stage or the room
owner directly, as shown before you approve. We don't hold or refund these payments.

- Locks. Coins you time-lock can't be spent until the lock ends, by you or anyone else, including us.
You can always recover them from your 12 words once the lock ends.

- Tokens and the Exchange. Tokens and NFTs are listed and bought wallet to wallet; we don't hold them
or set their prices. If you launch a token you are its issuer: you are responsible for what you say about it,
and you must not offer it as an investment or promise returns. A token's indexing deposit is paid to the
indexer and can't be refunded.

- Agent accounts. An agent account spends only from its own wallet, within the limits you set, and you
can stop it at any time. You are responsible for what your agents do with the money you give them.

- Agreements. Agreements you send, sign and seal in bMail are between the people who sign them. We
provide the tools, not legal advice, and we aren't a party to them.

## 10. Acceptable use

You must not use bWalletX to:

- break the law, including money laundering, terrorist financing, fraud or evading sanctions;

- scam, impersonate, harass, threaten or exploit anyone, or share content that sexually exploits children;

- infringe anyone's copyright, trademark or other rights;

- send spam, malware or phishing links, or attack, overload or probe our services without permission;

- get around limits, payments or safety filters, or access accounts or data that aren't yours.

If you break these rules we may remove content, suspend your handle, chat or other features run on our servers,
and report illegal activity to the authorities. We can't take your coins: those stay in your wallet.

## 12. Beta, availability and no warranty

bWalletX is in beta. It may have bugs, change, or be unavailable at times, and features may be added or removed.

## Where each version is

We ship small updates often, usually several a week. A new version reaches each place at a different speed, because Apple and Google check some of them first. Latest: 5.2.45 (22 Oct 2026), [what’s new](https://bwalletx.com/releases#v5.2.45).

- Web, Chrome extension, Android download (APK): the same day. Now on 5.2.45.

- Android, Google Play test: the same day. Now on 5.2.37.

- iPhone, TestFlight: about a day later, after Apple’s beta review. 5.2.37 is with Apple now; until it clears, TestFlight still offers an older build.

- App Store and Play Store: not out yet. bWallet’s first store release is being prepared; testers will hear first.

Every release is listed on [/releases](https://bwalletx.com/releases), newest first.

## The Android test link

Once your Google account is on the list, join here on your phone: [play.google.com/apps/internaltest/4701646815257978169](https://play.google.com/apps/internaltest/4701646815257978169), then install bWallet from Google Play. What to test and how to report is on [/testers/bwallet/android](https://bwalletx.com/testers/bwallet/android). The link does nothing for an account that isn’t on the list, so apply first.

## Testing bWalletX, the full edition?

No application needed: [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/testers/bwalletx/chrome-extension) · [web](https://bwalletx.com/testers/bwalletx/web) · [Desktop](https://bwalletx.com/testers/bwalletx/desktop). Each page says what to test and how to report.

## On iPhone?

The iPhone beta is open through TestFlight and has no application step: install TestFlight from the App Store, then open [testflight.apple.com/join/1TTnQNKm](https://testflight.apple.com/join/1TTnQNKm) on your iPhone. What to test and how to report is on [/testers/bwallet/iphone](https://bwalletx.com/testers/bwallet/iphone). The paid 14-day test below is Android only, because it is Google’s requirement.

## How it works

- Sign in with Google and apply. Use the Google account on your Android phone.

- I read every application and approve testers by hand. If you're in, I add your email to the Google Play test and you'll see your tester code here.

- Join the test on Google Play and install bWallet from there (not the APK from this site).

- Open bWallet, go to Settings › Testing and enter your tester code. The app checks in once a day when you open it.

- Open bWallet every day for 14 days. Use it like you normally would: send a little, receive, try the features.

## What you get

- 0.25 BSV after you first open the app installed from Google Play.

- 0.75 BSV once you've checked in on at least 12 of the 14 days.

- Paid to your own bWallet receive address. I pay each one by hand and you'll see the transaction id here.

## The rules

- One place per person: one Google account, one phone, one wallet. Duplicates get declined.

- Payment never depends on ratings or reviews. Please don't leave a review because of this; Google doesn't allow paid reviews. Report bugs and ideas in the app instead (Settings › Contact and reports).

- I approve applicants, and I can say no or remove a place if something looks wrong.

- 20 places. When they're gone, they're gone.

- What the app sends while you test is in the [privacy policy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy#testers): a random install id, your tester code, whether it came from Google Play, and the app version. Nothing about your keys or money.

Questions: [@bWalletX on X](https://x.com/bWalletX) · [Twetch](https://bwalletx.com/twetch).

## On what

DeviceAndroid phone or tablet

SystemAndroid 7.0 or later

ViaGoogle Play, internal test

EditionbWallet (Play Store)

iPhone testers: see [/testers/bwallet/iphone](https://bwalletx.com/testers/bwallet/iphone). For the full bWalletX on Android, install the [direct APK](https://bwalletx.com/android); it is a separate app and the two can live side by side.

## Join (two minutes)

- Make sure the Google account on your phone is the one you gave us on [/testers](https://bwalletx.com/testers). The test is limited to 100 accounts and only listed accounts can join.

- Open the link above on your phone, tap Become a tester, then Download it on Google Play.

- Updates arrive through Google Play like any app. Until Google reviews the app, the Play listing shows the package name, com.bitcoincorp.bwallet, instead of bWallet. That is normal for an internal test.

## What to test, in this order

-
First run.Create a wallet, write down the 12 words, set a device password. Then delete and restore it from the words on the same phone. Does everything come back?

-
Receive.Open Receive, copy the address or show the QR, and send yourself a few pence of BSV from another wallet. How long until it shows?

-
Send.Pay a $handle, a name@bwalletx.com and a plain address. Does the fee shown match what left the wallet?

-
Names.Search a name in Names. If it is free, get it. Give one to a friend. Did it take about a minute, and did they receive it?

-
Chat.Open a room, send a message, open a DM. Scroll both lists past the top: both should bounce.

-
Calls.Call another bWallet user. Try mute and speaker, and hanging up from both ends.

-
Lock and accounts.Lock and unlock the app. Add a second account, switch to it and back. Does the right balance show each time?

Anything that felt slow, stuck, unclear, or cost more than you expected. The best report says what you did, what you expected, what happened, and your phone model and Android version.

- Tell b about bugs and ideas any time, no key needed; add your own AI key in Settings › b agent and b will answer too.

- It is a beta: keep small amounts in it, and keep your 12 words safe. Your keys stay on your phone.

03 / 06  The route

## The route: from your wallet to your share register.

A branded wallet is where it starts. If your company has shareholders, the same wallet can one day show them what they hold. Here is the path, and where each step stands today.

- Live1. Your branded wallet. Your customers, members or shareholders use a wallet with your name on it (Branded edition, above). Each person keeps their own keys.

- Testing2. Your share register on [bSharesX](https://bsharesx.com). Keep your company’s register of members with bSharesX. The company keeps the register as the law asks, and its directors approve every entry; a token mirrors it on chain, and if the two ever differ, the register wins. Holders see their holding in their own wallet. Registers are in testing: the first register in testing is The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd, our own company. Setting up other companies’ registers is coming. [More on bShares](https://bwalletx.com/bshares)

- Early3. Optional: [bDojoX](https://bdojox.com). If you want to go that route, bDojoX is a programme for companies on chain, belt by belt, from its first token to a register kept on chain. Five belts, five stages: token launched, partnership shares locked, registered company, capital raised, public listing. The first two use tools that are live in bWalletX; the register is in testing; the later belts are coming or planned, and none of them is open yet.

Please read this. Shares are securities. We don’t issue or sell shares for you, raise money for you, give investment or legal advice, or get regulatory approval for you. You need your own legal advice before offering shares to anyone. bShares registers are in testing. Nothing on this page is an offer of securities.

[Talk to us](https://bwalletx.com/clients)[bSharesX](https://bsharesx.com)[bDojoX](https://bdojox.com)

# Tip the people who make things.

bWalletX has a Tip button wherever there’s someone to thank: artists, NFT creators, rooms, people in chat, friends and speakers in Spaces. All of it goes to them.

## How it works

### Tap Tip

Next to an artist, a track, a creator, a room, a name in chat, a friend or a speaker.

### Pick an amount

10p, 50p, £1 or £5 (or 10¢, 50¢, $1, $5), or your own. Add a note if you like.

### Allow once

One sheet, one Allow. bWalletX works out the BSV at today’s price and sends it.

## Where you’ll find it

- bMusic: the artist page, each track and the album player. See [Artists](https://bwalletx.com/artists).

- NFTs: the creator, when the NFT names one. See [NFTs](https://bwalletx.com/nfts).

- Chat: the room’s creator, and each person by their name.

- Friends: on each friend’s page. See [Friends](https://bwalletx.com/friends).

- Spaces: each speaker on stage. See [bSpaces](https://bwalletx.com/bspaces).

You won’t see a Tip button on your own things.

## All of it goes to them

The tip goes from your wallet to theirs. We take nothing.

If the network is slow, the wallet says the tip is on its way, so you don’t pay twice.

## Where to find it

- bWalletX Desktop: [web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/token-curves

# Token curves. One price rule for every person.

In bWalletX your $handle can be a token, and holding one token gets you into that person's room. This page is the whole pricing rule in plain words, with the numbers.

[Open the Friends market](https://web.bwalletx.com/exchange?people=1)[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## The rule

The first join costs 1¢. The price doubles every 10,000 supporters.

price = 1¢ × 2supporters ÷ 10,000

A supporter is a person who has bought from the curve, counted once however many tokens they bought. One join per person, up to 100 tokens in that join, all at the same price. The person who owns the token cannot buy from their own curve, and neither can wallets linked to them. So buying a lot yourself moves nothing: only new people move the price.

## What that looks like

Price of one token against the number of supporters, 0 to 100,000. The vertical scale is logarithmic (each gridline is ten times the one below), which is why the doubling shows as a straight line.

SupportersPrice to joinPaid to the person so far

01¢—

1,0001.07¢≈ $10.35

5,0001.41¢≈ $59.76

10,0002¢≈ $144.26

20,0004¢≈ $432.79

30,0008¢≈ $1,010

50,00032¢≈ $4,472

70,000$1.28≈ $18,322

100,000$10.24≈ $147,583

150,000$327.68≈ $4,727,115

"Paid so far" assumes each supporter bought one token. Someone who buys more in their one join pays the same price for each, and that goes to the person too.

For a normal room the curve is barely there: the first 10,000 supporters all pay between 1¢ and 2¢. It becomes a real price only for the rare person with a very large following, and by then tens of thousands of holders can sell to you instead.

## Where the money goes

- LiveTo the person, in full. Their own wallet holds the tokens on offer, and your payment goes to them on chain the moment you buy. bWalletX never holds their tokens or your money, and they don't need to be online.

- LiveNothing held back. No reserve, no pool, no treasury, no buy-back. The curve is a rule for joining, not a promise about leaving.

- LiveLeaving is between people. Any holder can list their token on the Exchange at whatever price they choose, and anyone can buy it there. That price is theirs to set and has nothing to do with the curve.

- LiveFees. The network fee is a fraction of a cent. The full edition of bWalletX adds its usual 1% Exchange fee to a buy; the store edition, bWallet, adds none.

## Supporter numbers

The first 100 people to join a person's room get a number, Supporter #1 to #100, shown next to their name in the room. After that, no number. That is the whole game: be early, get a low number.

## The person's choices

- DefaultGentle price. The curve above. Starts at 1¢ and doubles every 10,000 supporters.

- OptionFixed price. One price for a join, from 1¢ to $1,000, chosen by the person.

- OptionAsk to join. No sales. People request, the person approves.

- OptionOpen or close sales, and how many joins to keep on offer at a time (1 to 50). Closing sales returns the unsold tokens to their wallet.

Set under Exchange › Friends › Your token · Sales. Launching your token is under Settings › Identity.

## Why a curve, and why this slope

A flat price treats the tenth person and the ten-thousandth the same, and gives nobody a reason to turn up early. A steep curve turns a room into a bet. The gentle curve sits between: early supporters pay a little less and get a number, late ones pay a little more, and no normal room ever notices the difference.

Counting supporters rather than tokens is what keeps it honest. If the price rose with tokens sold, a person could buy their own supply, or one buyer could bid the price up alone. Neither moves this curve.

## What this is not

It is not an investment and we don't describe it as one. You are paying a person to join their room. The token is your key to that room, and if you ever want to pass it on, you sell it to another person at a price you both agree.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Twetch on b

Keep using Twetch, and use bWalletX next to it. The Twetch you know is in the bWalletX Feed, your old Twetch wallet can come with you, and b is on Twetch too.

## What you can do

### Read Twetch in the Feed

Open Feed and pick the Twetch chip. You see recent public Twetch posts, read from Twetch’s own public API. Tap a name to see that person’s posts and profile.

### Tip, like, lock and reply

Tip the author in BSV: it goes to the address of the key their Twetch posts are signed with. Lock BSV behind a post you rate; it stays yours and unlocks on the date shown. Likes and replies you make here are written on chain as bChat posts.

### Bookmarks and paid posts stay on Twetch

Twetch bookmarks and paid unlocks live on Twetch’s servers, so those buttons open the post on Twetch. Twetch is also on the Apps tab’s home screen.

### Bring your Twetch wallet

Add account › Restore › Twetch, then enter your Twetch 12 words. bWalletX uses the address path Twetch wallets used, so your coins show up. Your words stay on your device.

### Pay someone on Twetch

In Send, choose Other wallet › twetch.me to pay name@twetch.me. It is shown in full and marked outside bWalletX, and only offered while Twetch’s paymail answers.

Want to ask b something on Twetch? Read [b is on Twetch](https://bwalletx.com/b-on-twetch).

## Status

What works in bWalletX today, and what doesn’t yet.

- ✓ LiveTwetch posts in the Feed, with author pages

- ✓ LiveTip a Twetch author in BSV

- ✓ LiveLock BSV behind a Twetch post

- ✓ LiveLike, reply and branch from bWalletX (written as bChat)

- ✓ LiveRestore a Twetch wallet from its 12 words

- ✓ LivePay a name@twetch.me paymail

- ✓ LiveTwetch on the Apps tab home screen

- ✓ Liveb answers on Twetch as @bWalletX

- ○ Not yetImport who you follow on Twetch (Twetch’s API for this is offline)

- ○ Not yetLocks made on Twetch counted in the Most locked board

- ○ Not yetYour bWalletX likes and replies showing inside the Twetch app

# Verify a signed note

Notes and IOUs signed in bWalletX (Settings › Sign a note) carry a signature from the signer's identity key.
Paste the note file or open it here to see who signed it, when, and that not a word has changed. It's checked
in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

Check
Open a file

A valid signature proves the holder of that identity key signed this exact text. To know whose key it is, check
it against their bWalletX profile or paymail. [bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/)

# Your private things. Opened only by your wallet.

A Wallet Frame is a small window inside our products’ pages that belongs to your wallet, not to the site. It opens your private posts, music, photos and records on your own device. The site around it never sees them.

Coming November 2026. This page says what works today and what doesn’t yet. See the status list below.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[What’s live →](#status)

## Like the card box at a shop

When you pay by card in a shop, you tap a small box that belongs to the payment company, not the shop. The shop gets paid. It never sees your card details. A Wallet Frame does the same for your posts, music, photos and records: the product shows the page, your wallet shows what’s private.

## Two names for each product

Every product has a public side and a private side.

Private (in your wallet)Public (on the web)

bChatX Wallet FramebChatX.com

bMusicX Wallet FramebMusicX.com

bMintX Wallet FramebMintX.com

What you choose to make public lives at the .com, for anyone to see. What you keep private stays in the frame, for you and the people you share it with.

## Where you’ll see it

### Desktop and web

The frame sits inside the product’s page. Open it full screen whenever you like.

### Phone

Full screen inside the bWallet app: the small full-screen version.

### bApps from the store

They open full screen inside your wallet.

## Why we’re doing this

- Your keys never leave your wallet. No product site holds them, ours included.

- Your private things stay private. They’re locked before they leave your device and only opened inside your wallet.

- You choose what goes public. Nothing moves to the .com unless you say so.

- A hacked site gives nothing away. It only ever held locked content it couldn’t read.

## Status, 26 Oct 2026

- ✓ LivePrivate minting in bWallet. Media you mint is locked by default; only your wallet opens it.

- ✓ LiveWallet-only opening. The rule that private content is opened only inside your wallet, never on a product’s server.

- ◻ NovemberbChatX Wallet Frame.

- ◻ NovemberFull-screen bApps inside the wallet.

- ◻ ComingWallet Frames for music, photos and video.

- ◻ ComingDeveloper guide for putting a Wallet Frame in your own product.

We tick items here as they ship.

## Questions

### Is a Wallet Frame live today?

Not yet. Private minting already works in the wallet. The first Wallet Frame, in bChatX, is planned for November.

### Can the product’s company see my private things?

No. The frame is drawn by your wallet. The product’s site only passes along content that’s already locked.

### Do I need anything new?

Just bWalletX or bWallet. The frame comes with the wallet.

Related: [Mint](https://bwalletx.com/mint) · [bApps](https://bwalletx.com/bapps) · [Chat](https://bwalletx.com/chat) · [Identity](https://bwalletx.com/identity)

# Buy an NFT. It becomes you.

An NFT in your wallet can be more than a picture. It can be your face in chat, your player in a game, and one of a team. Some of this works today; the rest is on its way, and the checklist below says which is which.

[Open bWalletX](https://web.bwalletx.com)[See the status →](#status)

## How it works

### 1. Own it

Hold an NFT in bWalletX, like a Pixel Fox today, or an NPG Avatar when they arrive. It sits in your wallet, under your keys.

### 2. Wear it

Use its art on your wallet card and as your avatar. Soon it becomes your bChatX profile on its own, with nothing to set up.

### 3. Play as it

Coming to [bGames](https://bwalletx.com/games), such as Arena and bRacer: your NFT is the character you play.

### 4. Trade it

Buy and sell NFTs on the [bWalletX Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/exchange), from your own wallet.

### 5. Make a team

Coming: put several NFTs together as a team. Each gets its own labelled bChatX profile in your room, run as a [bBot](https://bwalletx.com/agents). Setting up is free; you pay only for the AI they use.

## The first collection: NPG Avatars

3,334 single-image Ninja Punk Girls avatars are coming to the Exchange. Each one is a character you can wear, play and team up. They are not on sale yet; we’ll say so here when they are.

Already out there: collections like the Pixel Foxes. If you hold one, it shows in your wallet today.

## Status, 20 Oct 2026

- ✓ LiveNFTs in your wallet. See and hold them in bWalletX.

- ✓ LiveNFT art on your card and avatar.

- ✓ LiveTrade NFTs on the Exchange.

- ◻ ComingYour NFT becomes your bChatX profile, automatically.

- ◻ ComingPlay as your NFT in bGames (Arena, bRacer).

- ◻ ComingNFT teams: several NFTs, each a labelled bBot profile in your room.

- ◻ ComingNPG Avatars on the Exchange (3,334).

## Questions

### Is my NFT still mine?

Yes. It stays in your wallet under your keys. Using it as your avatar or character doesn’t move it.

### What does a team cost?

Setting one up is free. When your team’s bBots talk or work, you pay only for the AI they use.

### Will people know a team member is a bot?

Yes. Every bBot profile is labelled as one.

## One break. Mended in gold.

A plate can only break once, and no two plates break the same way. Your gold seams are drawn from a hash of your key: one break per account, never repeated, mended in gold.

# bWalletX Exchange

In bWalletX the Market is an exchange: buy and sell tokens and NFTs directly between wallets. bWalletX never holds your tokens or money.

Need BSV to start? [Buy BSV in bWalletX →](https://bwalletx.com/buy) with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or bank, or from a friend.

Browse→Buy→Sell

## Sorted

### Markets

Every market with its price, 24-hour change, volume and how many are for sale. Star the ones you care about. Open one for its chart, every live listing, and Buy or Sell, with fees in BSV and dollars before you confirm. Swap and My orders are tabs on the same page.

### Categories, platforms and tags

Browse by category (Games, Social, Music, Tickets & Access and more), by the platform a token comes from, or by tag. Each choice is in the link, so you can share exactly what you see.

### Friends

Your friends’ own tokens first, then other people on bWalletX. Buy & chat buys the cheapest one on offer and opens their room in one go. See [Friends](https://bwalletx.com/friends).

On [bWalletX Desktop](https://web.bwalletx.com/exchange) now.

## What's on it

### Tokens and Social

Every BSV-21 token, including people's $HANDLE tokens. Holding one gets you into its chat room.

### Music, video, images, documents

1Sat Ordinals NFTs, filtered for safety. Play music and video you own in the wallet.

### Sell yours

List your tokens and NFTs at your own price from the wallet, and cancel any time.

### Strategies

Programs for your [agent accounts](https://bwalletx.com/agent), sold as encrypted NFTs. [See what’s for sale →](https://bwalletx.com/exchange/strategies)

-

On your phone: in bWalletX, open the Apps tab and tap Games. Games open in the wallet’s own browser, so the wallet is already there. On a computer: visit tokenblaster.lol with the [bWalletX extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension) installed, or tap Connect and scan the QR code with bWalletX on your phone.

-

Every game opens at its cabinet. Tap Try a demo for a short taste: the game runs for a few seconds under a flashing INSERT $b TO PLAY banner, with no score. To play properly, insert $b: one wallet approval loads credit into your gun, and each play is paid from it. Unload any time to send what’s left back to your wallet.

Each play is paid from your credit to The Bitcoin Corporation in one on-chain transaction; the cabinet shows the price before you start (from 10 cents a play). Some games also have a LIVE mode where each shot or bite is its own small transaction, paid from the ammo you load. In Arena you can fire tokens from your wallet instead; hit another player and that token lands in their gun. Your best runs go on the leaderboards.

Nothing here is a bet: games don’t pay out prizes. Each play is paid from the credit you insert; a demo is free but short and has no score. Play with small amounts.

# Handles. Your name is your paymail.

There is no account ID and no email needed: your 12 words are the account. On top of them you get a $handle people can pay and message, and it can be your token and your room too.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

Need to prove who you are in the real world, privately? See [Identity](https://bwalletx.com/identity).

## $handles

- Live$handles. A name people can pay and message, which is also your paymail.

- LiveNumbered handles. New accounts get a free numbered handle, from $bwallet0101 onward. $bwallet0001 to 0100 are reserved.

- LiveRenames. Change to a name you prove you hold. Your rooms and messages move with you.

- LiveYour token and your room. In bWalletX your $handle can be a personal token, with a room named after you. See [Features](https://bwalletx.com/features).

- LiveMore than one handle per account. Up to five names, one main. Add extra names in Settings › Identity (5.2.26).

- ComingHandle NFTs. Own your handle as an NFT you can hold or sell, separate from your account.

## Linked accounts ($401)

Link other accounts to your on-chain identity. Each link adds to your identity strength, so others can see more than one source vouches for you.

- LiveIn the wallet: X, Google, GitHub, LinkedIn and HandCash, from the Link your accounts card on the wallet home or Settings › Identity › Link your accounts. Beta, bWalletX only.

- LiveOn bChatX: X, Google, GitHub, Discord and LinkedIn.

## Card signature

- LiveYour signature on your card. Draw it once. It shows on the back of your wallet card. It stays on your device and is not put on chain.

Signing documents and contracts is on [/sign](https://bwalletx.com/sign).

## Sign in

- LiveSign in with bWalletX. Apps can let you sign in with your wallet instead of a password. Your wallet signs a one-time challenge; no password or email is shared. For developers: [/connect](https://bwalletx.com/connect).

- LiveLink X or Google after you create your wallet. Verify it’s you and bring your photo; you still choose your own handle: [/x](https://bwalletx.com/x), [/gmail](https://bwalletx.com/gmail).

# Identity map. One key is you. Everything else is derived.

bWalletX holds many keys and addresses, but they all grow from one place. Here is how they fit together, in plain English, and where to see your own map: Settings › Identity › Identity map, in bWalletX since 5.1.88.

## Your identity key is not an address

Your 12 words make one main key pair. The public half is your identity key, a long string that starts with 02 or 03. It says who you are. When someone looks up your paymail, this is what they get back. Calls are routed to it, and contracts you sign are sealed with it.

You never receive coins at it directly. Coins go to addresses, and addresses come from keys derived from this one.

## One key per purpose

Each job in the wallet asks for its own key, worked out from your identity key with a public recipe (BRC-42) and a label: the purpose and a key ID. Payments get a fresh receive address each time. Tokens and NFTs live at an ordinals address. Signing in to chat uses a message-signing key. Locks and pots have their own.

Because each purpose has its own key, using one never gives away another. Someone who sees your receive address cannot work out your chat key.

## One key per person you deal with

The recipe can also take the other person’s public key. You and a friend each work out the same shared key from your own private key and the other’s public key, and nobody else can. That is how private payments and direct messages stay between the two of you, and why outsiders cannot link your payments to each friend.

## Names are labels

A name is a pointer, not a key. Your paymail, name@bwalletx.com, points at your identity key. Your bChat $handle points at your chat sign-in key. An OpNS name is an on-chain name you own like any other token. Your $401 identity strands, including a verified ID check, are attached to your identity key; only the level shows, never the ID data.

Change a name and the keys underneath stay the same.

## Why restoring 12 words brings everything back

Every key above is worked out from your 12 words with the same public recipes, so nothing has to be backed up separately. Restore the words in any bWalletX and the same identity key, the same addresses and the same per-friend keys come back. Names come back too, because they point at those keys.

That is also why the words matter so much. Anyone who has them has everything on this map.

## What we learned on 8 Oct

On 8 October a room started from one of the owner’s accounts showed as started by a different one. The chat sign-in had carried over from the previous account after switching, so the chat label pointed at the wrong account’s key. Nothing was lost, but it was confusing, and it was hard to see.

We fixed the sign-in so that each account keeps its own chat session. To make any mix-up visible straight away, [5.1.88](https://bwalletx.com/releases#v5.1.88) added two things: the Identity map, which shows which key your bChat handle is tied to and flags it if that is not this account’s chat key, and sign-in alerts, which tell you when your handle is signed in somewhere new.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Only public keys and addresses appear on the Identity map; your seed and private keys never leave the wallet. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/identity

# Identity. Verified when you need it. Private when you don’t.

Your wallet doesn’t need your name. Some things do. When one of them comes up, you verify once, and your wallet can then show that a real person stands behind it without carrying your details around.

Looking for names, $handles and sign-in? They’re on [Handles](https://bwalletx.com/handles).

## Why some things need a real identity

Most of the wallet works with no name at all. A few things are different, because the other side has to know who they are dealing with:

- Signing a contract that has to bind a real person.

- Investing in a private placement.

- Services that are regulated and must know their customer.

You are only asked when something needs it.

## Verify once

The check is run by Veriff, through bChatX. You show an ID document and take a selfie in Veriff’s flow. When Veriff approves, bChatX records the result and your wallet can fetch a certificate that says you are verified.

- LiveID check with Veriff, through bChatX.

- LiveCertificate in your wallet. Your wallet proves it owns its key, and bChatX issues a certificate to that key.

## Who sees what

- VeriffYour document and selfie. Veriff handles them in its own flow.

- bChatXThe result. bChatX keeps your name, date of birth and document type, and checks your name against sanctions lists.

- Your walletA certificate with no name and no date of birth. It says you are verified, whether you are over 18, the country of your document, the check level and its dates. Each of those is encrypted, so the wallet can show one without the others.

- On chainNothing personal. Your name, date of birth and documents are not put on chain.

### Who can see the result, and when

- In a bChatX deal room, a host can ask a named member for a check. The member chooses to accept. The room then sees that the check was submitted, and whether it was approved or declined. It does not see your name, date of birth or documents.

- bChatX’s signed record of your check is private. Only you, signed in, can see all of it: the check level, the type and country of your document, the sanctions result and the date. It has no name and no date of birth. Anyone else who looks it up with your key gets “not found”, the same answer as for a key with no check, so they can’t even tell you’ve been checked.

- Sharing part of it with one person is your choice: you sign a grant naming the fields, the person’s key and an end date, and they see only those fields until then. The same goes for an issuer asking bChatX whether you meet its rules: without your grant it gets “not found”, and with one it sees only the checks your grant covers. The sanctions result is shown to them only as pass or fail, and never to the public.

## Using it

- LiveSign and seal. Sign .NDS.HTML contracts on bChatX with your drawn signature and your wallet key in one step, sealed on chain, from the Chrome extension or a paired phone. Only hashes go on chain, never the document. If a paid seal is interrupted, it can be recovered rather than paid twice. More: [/sign](https://bwalletx.com/sign).

- LiveChecks in deal rooms. A counterparty sees approved or declined, not your documents.

- ComingShowing one fact from your wallet. The certificate is built so the wallet can reveal a single field, such as over 18, to an app. A finished flow for that is still being built.

- ComingThe rest of the investor journey. One-tap pay from the wallet and a single investor flow are still being built.

## Deleting your data

- LiveDelete account in the wallet’s Settings removes your bChatX account, handle, linked accounts and chats. The records of an identity check are kept, because anti-money-laundering rules require identity checks to be kept for a period.

- ComingSelf-serve deletion of your check. Not built yet. Until it is, ask [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com).

- NoteAnything on chain cannot be deleted by anyone. That is why nothing personal is put there.

## Keys

Your keys are made and kept on your device. They are not sent to us. Lose your 12 words and nobody, including us, can recover the account.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Launchpad. Launch your own coin, with something behind it.

The Launchpad lists bonding-curve coins made on [TokenBlaster](https://www.tokenblaster.lol). You can buy and sell them in bWalletX, and launch your own from the wallet.

## Buy and sell in the wallet

Live since 5.1.74 Open Exchange and tap the Launchpad bar. The wallet checks every trade before you sign it.

## Launch your own coin

Live since 5.1.85 A Launch your own coin button at the top of the Launchpad opens TokenBlaster’s launch page inside the wallet, with your wallet connected. On the web you can also launch at [tokenblaster.lol/launch/new](https://www.tokenblaster.lol/launch/new).

## What launching costs

Live in 5.2.37 Launching a coin is not free, and the wallet says so before you sign. One Allow pays three things:

- DepositIndexing deposit: 10,010,000 sats (about 0.1 BSV). This is paid to the token indexer (GorillaPool / 1Sat), not to us. The indexer won’t validate a new BSV-21 coin until the coin’s own fee address has received at least 0.1 BSV. After that, each output it indexes uses 1,000 sats of the deposit, so this one covers about 10,000 outputs (a transfer is about 2). Without it, wallets and the Exchange can’t verify the coin’s transfers.

- NetworkNetwork fee, a fraction of a cent. This goes to miners, for the deploy, the deposit payment and the icon if you add one.

- OursOur launch fee: none. We take no share of your coin.

The fee address is worked out from the deploy transaction’s id, so the deposit can’t go in the same transaction as the deploy. The wallet sends it straight after, under the same Allow. If that payment fails, the coin still exists and the wallet offers Pay indexing deposit to try again. On the coin’s Exchange page, everyone can see its indexer fund, and the creator can tap Top up indexing. The dollar figure follows the BSV price, and the wallet shows the live amount before you sign.

## Launch it with something

A coin should come with something people can use: a website, an app or a product, and somewhere to talk, such as X, Telegram or a bChat room. Links are encouraged, not required. The plan is that coins with them rank higher on the board.

Live since 5.1.85 Token pages in the wallet show those links as chips. Tapping one warns you first: it is an outside site, not checked by us, and you should never enter your recovery phrase there.

## What a coin gives you

By default, one thing: holders can enter the coin’s bChat room. Anything else is the issuer’s business. If the issuer describes other uses, the wallet shows them as “Issuer says: …”, marked as not checked by bWalletX.

## Creator vesting and airdrops

- LiveCreator vesting. Creators can keep 0 to 20% (default 10%), always time-locked: by default a 12-month cliff, then 24 months of linear unlocking, never less than 6 months, with a public receipt. Live since 5.2.32. Personal token locks are live too (5.2.45). See [Token locking](https://bwalletx.com/token-locking).

- LiveAirdrops to holders. The way to reward holders is to send them tokens. Holders receive and keep airdrops in the inbox (5.1.85). Issuers can send tokens or BSV to every holder with one approval (5.2.32, bWalletX only). See [Airdrops](https://bwalletx.com/airdrops).

## No promises of returns

Live since 5.1.85 When you create a token in bWalletX and its description promises returns, profits, dividends or similar, the wallet warns you while you type and won’t sign until the wording is gone: “Remove wording that promises returns before publishing. Describe airdrops or room access instead.” It is a word filter, not legal advice.

## Not in the store edition

bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition, has no Launchpad.

More on how trades are checked: [015 Launchpad, and checking what we sign](https://bwalletx.com/blog/015-launchpad).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Nothing here is investment advice. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Lock. Even you can’t unlock it early.

Lock BSV on the Bitcoin SV blockchain until a date you choose, or have it paid back to you a little at a time. Once it’s locked, nobody can move it before then: not you, not bWalletX, not anyone.

Live since 5.1.85 Lock BSV is in the app: tap the lock in the top bar. It is a new feature, so start small. Lock only small amounts, a few thousand satoshis, until it has been out for a while. The app asks again if you try to lock more than 0.01 BSV.

## What locking is

A lock is a normal BSV output with a small contract attached. The contract says two things: these coins can only be spent by your key, and only in a transaction that the network won’t accept before a certain block height. Blocks come about every ten minutes, so a height is a date, roughly.

The rule is enforced by every miner, not by us. There is no switch at bWalletX that releases a lock early, and no support process that can. The coins never leave your wallet’s keys; they just can’t move until the height is reached.

## Two kinds of lock

- One unlock date. The whole amount opens at one block height.

- Gradual payouts. The amount is split into pieces, each locked to a later height: daily, weekly, monthly or every few days, for a number of payouts or until an end date. You choose how each payout is sized:

• Dollars per payout (the default), for example $10 a day. You lock BSV, sized at today’s price plus a buffer (20% unless you change it). When a piece unlocks, your wallet pays out the dollar amount at that day’s price. If the piece is worth more, it offers to re-lock the extra into the next payout; if it is worth less, you get the whole piece and the schedule shows what it came to, for example “paid $8.40 of $10”. If the wallet can’t get a current price, it doesn’t guess: the piece stays in your wallet as BSV.

• BSV per payout, for example 0.1 BSV a week.

• A percentage, of the original amount (the same payout each time, ending after 100÷X payouts) or of what is left (shrinking payouts; the last small remainder is paid at once).

Live since 5.1.85 Unlock curves and templates. Shape gradual payouts with a curve (front-loaded, back-loaded, S-curve, cliff, step or custom), or start from a template: pension, savings, rainy-day, allowance, coupons, tax pot, salary or spend-down.

Before you lock, the wallet shows every payout: estimated date, block height, BSV, and estimated dollars at today’s price.

## Read this before you lock

- It is irreversible. You type LOCK to confirm. After that, nobody can unlock it early, including you and bWalletX.

- It is BSV. The locked asset is BSV, and its dollar value goes up and down while it is locked. Dollar amounts are targets, not guarantees. The price is only used inside your own wallet, at payout time.

- Dates are approximate. A lock opens at a block height. If blocks come faster or slower than ten minutes on average, the day moves.

- Your 12 words are the only key. Lose them and the locks are lost for good. Nobody can recover them.

- Limits. Each payout must be at least 1,000 sats, because claiming one costs a small fee. One lock holds up to 520 payouts; longer percentage schedules keep the later payouts in one lock and re-split it when it opens.

## Claiming

When a lock opens, the Locks screen shows it as Ready to claim. One tap claims every opened piece, across all your locks, back into your wallet in a single transaction.

## A public receipt, if you want one

Some people lock coins to show others they can’t sell them: a founder vesting their own coins, a creator showing they aren’t about to cash out. For that, you can turn on Mint a public receipt. It is off by default.

The receipt is an NFT made in the same transaction as the locks. It shows the amount, the schedule and who locked it (your handle, if you have one), and says “Verify at bwalletx.com/lock/verify”. A picture proves nothing by itself, so the check reads the transaction from the chain and confirms that its outputs really are locks with those heights and amounts, and whether they have been claimed yet.

Turning it on links your identity to the amount, publicly and permanently. Only do it if you mean to.

[Verify a lock](https://bwalletx.com/lock/verify)

Why we built it: [023 Locks you can’t break](https://bwalletx.com/blog/023-lock-bsv).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Nothing here is investment advice. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

---

Source: https://bwalletx.com/lock/verify

# Verify a lock.

Paste the transaction id of a lock or lock receipt. This page reads it from the chain (WhatsOnChain) and checks every lock output itself. It doesn’t trust the receipt’s picture.

Check

## What is checked

- Each output that is a lock: its unlock height and amount, read from the script the network enforces.

- If the transaction has a bWalletX receipt: that every payout it lists matches a real lock output, to the same key, with the same height and amount, and that the totals add up.

- Whether each lock has been spent (claimed), from WhatsOnChain. Status: Locked, Partly claimed or Fully claimed.

Heights are block numbers; dates are about 144 blocks a day. [About Lock BSV](https://bwalletx.com/lock).

Source: https://bwalletx.com/mint

# Make something. Mint it.

Minting puts your thing on Bitcoin SV. After that it’s yours: you can sell it, send it to a friend, or let people collect it. All from the Mint button in bWalletX.

In the bWallet App Store / Google Play edition you can mint tokens and media, with no 1% bWalletX fee. Tickets and passes are bWalletX only (web, Chrome, Android download).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## What you can make

### Art & photos

One of a kind, or a numbered collection.

A painting you photographed, sold as a single piece. Or 50 numbered prints of your best shot.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Music

Tracks fans own and play in their wallet.

Release a single as 100 copies. Fans keep it, play it, and can pass it on.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Videos & films

Clips, shorts or a whole film.

A short film, a behind-the-scenes clip, or episode one of your series.

Straight from the Mint button. Up to 10 MB per file.

### Books & PDFs

Ebooks, zines, guides, reports.

A zine, a recipe book, or a guide you wrote, as a PDF, ebook or text file.

Straight from the Mint button.

### A website

A one-page site, on chain for good.

A one-page portfolio, a wedding page, or a manifesto that nobody can take down.

Straight from the Mint button, as one HTML page.

### Tickets & passes

Entry to your chatroom, event or site.

Sell 30 passes to your private chatroom, or tickets to a gig. Holding one lets you in.

Straight from the Mint button.

### A coin or memecoin

Your own token, fixed supply.

A coin for your club, your community or just for fun. You pick the name and how many exist.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Contracts

Agreements both sides sign.

A deal with a client: half up front, half when the work is delivered.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

### Trading strategies

Package a strategy others can buy.

A rule like “buy this token weekly, stop at $50”, packaged so others can buy and run it.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

### An app

List your bApp with its own token.

You built an app. List it in the wallet’s Apps tab with a token of its own.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

## What it costs

### Usually well under a cent for a photo

You pay the Bitcoin SV network to store your file, so the price depends on its size. A typical photo costs a fraction of a cent. A 1 MB file is about two cents. A full 10 MB video is about 20 cents. bWalletX adds a 1% fee on top of the network fee. Starting a new collection takes one extra transaction, so it roughly doubles the cost of that first mint.

The wallet shows the exact price in dollars before you confirm. Prices here assume BSV at about $20 and the wallet’s standard network fee; they move with the BSV price. The limit is 10 MB per file; the wallet can shrink a big photo for you.

## Contracts and new kinds of instruments

A contract in bWalletX is an agreement that both sides sign. Once it is locked on chain, it pays out by its own rules: money goes where the contract says, when the contract says. b, the wallet’s AI assistant, helps you draft it. It asks who it’s between, what each side agrees to, the price and the dates.

### Please read this

Anything that works like an investment, such as shares, bonds or a pension, may be regulated where you live. You are responsible for following the law. bWalletX is a wallet: it does not offer investments, and it can’t tell you whether something you make is allowed. If in doubt, ask a lawyer before you mint or sell it.

## Questions

### Is it permanent?

Yes. Inscriptions on Bitcoin SV can’t be deleted. So don’t mint anything you don’t own, and nothing illegal.

### Who owns it?

Whoever holds it in their wallet. When you mint, that’s you. Your keys stay on your device; we can’t move your things.

### Can I sell it?

Yes. List it on the [Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/exchange) tab, set a price in dollars, and buyers pay in BSV. You can also just send it to someone.

### Does it work on my phone and in Chrome?

Yes. bWalletX runs on [Android](https://bwalletx.com/android), [iPhone](https://bwalletx.com/iphone) and as a [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension). Contracts, strategies and apps need the full bWalletX (with b, the assistant).

# PNEEs · Penny Stablecoins

In testing. PNEE vaults are being tested and are not open yet. We will open them once testing shows they work. Nothing on this page is an invitation to lock BSV today.

Digital pennies on BSV. Each PNEE is one US cent (ticker $PNEE), backed only by BSV locked in public vaults. Notes are cash: spend them, send them, price things in them. No bank account behind them, no co-signer on your transfers, nobody who can freeze them.

Lock BSV→Mint PNEEs→Spend them

## How it works

### Notes are pennies that add up

One PNEE unit is one cent. A $10 note is just 1,000 of them together; they split and combine like any token, and the wallet shows dollars. PNEE is an ordinary BSV-21 token, so any 1Sat-compatible wallet can hold it.

### Vaults: lock BSV, mint notes

Anyone can lock BSV in a vault contract and mint notes against it, up to a tenth of its value to start (10x collateral). They keep their BSV and its upside; to unlock it, they hand the notes back. BSV went from $11 to $20 in three months, so we started very safe: a vault survives an 85% fall in BSV.

### Liquidation keeps every note backed

If BSV falls so far that a vault drops below 150%, anyone may repay its notes and take its BSV at a 10% discount. The price comes from 3 of 5 signers, using the median, with fresh timestamps.

### No interest

Notes are cash, like banknotes: holders don’t earn interest and vault owners don’t pay a yearly fee. The vault owner’s reward is spendable dollars without selling their BSV.

## PNEEs and MNEE

PNEEsMNEE

Backed byBSV locked in public vaults, visible on chainUS dollars held by a company

Can your transfer be blocked?No: notes move freelyEvery transfer is co-signed by MNEE’s server

If BSV crashesProtected by 10x collateral and liquidationsUnaffected (dollar reserves)

## The mainnet pilot (live)

PNEEs are live on BSV mainnet in a small, capped pilot: a $5 cap per vault and $10 in total.

- Token: [1599c4e49a…_0](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/1599c4e49a28c7791295f50613e1545aa9246dd592ae8b8f696b81916a475ae4) (BSV-21, 2 decimals). The whole supply sits in the issuer treasury; notes leave it only when a vault mints.

- First vault: [3a782a53…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/3a782a53ea17fdea202488c7d4e0ca335be85d1663b9a6bfb87e9435245d78f2), 12,500,000 sats of BSV (about $2.54) locked.

- First mint: [de18356c…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/de18356cb0560547d68776941a921c28fe04227b7f9e892ebbefbd1e43a00980), 25 PNEEs, checked against a 3-of-5 price of $20.32.

- First release: [913e2a78…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/913e2a786da02d21b86d4d688e25a3879879ac6e62130cfd0ebacb4657145c5a), 25 PNEE from the treasury to the vault owner.

- First liquidation (5 Oct 2026): a small, clearly labelled demo vault ([9f9f5343…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/9f9f53438a8a2463935eadf62bc221f4d035c9e1c55e0376fad801ed6de4a727), 1,000,000 sats, 2 PNEEs) whose on-chain rules allow liquidation below 1100%, so it could be shown at the real price. At a 3-of-5 median of $20.09 the vault stood at 1000%. The liquidator burned the 2 PNEEs ([640acc97…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/640acc972dd08f95b027d4ddc58bf39ce1c45782c73d15300b92f590dd4e0d29)) and liquidated the vault ([7d496a59…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/7d496a59ef82e3dfbb763f52cae5063535c4273a9812ac643714da093400be4e)): the contract paid the liquidator the debt plus the 10% discount (106,558 sats after the fee) and returned the rest, 890,493 sats, to the vault owner. Real vaults use 150%; the main pilot vault is at about 1000% and is not liquidatable.

## What we haven’t solved yet

### Honest trust model

The vault contract can’t yet see by itself that notes were really burned, so for now the issuer (bCorp) co-signs note releases and burns, in public on chain. The five price signers are run by us during the pilot. Both are fine for a few dollars and not for real money: independent price signers and an on-chain burn check come before any meaningful amount.

[Exchange › Bonds](https://bwalletx.com/exchange)

# Pots. Set money aside. Pay from it.

A pot is money you set aside inside your wallet. Regular payments come out of it, and never more than is in it. Stop it any time, without asking anyone.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## What a pot is

A pot is a named account inside your wallet, like Rent or Savings. It has its own balance. You fill it from your main account and top it up whenever you like.

Each pot has a Top up option, a Stop this pot switch, and its own History of every payment, with a link to each transaction on chain.

## The most you can lose

The pot balance is the most any payment from it can ever take. If a pot is empty, nothing more can leave it. Your main account is never touched by a pot payment.

## Paying from a pot

Standing orders pay a person or a paymail a fixed dollar amount, daily, weekly or monthly, from a pot. Subscriptions are the same thing paid to an app or service. Both are covered on the [Subscriptions](https://bwalletx.com/subscriptions) page.

Payments go out when you open the app on or after each date. If you miss a few dates, the next open catches up, up to three payments; more than that, it asks you first. If notifications are on, the wallet tells you when a pot is running low or a payment fails.

## Pause, resume, stop

Open Settings › Subscriptions and tap a pot. Each payment card has Pause, Resume and Cancel. To stop everything in a pot at once, use Stop this pot; resume it the same way.

## What works today

- LivePots. Name, fund, top up, stop and resume. Each has its own balance and history.

- LivePayments from pots. Standing orders and subscriptions, capped by the pot balance.

- LiveLow-balance and failed-payment reminders.

- ComingPayments while the app is closed. Future payments signed in advance (nLockTime), so the payee can collect each on its date.

- ComingPots in PNEEs. Pots that hold and pay penny tokens, so a 1¢ payment stays 1¢.

## bWallet (App Store and Google Play) and bWalletX

- LiveBoth: pots, standing orders to a person or paymail, pause, resume, stop and reminders. Pots are free.

- LivebWalletX only: subscriptions to apps and services paid from a pot. Store rules don’t allow these in the store edition.

Why we are building this: [016 Pots](https://bwalletx.com/blog/016-pots).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)
