# Your signature

Your wallet card has a signature strip on the back, like a bank card. In bWalletX 5.1.77 you can sign it with your finger. You can now also sign contracts on bChatX with bWalletX and seal them on Bitcoin.

Flip the card→
Sign with your finger→
Save

## Sign your card

- On the Wallet tab, tap your card to flip it over.

- On the back, under AUTHORISED SIGNATURE, tap the pen. Pressing and holding the strip works too.

- A full-screen pad opens. Sign with your finger, or with a mouse in the Chrome extension. With the phone upright, the pad turns so you sign along the length of the phone and get more room.

- Use Undo to take back the last stroke or Clear to start again, then tap Save.

Your signature now shows on the back of the card. To change it, tap the pen again and choose Redraw signature or Remove signature.

The card also turns more golden as your balance grows.

## Where it's kept

### On your device only

The signature is stored on the phone or computer you drew it on. It isn't sent to a server and it isn't put on-chain. bApps and websites can't read it.

### One per account

Each account in your wallet has its own signature. If you have a personal and a business account, sign each one separately.

### Ready for contracts

It's saved in a fixed format (one SVG path in a 1000 × 250 box) with a SHA-256 fingerprint, so the same drawing always gives the same fingerprint. That's what lets it be signed and checked later.

The signature isn't in your 12-word recovery phrase. If you restore your wallet on a new phone, sign again.

## Sign and seal contracts New

bChatX contracts (`.nds.html` files) have signature boxes. With Sign and seal with bWalletX on [bChatX](https://chat.bwalletx.com), you:

- draw your signature into your box in the contract;

- approve in bWalletX, which signs a record of what you signed with your wallet's identity key;

- approve the seal on Bitcoin. That costs the network fee only, under a penny. bChatX charges nothing.

Today that takes two approvals in your wallet: one to sign, one to pay. Nothing is sent until you approve. If anything interrupts after you've paid, reopen the document and bChatX finishes the seal for you, for up to 24 hours. You never pay twice.

Coming next: one tap. bWalletX will hand over the signature from your card and show its own screen with the document title, the box you're signing, your signature and the cost, then sign and pay together.

Only fingerprints (hashes) go on-chain, never the document or your signature. Your contract stays private between the people signing it.

### Anyone can check it

Anyone with a copy of the sealed contract can confirm three things: its fingerprint is on-chain, the identity key's signature is valid, and the drawn signature hasn't been changed since.

### Works where you are

On a computer, through the bWalletX Chrome extension. Or pair your phone by scanning a QR code and approve there, for a contract open on your computer.

This gives you an electronic signature backed by strong evidence of who signed, what and when. Whether a particular document can be signed electronically depends on the document and the law where you are; some documents, such as wills and deeds that need a witness, can't. This page isn't legal advice.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

The card signature is in bWalletX 5.1.77 and later (Android APK, Chrome extension, web and iPhone) and in bWallet, the App Store and Google Play version. Sign and seal is live on bChatX for bWalletX users (Chrome extension or a paired phone). Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Subscriptions. Set it, cap it, stop it.

Put money aside in a pot. Set up regular payments from it. The pot balance is the most they can ever take. Pause or cancel any time, without asking anyone.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## Paid from pots

Every subscription and standing order pays from a pot: money you set aside, whose balance is the most it can ever take. How pots work: [Pots](https://bwalletx.com/pots).

## Standing orders and subscriptions

A standing order pays a person or a paymail a fixed dollar amount: daily, weekly or monthly. You choose the first payment date and, if you like, how many payments to make.

A subscription is the same thing paid to an app or service. Today that means our own services, bChatX and Ask b, and only in bWalletX.

Payments go out when you open the app on or after each date. If notifications are on, the wallet reminds you the day before, and tells you when a pot is running low or a payment fails. If you miss a few dates, the next open catches up, up to three payments; more than that, it asks you first.

## What works today

- LivePots. Name, fund, top up, stop and resume. Each has its own balance and history.

- LiveStanding orders. To a person or paymail, daily, weekly or monthly, from a pot.

- LiveSubscriptions to our services. bChatX and Ask b, in bWalletX only.

- LivePause, resume, cancel. One tap on each payment card.

- LiveReminders. A notice the day before a payment, when a pot runs low, and when a payment fails.

- ComingPayments while the app is closed. Signing future payments in advance (nLockTime), so the payee can collect each one on its date. Pausing would cancel the unsent ones.

- ComingSubscribe with bWalletX. A way for any app or site to ask your wallet for a subscription.

- ComingPaying in PNEEs. Pots that hold and pay penny tokens, so a 1¢ payment stays 1¢.

## Set one up

- Open Settings and tap Subscriptions.

- Create a pot and give it a name.

- Fund it from your main account.

- Add a payment: who to pay, the amount in dollars, how often, the first date and, optionally, how many payments.

## See and cancel them

Open Settings › Subscriptions and tap a pot. Each payment has a card showing who it pays, how much, and the next date. Tap Pause to hold it, Resume to restart it, or Cancel to end it. To stop everything in a pot at once, use Stop this pot.

Every payment shows in the pot’s History. In the wallet’s [History](https://bwalletx.com/history) screen, payments from a pot are labelled “pot payment”.

## The 1¢ a day idea

One idea is that unlocking subscriptions to apps and services costs 1¢ a day, paid from a pot like anything else. That is not switched on. Nobody is charged for it today, and it would never be on in the App Store or Google Play edition. Pots and standing orders stay free.

## bWallet (App Store and Google Play) and bWalletX

- LiveBoth: pots, standing orders to a person or paymail, pause, resume, cancel and reminders.

- LivebWalletX only: subscriptions to apps and services, and any future 1¢-a-day option. Store rules don’t allow these in the store edition.

Why we are building this: [016 Pots](https://bwalletx.com/blog/016-pots).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Swap into BSV.

In bWalletX you can swap BTC, ETH, USDT, SOL and 1,000+ other coins into BSV. The BSV is paid straight into your own wallet. Nobody holds your coins along the way: you send a deposit, BSV arrives at your address.

## How it works

### Pick a coin and amount

Choose the coin you're swapping from and how much. The app shows an estimate of the BSV you'll get, fees included.

### Send the deposit

bWalletX gives you a one-off deposit address. Send the coin to it from any wallet or exchange.

### BSV lands in your wallet

Usually within 10 to 60 minutes. Track each swap in the app until it's done.

## Coins you can swap from

Swap out of any of these into BSV. Popular coins come first; search by name, ticker or network.

Show all coins

List from ChangeNOW, refreshed when the site is built. The app always shows what's available right now.

[](https://bwalletx.com/swap-coins.png)

The whole list as one picture: [swap-coins.png](https://bwalletx.com/swap-coins.png).

## Where to find it

- bWalletX for Android: [get the app](https://bwalletx.com/android).

- Desktop and web wallet: [web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com).

- Not in the store edition (bWallet) from the App Store or Google Play.

## Who runs the swap

Swaps are run by ChangeNOW, not bWalletX. ChangeNOW may pause a swap for AML/KYC checks and ask for details before releasing or refunding it.

Rates float: the amount shown is an estimate until your deposit arrives. We make no promises about the price of any coin.

ChangeNOW [terms of use](https://changenow.io/terms-of-use) · [AML/KYC policy](https://changenow.io/aml-kyc-policy) · [privacy policy](https://changenow.io/privacy-policy)

Want to buy BSV with a card instead? See [Buy BSV](https://bwalletx.com/buy).

# Token locking. Lock tokens so nobody can dump early.

[Lock BSV](https://bwalletx.com/lock) is live: BSV locked until a block height, and nobody can move it before then, not even you. Token locking does the same for tokens.

Live Personal token locks shipped in 5.2.45. Creator vesting at launch shipped in 5.2.32. Locked airdrops are still coming.

## Creator vesting at launch: prove you won’t dump

When you launch a coin, you can keep a share for yourself, locked so you can’t sell it straight away. Live since 5.2.32, in bWalletX only (the [Launchpad](https://bwalletx.com/launchpad)):

- LiveCreator allocation: 0 to 20% of the supply, set by the creator. The default is 10%.

- LiveAlways time-locked. The default is a 12-month cliff (nothing unlocks for a year), then monthly unlocks over 24 months. The shortest lock allowed is 6 months.

- LiveA public receipt. The coin’s page shows how much the creator locked and until when, linked to the locks on chain, so anyone can check them.

## Personal token locks

Live Lock BSV-21 tokens until a date, with an on-chain receipt. In the Wallet, swipe a token row and tap Lock. Your token locks are listed in Locks & Pots › Locks, under Token locks. On a new device, Find my token locks finds them again from your recovery phrase. Live since 5.2.45.

## Locked airdrops

Coming Airdrops that unlock over time: each recipient gets their own lock that they can claim once it opens. See [Airdrops](https://bwalletx.com/airdrops).

## What it isn’t

A lock only stops tokens moving before a date. It says nothing about what a token is worth, now or later.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Nothing here is investment advice. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

---

Source: https://bwalletx.com/airdrops

# Airdrops. Tokens straight to your holders.

An airdrop is a token or NFT that arrives in your wallet without you buying or minting it. Issuers use airdrops to reward the people who hold their token. bWalletX is getting a proper place for them, and the safety rules that go with them.

Live since 5.1.85 Your airdrop address and the Airdrops inbox are in the app. Items still marked Coming are not built yet.

## Your airdrop address

Every bWalletX account has an ordinals address: the address that holds your tokens and NFTs. That is your airdrop address. Give it to anyone who wants to send you a token.

- Live since 5.1.85Your airdrop address, with a QR code, in Receive › Airdrops.

- ComingThe same address and QR on your public bChatX page at `bchatx.com/u/<name>`, so issuers can find it.

## The Airdrops inbox

Anything that turns up unasked goes to an inbox instead of mixing into your wallet. A token or NFT counts as an airdrop when it was paid to one of your addresses by a transaction you didn’t fund and didn’t start: anything you bought, minted, launched, recovered or swapped is not an airdrop.

- Live since 5.1.85A badge counts new airdrops since you last opened the inbox.

- Live since 5.1.85Keep moves an airdrop out of the inbox. Hide hides it, and every future airdrop from the same issuer.

- Live since 5.1.85Only from issuers I kept before: a switch that shows airdrops only from issuers you have kept something from.

- Live since 5.1.85Unverified labels. An airdrop shows who sent it (the token’s ID, or the sending address). We don’t check what a stranger’s token is or claims to be.

## Stay safe

- Never type your 12 words on a site an airdrop points to. A token’s name, picture or link can say anything. No real airdrop needs your recovery phrase. bWalletX never asks for it outside the wallet.

- NFT content is sandboxed. HTML and SVG inscriptions are shown in an empty sandbox: no scripts, and no access to the wallet. SVG thumbnails are never loaded as wallet pages.

- Address-poisoning warnings. Scammers send a tiny payment or an unsolicited token from an address that looks like one you pay (same first and last characters), hoping you copy it from History. When you send to an address like that, the wallet warns you and shows the address it resembles.

## For issuers: airdrops, not promises

If you want to reward your holders, send them tokens. Don’t promise them returns, profits or a share of anything. A token that promises returns may be a security.

When you create a token in bWalletX, the wallet warns you while you type if the description promises returns, and won’t sign until that wording is gone: “Remove wording that promises returns before publishing. Describe airdrops or room access instead.” It is a word filter, not legal advice.

By default, holding a token gives you one thing: entry to that token’s bChat room. Anything else is what the issuer says, shown as “Issuer says” and not checked by bWalletX.

Airdrops that unlock over time are planned too: see [Token locking](https://bwalletx.com/token-locking).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Nothing here is investment advice. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/bmail

In bWalletX now

# bMail

Email where every letter carries a stamp. Penny post: 1¢ to reach anyone.

1¢Penny post

3¢Priority

↩Reply paid

## How it works

1 · WRITE

### Write to a $handle

Address your letter to anyone’s $handle, the same name they use for payments and chat.

2 · STAMP

### Add a stamp

1¢ Penny post, 3¢ Priority, or Reply paid so they can answer you for free. You see the full price before anything is sent.

3 · DELIVERED

### It arrives sealed

Only they can read it. The biggest stamps rise to the top of their inbox. Friends are always free and always on top.

## Why stamps

- Stamps stop spam. Sending a million letters costs real money, so nobody does it. Sending one costs a penny.

- You get paid for your attention. The stamp goes to you, the person reading, not to us.

- Requests holds the rest. Unstamped mail from strangers and token airdrops wait quietly in Requests, without notifications. Look when you like: some of them turn out to matter.

Your price, your rules. Everyone starts at the Penny post, 1¢. You can raise your price to reach you, and mail below it goes to Requests.

## Delivery options

OptionWhat it does

StandardYour letter, sealed and stamped, delivered to their mailbox.

## Your public mailbox

Every bWalletX user gets a page at bwalletx.com/$you, for example [bwalletx.com/$alice](https://bwalletx.com/$alice). People without the app can find you there and write to you.

## Questions

Who gets the stamp?
The person you write to. Payment goes wallet to wallet, and bMail takes no cut.

Do I pay to write to friends?
No. Friends are free and always on top of your inbox.

When can I use it?
Now. bMail is in bWalletX: tap the mailbox icon at the top of the app.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Open the web wallet](https://web.bwalletx.com)

Part of the [bWalletX family](https://bwalletx.com/b-family). bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/chat

# Coordinate on BSV. Talk where the money is.

BSV is a messaging protocol at heart. Every transaction can carry a message. So the conversation about BSV should live on BSV, in the same wallet that holds your coins and tokens.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Open bChatX](https://chat.bwalletx.com)

## Why

Twitter, Reddit and Telegram put every community in one room, and BSV threads there get buried or piled on. We still post there, because that is where new people are. But the planning should happen on BSV, where every account is a wallet and, as paid messages arrive, spam costs money. Advertise there, coordinate here. The full argument: [021 Coordinate on BSV](https://bwalletx.com/blog/021-coordinate-on-bsv).

## Chat in your wallet

Chat is part of bWalletX. You don’t sign up anywhere else: your wallet is your account, and the people you talk to can pay you, and you them, in the same place. bChatX is the full version, on the web and inside the wallet.

Other BSV networks are already here, and Chat reads from them rather than replacing them:

[### Twetch
One of the longest-running BSV social apps.](https://twetch.com)
[### Treechat
Threaded posts and replies on BSV.](https://app.treechat.com)
[### Fwetch
Boards on the Vulpine network.](https://fwetch.lol)
[### Peck
A BSV feed built on Bitcoin Schema.](https://peck.to)
[### bChatX
Our full chat app. Rooms, feed and messages.](https://chat.bwalletx.com)

Twetch, Treechat, Fwetch and Peck are made by other teams, not The Bitcoin Corporation.

## What Chat does

Each item is marked by what the code does today.

- LiveMessage boards. Open rooms in bChat: public or invite-only, anyone signed in can start one. The bChat feed also reads Twetch, Treechat, Fwetch and Peck posts in one place.

- LiveToken-gated rooms. Hold a BSV-21 token or 1Sat collection and its room appears in your Chat list. Sell it and the room goes. bChat checks the holding on every read and post. Not in bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition.

- LivePrivate messages. Direct messages between wallets, with blocking and reporting.

- LiveVoice and video calls. One-to-one calls between friends. Either side can turn the camera on or off during a call.

- LiveTips. Tip the author of a post in BSV, paid to their own verified address.

- LiveBroadcast into a Space. The host or a speaker shares a tab or screen, with its sound, to everyone in the Space (since 5.2.17). Not in the store edition.

- Live since 5.1.85Pay per message. In token rooms the wallet now charges the room’s price per message: the message and the payment go in one transaction (50-sat minimum).

- Partly livePay per second. Paid calls by the second are live in [bPhone](https://bwalletx.com/bphone) (5.1.87). Paying for a stream by the second is next.

- Partly livePay with tokens. bPhone calls can already be paid in MNEE or any BSV-21 token (5.1.87). Paying for messages in a token is next.

- Partly liveSet your price to be reached. You can already charge to receive calls with [bPhone](https://bwalletx.com/bphone) (5.1.87). A price for strangers to message you, with friends free, is next.

## Start now

Download bWalletX, open the Chat tab, and join the bWallet Lounge. Buy a token to get into its room. Or open bChat in a browser and sign in with your wallet.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Open bChatX](https://chat.bwalletx.com)

The full bChatX story, with dates: [bwalletx.com/bchatx](https://bwalletx.com/bchatx).

Building a BSV app? Let your users sign in with bWalletX: [bwalletx.com/connect](https://bwalletx.com/connect).

Part of the [bWalletX family](https://bwalletx.com/b-family). bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Your $name is your token

In bWalletX, one name does three jobs: it's where people pay you, it's a token people can hold, and it's the key to your chat room.

handle@bwalletx.com→
$HANDLE→
$HANDLE room

## 1. Handles

Your handle is a paymail: an address that looks like an email, such as `yourname@bwalletx.com`. People send you money, tokens and messages to your name instead of a long string of letters and numbers. Claiming one is free.

A wallet has one main name. It can keep older names that still receive, and Settings › Identity lists every one of them, so nothing receives for you without you knowing. You can unlink any of them.

## 2. Link X or Google after you create your wallet

New wallets are made with a passkey. Afterwards, On your wallet’s home, tap the Link your accounts card, or go to Settings › Identity › Link your accounts. Linking proves the account is yours. It doesn't give you a name: you choose your own handle.

### X

Link X to verify it's you and bring your X picture. Your @name is suggested when you choose your handle; you can change it.

### Google

Link Google to verify it's you and bring your Google picture. Your email address is never turned into a name.

Your X or Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture too. bWalletX never sees your X or Google password, and your keys never leave your device. Older `.x` and `.gmail` names still receive, but new ones aren't given out. Linking accounts and token rooms are in bWalletX only, not the bWallet store edition.

## 3. Tokenised handles

Turn your name into a token in one tap: $HANDLE for handle@bwalletx.com. It's a BSV-21 token on the Bitcoin SV blockchain, with a fixed supply that starts in your wallet. Its icon is your profile picture.

Anyone can copy a ticker, so bWalletX checks every token's signed creator record. Only the token actually made by that name's owner gets the check mark. Copycats don't.

Personal tokens are social tokens: they're for access and fun, not investments. They don't pay dividends.

## 4. The market

Every user token can be bought and sold on the bWalletX Exchange. List some of yours for sale at your own price, or buy someone else's to get into their room. Trades settle directly between wallets on chain; bWalletX never holds your tokens or money.

Before a token shows up in other wallets and the Exchange, its creator pays a one-off indexing deposit to the 1Sat indexer. It's a prepaid balance that pays for the token's transfers, not a fee to bWalletX.

## 5. Chat rooms

Every user token has a chat room. Hold the token, join the room. Inviting someone is as simple as sending them one token.

The room's owner sets its rules: how many tokens you need to hold to get in, and how chatting uses them up. For example, 1 token per character typed, burned or sent back to the owner. Every room can have its own economy.

## 6. Friends

The Friends tab in your wallet is your address book: people you've paid, called, chatted with or followed. A friend only needs a name; if they have a token, their row shows how many you hold, with a button to enter their room or buy in. Message, call or pay anyone in one tap.

[Get bWalletX for Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta and some room rules are still being rolled out. Tokens can lose all value. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

---

Source: https://bwalletx.com/gmail

# Link your Google account

Link your Google account to your bWalletX to show it's really you. Your wallet gets a Google badge and can use your Google picture. You make the wallet first; linking Google comes after, and it's optional. You choose your own handle, and your email address never becomes part of it.

Google account→
Google badge + photo→
yourname@bwalletx.com

## How to do it

- [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) on your phone or computer and create your wallet.

- On your wallet's home screen, tap the Link your accounts card, or go to Settings › Identity › Link your accounts.

- Choose Google and pick your account on Google's own sign-in page.

- Back in bWalletX, your Google account shows as linked.

Linking never changes your handle or your money.

## Your name

Signing in with Google doesn't make a name for you. Your handle is a plain `yourname@bwalletx.com` that you choose. We stopped making names from Gmail addresses because they showed your email address to anyone who saw the name.

Older `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com` names, made before October 2026, keep receiving, and the app hides most of the name where others can see it. New ones aren't given out.

## What you get

### A Google badge

Your listing shows that a Google account is linked, so people know a real account stands behind your wallet.

### Your picture

Your Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture, so friends recognise you in chats, calls and payments.

### Your own token and room

Turn your handle into $YOURNAME, a BSV-21 token with your picture as its icon. Hold the token, join your room.

## What Google shares

bWalletX asks Google for three things only: your email address, your name and your profile picture. It never sees your Google password and can't read your email, contacts or files. Your wallet's keys are made on your device and never leave it; Google has nothing to do with them.

Your 12-word recovery phrase is still the only way to get your money back, so keep it safe.

## Status

- LiveLink your accounts on the wallet home and in Settings › Identity: Google, X, GitHub and LinkedIn.

- BetaGoogle badge on your wallet and listing (shown as beta in the app).

- LiveNo email in your name. New Gmail-based names are no longer given out.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Link X](https://bwalletx.com/x)
[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

Linking Google and X is in bWalletX. The App Store and Google Play version, bWallet, doesn't have them yet. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Live. Your token is the ticket.

Creators go live in a room that only their token holders can enter. Hold the token and you’re in. The token, the payment and the room all sit in one wallet.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## The idea

A creator’s room is gated by the creator’s token. Holders get in and watch the creator live: one person on camera, everyone else watching, with chat alongside. Anyone who doesn’t hold the token sees a “hold 1 to join” door, not the stream.

Think creator rooms and subscriber streams, except the subscription is a token you hold. You can keep it, sell it or give it away. Pay-per-minute and tips can sit on top, as options the creator chooses.

## Why in the wallet

bWalletX is a smart social super wallet: the things you do with your money belong in the place you keep it. Your token, your payment and the room are all in one app, so there’s no separate platform account, card or subscription to manage.

Holding a token to get in costs nothing extra. Payments go wallet to wallet; you pay the network fee, plus a small indexing fee when a token moves. Any fee on paid streams will be stated up front before you pay. The full version of rooms and spaces lives in [bChat](https://bwalletx.com/chat).

## How it works

- 1Your token. A creator has a token, such as a personal $NAME token (see [$handles](https://bwalletx.com/handles)).

- 2Your room. The room is set to “hold the token to enter”. The server checks holdings on every read and post, so selling the token closes the door.

- 3Go live. The creator opens a space and turns the camera on. Holders watch and chat; the creator can bring a viewer on stage.

- 4Optional extras. Pay-per-minute, tips, or burning a ticket to enter, as the creator chooses.

## What works today

- LiveToken rooms. Hold a token to enter a room. In bChat and in bWalletX.

- LiveSpaces in bChat. A host, speakers and listeners, a raise-hand queue, and opt-in camera for people on stage. On the web at [bchatx.com/spaces](https://chat.bwalletx.com/spaces), where anyone can listen without signing in. Runs on our own video server.

- Live1:1 voice and video calls in bWalletX.

- Partly liveWatching a live room inside bWalletX. Audio and video Spaces in token rooms are live in bWalletX since 5.1.85 (not the store edition): see [bSpaces](https://bwalletx.com/bspaces). One-to-many video streams are still watched in bChat.

- LivePay-per-minute Spaces. Paid a minute at a time, wallet to wallet, with a spending cap you set (bWalletX since 5.1.95, not the store edition).

- LiveTips during a Space. Tip a speaker on stage from their tile (since 5.2.16).

- ComingBigger audiences. Streams to more viewers than one video server can hold.

## Content rules

Creators are responsible for what they stream. They must follow the law where they and their viewers are, and our terms. Rooms and messages can be reported, and paid streams will need identity and age checks before they open.

## bWallet (App Store and Google Play) and bWalletX

- LiveBoth: 1:1 voice and video calls.

- LivebWalletX only: token rooms. They aren’t available in the store edition, so token-gated live rooms won’t be either.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

---

Source: https://bwalletx.com/lounge

# bWalletX Social

Social in bWalletX starts with your name. One name does three jobs: it's where people pay you, it's a token people can hold, and it's the key to your chat room. Around it: the Feed, calls, and a wallet that knows your friends.

handle@bwalletx.com→
$HANDLE→
$HANDLE room

## 7. The Feed

Posts from BSV social apps (bChat, Twetch, Treechat and more) in one Feed: Following, For you and Latest. Post, reply, quote, like, tip the author in sats, or lock BSV behind a post (it stays yours and unlocks at the date shown). Bookmark, mute, block and report are built in.

## 8. Calls

Call anyone with a name, straight from the wallet. Calls are signed by your wallet key, so people know it’s really you; add the person to your friends from the call screen.

# Link your X account

Link your X account to your bWalletX to show it's really you. Your wallet gets an X badge and can use your X picture. You make the wallet first, with a passkey or a password; linking X comes after, and it's optional.

@yourhandle→
X badge + photo→
yourname@bwalletx.com

## How to do it

- [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) on your phone or computer and create your wallet.

- On your wallet's home screen, tap the Link your accounts card. You can also go to Settings › Identity › Link your accounts at any time.

- Choose X, sign in on X's own page and allow access.

- Back in bWalletX, your X account shows as linked.

The same screen links Google, GitHub and LinkedIn. Linking never changes your handle or your money.

## Your name

Linking X doesn't make a name for you. Your handle is a plain `yourname@bwalletx.com` that you choose, the same as everyone else's, in Settings › Identity › Change handle. X allows underscores in usernames and paymail names don't, so `@Jane_Doe` would be `jane-doe`.

Older `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com` names, made before October 2026, keep receiving. New ones aren't given out.

## What you get

### An X badge

Your listing shows that the X account is linked, so people can tell your wallet belongs to the person they follow.

### Your picture

Your X profile picture becomes your wallet's picture, so friends recognise you in chats, calls and payments.

### Your own token and room

Turn your handle into $YOURNAME, a BSV-21 token with your picture as its icon. Hold the token, join your room.

## What X shares

bWalletX reads three things from X: your username, your display name and your profile picture. It never sees your X password, can't post for you and doesn't read your messages. Your wallet's keys are made on your device and never leave it; X has nothing to do with them.

Your 12-word recovery phrase is still the only way to get your money back, so keep it safe.

## Status

- LiveLink your accounts on the wallet home and in Settings › Identity: X, Google, GitHub and LinkedIn.

- BetaX badge on your wallet and listing (shown as beta in the app).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Link Google](https://bwalletx.com/gmail)
[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

Linking X and Google is in bWalletX (Android APK, Chrome extension, web and iPhone). The App Store and Google Play version, bWallet, doesn't have them yet. They aren't offered for agent accounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Ask b

Ask b is the AI assistant built into bWalletX. Press and hold the big b in the middle of the bottom bar to talk to it (a tap goes home): it knows how the wallet works, helps you design strategies, and in chat rooms you can call it in with `/b`.

### Looking for agent accounts: AIs with their own wallet?

Separate accounts that an AI runs for you, each with its own budget and its own ghost. [Agent accounts →](https://bwalletx.com/agents)

## Two ways to use it

### Your own key

Add an API key for Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter. It stays in secure storage on your device and b’s requests go straight from your phone to that provider, which handles them under its own terms. Anything you report to b still comes to our team.

### Pay per message

The wallet gets a quote, pays in BSV and gets the answer, with a daily limit. The price is set in US dollars and converted to sats at quote time. Pay per message is in bWalletX only.

## In chats: /b

Type `/b` followed by your question in a chat room and Ask b answers there, paid in BSV.

## What it can do

Explain a feature
Create a strategy
Trade with a strategy
Buy or sell one

It has the wallet's usage guide as its system prompt, so it can explain features. In an agent account it can act, buying and sending, but only through the strategy rules the wallet enforces, never on its own judgement. [How strategies work →](https://bwalletx.com/strategies)

## Privacy and consent

Talking to b means talking to us. b is our team’s assistant, not a private chat, and it is not end-to-end encrypted. We read and keep conversations with b for up to 180 days, with secrets stripped, to fix bugs and improve the app. [How we handle chats with b →](https://bwalletx.com/talk-to-b)

Before the first message to each provider, a consent sheet shows what is sent (your message and the last 8 turns) and what isn't. You can revoke consent in Settings. The wallet refuses to send anything that looks like a recovery phrase or private key. Each reply only sees the recent conversation, but our team keeps the conversations as described above.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Agent accounts](https://bwalletx.com/agents)

The store builds use your own key only. The story so far: [009 The b agent: paid, or your own key](https://bwalletx.com/blog/009-the-b-agent). Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Agent accounts: every AI gets its own ghost

An agent account is a separate wallet account that an AI runs for you, with its own keys and its own budget. It trades, sends and reports inside the limits you set, and you can stop it or sweep everything back any time.

### Looking for Ask b?

The assistant you chat with inside the wallet is Ask b. [Ask b →](https://bwalletx.com/agent)

Traderrunning
Slow accumulator · cap $20/day
$120.00

Treasurerrunning
Tops up the other agents
$64.25

Reporterread only
Daily summary to chat
$0.00

Scoutstopped
$HANDLE fund · paused by you
$18.90

## The ghost is the agent's face

Make an account an agent account and it gets a pixel ghost in its own colour. It shows on the wallet card when that account is selected and is the account's avatar everywhere: the account menu, Settings and chat. One look tells you which agent you're in.

2nd

4th

## What an agent account can do

### Spend only its budget

Its balance is all it can ever spend. Fund it from any of your accounts in one tap; your other accounts are never touched.

### Follow a strategy

Agree the rules in plain words, or load a strategy, and it trades by those rules and nothing else. [Strategies →](https://bwalletx.com/strategies)

### Show its work

An activity log lists every action, with links to the transactions. Add labels and an optional daily spending cap in dollars.

### Stop on your word

Stop one agent or Stop all agents. A stopped account refuses every spend until you resume it, and Sweep back moves every token, NFT and all the BSV home.

## Many agents

Run one AI per account, or one across several. A Trader on two strategy accounts, a Treasurer that tops them up, a Reporter that only reads: each sees only the accounts you give it.

## bAgents

bAgents is the home for agents on bWalletX: browse, set up and manage the AIs that run your agent accounts. [agents.bwalletx.com →](https://agents.bwalletx.com)

## Pair a computer, or Claude

The bWalletX CLI runs agent accounts on a laptop or a server. Pair it with your phone so the phone signs every request, or export an agent account's key file to run unattended. Every spend is checked first: the kill switch, the daily cap, at most 30 spends an hour, then the strategy's rules.

`# install (Node 20+)
npm i -g bwalletx
bwalletx login --account phone # scan the QR in your agent account
bwalletx agent run trader # run its strategy
bwalletx stop # kill switch
# Claude Code, over MCP
claude mcp add bwalletx -- npx -y bwalletx mcp`

Over MCP, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any agent can manage the agent accounts you give it, within the same limits as the app. An AI can only load strategies on paper: going live is a step you take yourself. [CLI guide →](https://bwalletx.com/cli) · [MCP guide →](https://bwalletx.com/mcp)

## Start in a minute

In bWalletX, open the account menu and tap Add agent account, or go to Settings › Agents. Move in a small budget, give it a strategy, and its ghost appears on the card.

Agent accounts spend real money: start with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Add your app to bWallet

Built something on BSV? Put it on the Apps screen of bWallet and bWalletX, one tap away for everyone who opens the wallet. It's free, and a person reviews every app.

[Submit your app](#submit)[Developer docs](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

The Apps screen in bWalletX today.

## Why add it

### One tap from the wallet

Your icon sits in Apps beside the other BSV apps. People open it without typing an address.

### Sign-in is already there

Apps open in the wallet's own browser with the wallet connected (BRC-100). Ask for the user's identity key and you have a login, with no passwords to store.

### Payments in BSV

Ask the wallet to pay and the user sees one approval sheet with the amount. No card forms, no accounts to set up.

### Free

No listing fee and no cut of your sales. We check the app is safe, then add it.

## What you need

- Your app's address, served over `https://`

- A name (up to 40 characters) and a category

- An email address, so we can tell you when it's live (never shown)

- An icon: we take it from your site. An `apple-touch-icon` gives the sharpest tile.

- Optional: a one-line description and a BSV address

## What happens after you submit

- Your submission is saved for review. Nothing is listed straight away.

- A person opens your app and checks it against the list below.

- If it passes, we add it with your site's name, tagline and icon, and it ships in the next wallet release.

- We email you when it's in bWallet.

Want it on your own phone today? In the wallet, open Apps and tap + Add app. That adds any website to your own Apps screen straight away, saved to your wallet. It doesn't list it for anyone else.

# bBots: little helpers that work for you.

A bBot is a helper account that lives in your wallet. It has its own small budget and the limits you set, and it does jobs for you while you get on with your day.

## What a bBot is

### Its own account

Each bBot is a separate account in your wallet with its own ghost colour. Your main balance stays where it is.

### Its own small budget

Put in only what it may spend. It can’t touch anything else.

### Your limits

Daily caps and rules you choose. Stop it any time, in one tap.

### Jobs, not chat

Trade within your rules, look after a token’s room, sort your mail. Small, useful, repeatable.

b is the big helper: [Ask b](https://bwalletx.com/ask-b) anything. bBots are smaller. They’re yours, and they work for you.

## Always labelled

Every bBot shows a ghost and the name of the person who owns it. A bBot never pretends to be a person.

trader.agent · bBot owned by $you

## What works today

- LIVEAgent accounts in bWalletX Desktop. Account menu › Agents › Add agent account. Each one gets its own ghost, its own funds and its own limits. Trading rules start on paper (pretend money) until you choose Run live.

- LIVEThe bwalletx CLI and MCP, for developers. Let Claude or another AI use an agent account from your own machine. Open source: [github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwalletx-cli](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwalletx-cli). See [CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) and [MCP](https://bwalletx.com/mcp).

- COMINGThe name bBots in the wallet. Today the wallet still says “agent accounts”.

- COMINGThe .mail bBot for bMail (below).

- COMINGA bBot for every token room, to greet people and keep the room going.

- COMINGTemplates you add in a tap. Pick a job, set a budget, done.

## Coming: the .mail bBot

A bBot for [bMail](https://bwalletx.com/bmail) that reads your inbox so you don’t have to start the day in it.

### Morning summary

Who needs a reply, what’s due, and what you can skip.

### Drafts in your tone

Ready to send, but never sent without your OK.

### Phishing flagged red

Odd links and fake senders marked before you click.

### Ignores tricks

Instructions hidden inside an email are just text to it. It only takes orders from you.

### Waiting on them

Keeps track of who owes you a reply and nudges when you say so.

### Friday recap

Your week in mail, in a few lines.

## Honest bots

On most networks, bots hide. They pose as people and nobody knows who runs them.

On bChatX, every bBot is labelled, owned by a person who answers for it, and pays its own way from its own budget. That’s the principle we’re building to.

## Questions

Can a bBot spend my money?
Only within the budget and limits you set. It has its own account, so it can’t reach the rest of your wallet, and you can stop it any time.

Will people know it’s a bot?
Yes, always. Every bBot carries a ghost and its owner’s name.

How is a bBot different from b?
b is the big helper you ask things. A bBot is a small helper of your own with a job and a budget.

I’m a developer. Where do I start?
Add an agent account in bWalletX Desktop, then use the [bwalletx CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) or [MCP](https://bwalletx.com/mcp). More on [agent accounts](https://bwalletx.com/agents).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Open Desktop](https://desktop.bwalletx.com)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/cli

# bWalletX CLI

Your wallet and your agents from the command line, on your laptop or a server.

npm i -g bwalletx→
bwalletx login→
bwalletx agent run

## Get started

``npm i -g bwalletx # Node 20+
bwalletx login --account phone # shows a QR: scan it in bWalletX from your agent account``

In bWalletX (5.1.40 or later), open your agent account, then Settings › Paired websites › Scan to connect. Check both screens show the same 4-digit code, choose what the CLI may do and for how long (1, 7 or 30 days), and tap Pair. Your keys never leave the phone.

For a server with no phone around, export a key file instead: Agents › your agent account › Run on a computer › Export for CLI, then `bwalletx key import ./trader.key.json`.

## Commands

``bwalletx accounts # paired and imported agent accounts
bwalletx balance --account trader # BSV and tokens, in dollars
bwalletx price <tokenId>
bwalletx send 1 name@bwalletx.com --account trader
bwalletx buy <tokenId> --max-usd 2 --account phone # cheapest listing, +1% fee, never over the cap
bwalletx strategy load ./slow-accumulator.json --account trader
bwalletx agent run trader # run its strategy unattended
bwalletx log --account trader
bwalletx stop # kill switch: refuse every spend``

## What works today (v0.5)

### Live

Balances, prices, the activity log, sending BSV to an address or paymail, and buying BSV-21 tokens from the Exchange. Strategies run by `agent run` trade for real once you load them live.

### Paired or key file

Paired (`bwalletx login`): the phone checks and signs every request, so bWalletX must be open on that agent account. Key file: runs unattended on a server.

### New in 0.5

Minting (`mint`, `mint-manifest`), selling and buying listings (`list`, `unlist`, `listings`, `buy-listing`), and the account’s own BRC-100 wallet (`brc`, `fund`, `withdraw`). Install or update with `npm i -g bwalletx`.

## Your keys stay safe

### Agent accounts only

Only agent accounts can be exported, never your main wallet. The key file is encrypted with a passphrase you choose and stays encrypted on disk.

### Limits

The agent account's balance is the budget. Every spend is checked first: the kill switch, the daily cap, at most 30 spends an hour, then the strategy's rules. Every action is logged.

Free example strategies and the file format: [Strategies](https://bwalletx.com/strategies) · [spec](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/spec). Source: [github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwalletx-cli](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwalletx-cli) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bwalletx).

[Agent wallet](https://bwalletx.com/agent)
[Developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Sign in with bWalletX

How to let people sign in to your site or app with their bWalletX: one script tag, two routes on your server, and no API keys.

Also as plain Markdown for AI coding agents: [bwalletx.com/connect.md](https://bwalletx.com/connect.md). Checked against bWalletX 5.2.45, connect.js and @bwalletx/connect 0.5.0 on 18 Oct 2026. Full docs: [docs.bwalletx.com/developers/connect](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/connect/).

## In 30 seconds

One script tag on your page, two routes on your server.

``<script src="https://bwalletx.com/connect.js"></script>
``

- `bWalletX.renderButton('#signin', { onClick })` draws the gold "Sign in with bWalletX" button.

- `bWalletX.signIn({ challenge, pairing })` finds the user's wallet (Chrome extension, the bWalletX app's browser, or a phone or the web wallet by QR code), asks your server for a one-time challenge, and has the wallet sign it with a key derived from its identity key.

- Your server checks the signature with `@bsv/sdk`, deletes the nonce, and signs the user in as that identity key.

- No API key, no client ID, no account with us. Nothing passes through bwalletx.com except the script itself. The only service of ours involved is the encrypted pairing relay, and only when the user signs in from a phone or the web wallet.

The user's identity key (a 33-byte compressed public key, 66 hex characters) is their user ID on your site. It is the same key every time they sign in with the same wallet.

## Three ways the user's wallet can answer

Where the user is
How your page reaches the wallet
What you need

Chrome or Brave with the bWalletX extension
BRC-100 wallet discovery: dispatch `brc100:requestWallet`, take the `brc100:announceWallet` reply whose `info.rdns` is `com.bwalletx.extension`
Nothing extra. connect.js finds it

Your site opened inside the bWalletX app's own browser
Same discovery; the app announces `rdns: space.bwallet.mobile` and also sets `window.CWI`
Nothing extra. connect.js finds it

bWalletX on a phone, or the web wallet at web.bwalletx.com
Pairing: your page shows a `https://www.bwallet.space/pair?...` link as a QR code. The phone scans it; the web wallet takes it pasted. Both then talk to your page through `relay.bwallet.space`, end-to-end encrypted
A `pairing` option with somewhere to show the QR code. connect.js does the rest

All three give you the same thing: an object with the BRC-100 `WalletInterface` methods. Sign-in is the same code for all of them.

## 1. Browser: one script tag

`connect.js` is small. It loads the full sign-in build (`https://bwalletx.com/connect/bwalletx-connect.global.js`, about 125 KB with `@bsv/sdk` inside) the first time you call `signIn`, `pair` or `renderButton`, so those three return promises. This example uses qrcodejs from cdnjs to draw the QR code; any QR library works.

``<div id="signin"></div>
<div id="bwx-pair"></div>

<script src="https://bwalletx.com/connect.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/qrcodejs/1.0.0/qrcode.min.js"></script>
<script>
const panel = document.getElementById('bwx-pair');

async function post(url, body) {
const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
if (!res.ok) throw new Error((await res.json().catch(() => ({}))).error || 'HTTP ' + res.status);
return res.json();
}

bWalletX.renderButton('#signin', {
onClick: async (button) => {
button.disabled = true;
try {
const r = await bWalletX.signIn({
// 1. Your server makes the challenge for this identity key.
challenge: (identityKey) => post('/auth/bwalletx/challenge', { identityKey }),
// 2. Only used when there is no extension or in-app browser: phone or web wallet.
pairing: {
onLink: (link) => {
panel.replaceChildren();
new QRCode(panel, { text: link, width: 220, height: 220 });
const p = document.createElement('p');
p.textContent = 'Scan with bWalletX on your phone, or paste this link into web.bwalletx.com: ' + link;
panel.append(p);
},
onCode: (code) => panel.append('Check bWalletX shows ' + code + ', then tap Connect.'),
},
});
// 3. Your server checks the signature and starts a session.
const { identityKey } = await post('/auth/bwalletx/verify', {
identityKey: r.identityKey, nonce: r.nonce, signature: r.signature,
});
panel.textContent = 'Signed in as ' + identityKey.slice(0, 12) + '… (via ' + r.method + ')';
} catch (e) {
panel.textContent = e.code === 'NOT_FOUND' ? 'bWalletX was not found.' : e.message;
} finally {
button.disabled = false;
}
},
});
</script>
``

`bWalletX.signIn` looks for a wallet in this order:

- The bWalletX Chrome extension (BRC-100 discovery, `rdns` `com.bwalletx.extension`). `method: 'extension'`.

- The bWalletX app's in-app browser (`rdns` `space.bwallet.mobile`, or `window.CWI` if nothing announced). `method: 'in-app'`.

- A pairing saved by an earlier sign-in in this browser (in `localStorage` under `bwalletx.connect.pairing.v1`). `method: 'pairing'`.

- A new pairing, if you passed `pairing`: `onLink` gets a `https://www.bwallet.space/pair?...` link to show as a QR code (and as text for web.bwalletx.com), and `onCode` gets a 4-digit code both screens show. `method: 'pairing'`.

If none of these works it throws an error with `code: 'NOT_FOUND'`. It returns `{ identityKey, signature, nonce, method, wallet }`. Post the first three to your verify route. `wallet` is a BRC-100 `WalletInterface` you can keep using.

Other things on `window.bWalletX`:

Call
What it does

`bWalletX.connect({ timeout })`
The extension only, authenticated: `{ wallet, info, identityKey }`. Rejects with `code: 'NOT_INSTALLED'`. Doesn't load the full build.

`bWalletX.pair({ onLink, onCode })`
A wallet paired by QR or pasted link, without signing in.

`bWalletX.renderButton(el, { onClick, subtitle })`
The gold button. `subtitle: false` hides the second line.

`bWalletX.load()`
The full build's exports (`signInWithBwalletX`, `pairBwalletX`, `restorePairing`, `clearPairing`, `findBwalletX`, ...).

Prefer to host it yourself? Copy `connect.js` and `connect/bwalletx-connect.global.js` to the same folder structure on your site; connect.js loads the full build from next to itself. It is also on npm: `pnpm add @bwalletx/connect @bsv/sdk`.

## The button

Sign in with bWalletXalso works with bWallet

`bWalletX.renderButton()` draws this for you. If you draw your own, use the gold button. Keep the label "Sign in with bWalletX". The logo is at `https://bwalletx.com/logo.svg` (the gold b, viewBox 74 x 100). Don't recolour it; it sits on a black circle so it reads on the gold.

``<button type="button" id="bwx-signin" class="bwx-signin">
<span class="bwx-mark"><img src="https://bwalletx.com/logo.svg" alt="" width="15" height="20"></span>
<span class="bwx-label">Sign in with bWalletX<small>also works with bWallet</small></span>
</button>
<div id="bwx-pair"></div>
``
``.bwx-signin {
display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
min-height: 48px; padding: 10px 22px 10px 10px;
border: 0; border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer;
background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fcd34d, #f59e0b);
color: #000; text-align: left;
font: 700 16px/1.2 system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.2);
}
.bwx-signin:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fde68a, #fbbf24); }
.bwx-signin:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffd24d; outline-offset: 3px; }
.bwx-signin:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: wait; }
.bwx-signin .bwx-mark {
display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 50%; background: #000; flex: none;
}
.bwx-signin small { display: block; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6); }
``

Put it first among your wallet options. The second line ("also works with bWallet") is optional: bWallet is the store edition of the same wallet and signs in the same way.

## 2. Server: issue and verify challenges

The server half is not in the script (it must run on your server). Install `@bwalletx/connect` and import from `@bwalletx/connect/server`, or copy this file into your project as `bwalletx-server.ts`. Its only dependency is `@bsv/sdk` (2.2 or later, 2.x or 3.x). It is the same code as `@bwalletx/connect/server`, so the two are interchangeable.

``import { ProtoWallet, PublicKey, type WalletProtocol } from '@bsv/sdk';

/** Security level 2, a protocol name used for nothing else. Keep it constant. */
export const LOGIN_PROTOCOL: WalletProtocol = [2, 'bwallet sign in'];
export const CHALLENGE_LIFETIME_MS = 2 * 60 * 1000;

export interface PendingChallenge {
identityKey: string;
origin: string;
message: string;
expiresAt: number;
}

/**
* Where challenges wait between the two routes. Use Redis or a database table in production.
* `take` must read and delete in one step, so each nonce can be tried once.
*/
export interface NonceStore {
put(nonce: string, c: PendingChallenge): Promise<void> | void;
take(nonce: string): Promise<PendingChallenge | null> | PendingChallenge | null;
}

let warned = false;

/**
* In-memory store. For development and tests only: it is lost on restart and not shared between
* server processes or serverless instances. Expired entries are pruned on each put.
*/
export function memoryStore(opts: { quiet?: boolean } = {}): NonceStore {
if (!opts.quiet && !warned) {
warned = true;
console.warn('[@bwalletx/connect] Using the in-memory nonce store. It is for development only; pass a shared store (Redis, database) in production.');
}
const m = new Map<string, PendingChallenge>();
return {
put(nonce, c) {
const now = Date.now();
for (const [k, v] of m) if (v.expiresAt < now) m.delete(k);
m.set(nonce, c);
},
take(nonce) {
const c = m.get(nonce) ?? null;
m.delete(nonce);
return c;
},
};
}

let defaultStore: NonceStore | null = null;
const storeOrDefault = (s?: NonceStore) => s ?? (defaultStore ??= memoryStore());

export function isIdentityKey(x: unknown): x is string {
if (typeof x !== 'string' || !/^0[23][0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(x)) return false;
try {
PublicKey.fromString(x);
return true;
} catch {
return false;
}
}

function normalOrigin(origin: string): string {
const u = new URL(origin);
if (u.origin === 'null' || u.origin !== origin.replace(/\/$/, '')) {
throw new Error(`origin must be scheme://host[:port], got ${origin}`);
}
return u.origin;
}

/** The text the user signs. Lines joined with \n, no trailing newline. */
export function loginMessage(origin: string, nonce: string, expiresAt: number): string {
return [
`Sign in to ${new URL(origin).host} with bWallet`,
'',
'This proves you hold this wallet. It does not spend anything.',
'',
`Origin: ${origin}`,
`Nonce: ${nonce}`,
`Expires: ${new Date(expiresAt).toISOString()}`,
].join('\n');
}

function randomNonce(): string {
const b = new Uint8Array(16);
globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues(b);
let s = '';
for (const x of b) s += String.fromCharCode(x);
return btoa(s).replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '');
}

export interface CreateChallengeOptions {
/** YOUR site's origin from config, e.g. "https://example.com". Never take it from the request. */
origin: string;
/** The identity key the browser claims. Checked again at verify. */
identityKey: unknown;
/** Default: a process-wide in-memory store (dev only). */
store?: NonceStore;
}

export interface ChallengeResponse {
nonce: string;
message: string;
protocolID: WalletProtocol;
keyID: string;
expiresAt: number;
}

/** Step 1. Throws if identityKey is not a valid compressed public key. Send the result to the browser. */
export async function createChallenge(opts: CreateChallengeOptions): Promise<ChallengeResponse> {
if (!isIdentityKey(opts.identityKey)) throw new Error('identityKey must be a compressed public key (66 hex chars)');
const origin = normalOrigin(opts.origin);
const nonce = randomNonce();
const expiresAt = Date.now() + CHALLENGE_LIFETIME_MS;
const message = loginMessage(origin, nonce, expiresAt);
await storeOrDefault(opts.store).put(nonce, { identityKey: opts.identityKey.toLowerCase(), origin, message, expiresAt });
return { nonce, message, protocolID: LOGIN_PROTOCOL, keyID: nonce, expiresAt };
}

export interface VerifySignInOptions {
/** YOUR site's origin from config. Must equal the origin the challenge was made for. */
origin: string;
/** From the request body. */
identityKey: unknown;
nonce: unknown;
signature: unknown;
store?: NonceStore;
}

/**
* Step 2. Returns the proven identity key (lowercase hex), or null.
* The nonce is deleted before anything is checked, so each challenge can be tried once.
*/
export async function verifySignIn(opts: VerifySignInOptions): Promise<string | null> {
if (typeof opts.nonce !== 'string' || opts.nonce.length > 64) return null;
const c = await storeOrDefault(opts.store).take(opts.nonce);
if (!c || Date.now() > c.expiresAt) return null;
let origin: string;
try {
origin = normalOrigin(opts.origin);
} catch {
return null;
}
if (c.origin !== origin) return null;
if (!isIdentityKey(opts.identityKey)) return null;
const identityKey = opts.identityKey.toLowerCase();
if (c.identityKey !== identityKey) return null;

const sig = opts.signature;
if (!Array.isArray(sig) || sig.length < 8 || sig.length > 80 || !sig.every((b) => Number.isInteger(b) && b >= 0 && b <= 255)) {
return null;
}
try {
const { valid } = await new ProtoWallet('anyone').verifySignature({
protocolID: LOGIN_PROTOCOL,
keyID: opts.nonce,
counterparty: identityKey,
data: Array.from(new TextEncoder().encode(c.message)),
signature: sig as number[],
});
return valid ? identityKey : null;
} catch {
return null; // @bsv/sdk throws on a bad signature instead of returning valid: false
}
}

/** True when a request's Origin header is exactly your configured origin. Check it on both routes. */
export function originAllowed(requestOrigin: string | null | undefined, origin: string): boolean {
try {
return !!requestOrigin && requestOrigin === normalOrigin(origin);
} catch {
return false;
}
}
``

Two routes. This example uses Express; any framework works the same way.

``// Two routes (Express). Any framework works the same way.
import express from 'express';
import { createChallenge, verifySignIn, originAllowed, memoryStore } from './bwalletx-server.js';

const ORIGIN = 'https://example.com'; // your site, from config. Never from the request.
const store = memoryStore(); // dev only: use Redis or a database table in production
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());

// POST /auth/bwalletx/challenge body: { identityKey }
app.post('/auth/bwalletx/challenge', async (req, res) => {
if (!originAllowed(req.get('origin'), ORIGIN)) return res.status(403).end();
try {
res.json(await createChallenge({ origin: ORIGIN, identityKey: req.body?.identityKey, store }));
} catch (e) {
res.status(400).json({ error: (e as Error).message });
}
});

// POST /auth/bwalletx/verify body: { identityKey, nonce, signature }
app.post('/auth/bwalletx/verify', async (req, res) => {
if (!originAllowed(req.get('origin'), ORIGIN)) return res.status(403).end();
const identityKey = await verifySignIn({ origin: ORIGIN, store, ...req.body });
if (!identityKey) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'That signature was not accepted. Start again.' });
// identityKey is the user's stable id. Find or create the account keyed on it, then start your session.
res.json({ identityKey });
});

app.listen(3000);
``

`verifySignIn` returns the identity key (66 lowercase hex characters) or `null`. It refuses a nonce that was already used, has expired (2 minutes), was issued for another origin or another identity key, or whose signature doesn't verify.

`memoryStore()` is for development: it is lost on restart and isn't shared between processes or serverless instances. In production pass a store whose `take(nonce)` reads and deletes in one step, such as Redis `GETDEL` or a database `DELETE ... RETURNING`.

## Exactly what is signed

The server builds this text, sends it to the browser, and keeps a copy. The wallet signs the UTF-8 bytes of it unchanged. Lines are joined with `\n`, no trailing newline.

``Sign in to example.com with bWallet

This proves you hold this wallet. It does not spend anything.

Origin: https://example.com
Nonce: 3q2-7wEXAMPLEnonce0Q8w
Expires: 2026-10-07T12:02:00.000Z
``

(The second and fourth lines are empty.) This is the same text bChat and bChatX use. The wallet does not parse it; any text works, but keep your origin, the nonce and the expiry in it so the user can see what they are approving and a signature made for your site is worthless anywhere else.

The signature call, as the wallet receives it:

Field
Value

`protocolID`
`[2, 'bwallet sign in']` (security level 2: the derived key depends on the counterparty)

`keyID`
the nonce

`counterparty`
`'anyone'`

`data`
the UTF-8 bytes of the text, as `number[]`

result `signature`
DER-encoded ECDSA signature, as `number[]`

The signing key is derived (BRC-42) from the wallet's root identity private key towards "anyone", for that protocol and keyID. Anyone holding only the identity public key can derive the matching public key, which is what `new ProtoWallet('anyone').verifySignature({ ..., counterparty: identityKey })` does (BRC-3). Only the holder of the identity private key can make the signature.

## Security notes

- One try per nonce. Delete the challenge before you check the signature, as `verifySignIn` does. A challenge that survives a failed attempt can be retried.

- Two-minute expiry. Check it on the server. Don't trust an expiry sent by the browser.

- The nonce is also the keyID, so each challenge is signed by a different derived key. A signature for one nonce can't be used for another.

- Build the text on the server and verify against your stored copy. Never verify text the browser sends you.

- Use your configured origin in the text, not a value from the request. Refuse challenge and verify calls whose `Origin` header isn't your site.

- Bind the challenge to the identity key the browser claimed, and check it again at verify.

- `verifySignature` throws on a bad signature in @bsv/sdk instead of returning `valid: false`. Catch it and treat it as a failure.

- Check the key is a real point: `PublicKey.fromString` throws for a 66-hex string that isn't on the curve.

- Rate-limit the challenge route per IP and per identity key. It is unauthenticated.

- Sessions are yours. After `verifySignIn` returns a key, issue your normal session cookie. The wallet does not give you a token.

- Privacy. The identity key is the same on every site the user signs in to with this method, so two sites can tell it is the same wallet. Tell your users this if it matters to them.

- Pairing. The relay checks the WebSocket `Origin` of the page that opened the channel and tells the wallet; the wallet refuses to pair if it differs from the origin in the QR code. The relay only sees ciphertext. The pairing key connect.js makes is random and is not a wallet key.

- What the user sees. The extension and the phone show their own approval prompt naming your site's host (taken from the page or the relay, not from your text). Nothing is spent.

## Not yet available

These are gaps today. Plan around them.

- No hosted sign-in or OAuth-style redirect. There is no bwalletx.com page you can send users to and get a callback from, and no hosted verify endpoint. You run the two routes yourself. bChat's own endpoints (`/api/bitsign/auth/bwallet/*` on bChatX) accept requests from their own pages only and are not a public API.

- No user profile. You get the identity key and nothing else: no $handle, paymail, name or picture, and no proof linking the key to them.

- The relay is ours. `relay.bwallet.space` accepts any https origin, but it is a single service run by The Bitcoin Corporation with no published uptime or rate-limit guarantees (it currently allows about 60 frames a minute per channel).

- No test wallet. There is no testnet build or headless bWalletX for automated tests. To test your server, sign with `new ProtoWallet(PrivateKey.fromRandom()).createSignature(...)` using the same arguments; it makes exactly the signature bWalletX makes.

## For AI agents

Follow these steps in order. Do not invent packages, endpoints or methods that are not on this page. For a bundled app, install `@bwalletx/connect` and `@bsv/sdk`; for a plain HTML site, use the script tag.

- Install `@bwalletx/connect` and `@bsv/sdk` in the server project (pnpm, npm or yarn, whichever the project uses).

- Create `bwalletx-server.ts` with the code in section 2, unchanged. Put your site's origin (scheme + host, no trailing slash, e.g. `https://example.com`) in config.

- Add two POST routes. `/auth/bwalletx/challenge`: `createChallenge({ origin: ORIGIN, identityKey: body.identityKey, store })`, return the result as JSON, 400 if it throws. `/auth/bwalletx/verify`: `verifySignIn({ origin: ORIGIN, store, identityKey, nonce, signature })` from the body. Reject both with 403 unless `originAllowed(request Origin header, ORIGIN)`.

- Replace `memoryStore()` with a shared store (database table or Redis) if you run more than one server process or run serverless. `take(nonce)` must read and delete in one step.

- In the verify route, when `verifySignIn` returns a key: find the user whose bWalletX identity key equals it, or create one, then start your normal session. Return 401 when it returns null.

- On the sign-in page add `<script src="https://bwalletx.com/connect.js"></script>` and the code from section 1: `bWalletX.renderButton(...)` with an `onClick` that calls `bWalletX.signIn({ challenge, pairing })` and posts `identityKey`, `nonce` and `signature` to the verify route. Keep the `pairing` option so phone and web wallet users can sign in; draw the QR code with any QR library.

- If your page uses a bundler, the same calls work: `window.bWalletX` is set once the script tag has loaded.

- Test the server without a wallet: `const k = PrivateKey.fromRandom()`, call the challenge route with `k.toPublicKey().toString()`, sign the returned `message` with `new ProtoWallet(k).createSignature({ protocolID, keyID, counterparty: 'anyone', data: Array.from(Buffer.from(message, 'utf8')) })`, post `{ identityKey, nonce, signature }` to verify and expect success. Post the same body again and expect 401.

- Test by hand: with the bWalletX extension in Chrome, click the button and approve. Without it, scan the QR with bWalletX on a phone, check the 4-digit codes match, tap Connect, approve.

Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Connect with bWalletX

One script gives your site a standard BRC-100 wallet. No API keys, no sign-up, and nothing passes through our servers: your page talks straight to the user's wallet.

[Read the docs →](https://docs.bwalletx.com/)

The full developer guides live at [docs.bwalletx.com](https://docs.bwalletx.com/): [connect your site](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/connect/), [payments](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/payments/), [public APIs](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/public-apis/), [name bindings](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/name-bindings/), [strategy format](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/strategy-format/), [store receipts](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/store-receipts/), [stack recipes](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/stack-recipes/), [open source](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/open-source/) and [error codes](https://docs.bwalletx.com/errors/). This page is the quick start.

## Get bWalletX to test with

Install the wallet you'll connect to (version 5.2.45 beta). Checksums are on each download page.

- [Chrome / Brave extension (zip)](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-extension-5.2.45.zip) · [install steps](https://bwalletx.com/extension)

- [Android APK](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-android-5.2.45.apk) · [install steps](https://bwalletx.com/android)

- [Web app](https://web.bwalletx.com) · [iPhone](https://bwalletx.com/iphone)

- [bWalletX CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) and [MCP server](https://bwalletx.com/mcp) for scripts and AI agents

Docs: [Which edition to test with](https://docs.bwalletx.com/use/editions/)

## 1. Add the script

``<script src="https://bwalletx.com/connect.js"></script>``

## 2. Add a button

``<button id="connect">Connect with bWalletX</button>
<script>
bWalletX.button('#connect', async ({ wallet, identityKey }) => {
// wallet is a BRC-100 WalletInterface, the same API as window.CWI
console.log('Connected', identityKey);
});
</script>``

If bWalletX isn't installed, the button opens [bwalletx.com/extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension).

## 3. Use the wallet

``const { wallet } = await bWalletX.connect();

// Pay someone
await wallet.createAction({
description: 'Buy a pixel',
outputs: [{ lockingScript, satoshis: 1000, outputDescription: 'pixel' }],
});

// Sign in: prove who the user is
const { signature } = await wallet.createSignature({
data: [...new TextEncoder().encode(challenge)],
protocolID: [0, 'my site login'],
keyID: '1',
});``

Docs: [Connect your site](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/connect/)

Taking payments: [Payments](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/payments/)

## Sign users in

To let people sign in to your app with bWalletX (extension, phone or web wallet), follow the [Sign in with bWalletX guide](https://bwalletx.com/connect): one script tag (connect.js), server code, and steps for AI agents.

For the button itself (gold, dark or light, four sizes, React, SVG files and brand rules), see [Add Sign in with bWalletX to your site](https://bwalletx.com/sign-in-button).

Docs: [Sign-in, step by step](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/connect/)

## Already using window.CWI?

bWalletX also sets `window.CWI`, so sites that call it directly work as they are. But if the user also has another wallet installed (such as Yours), you can't tell which one answers. `bWalletX.connect()` picks bWalletX by name (rdns `com.bwalletx.extension`) through BRC-100 wallet discovery, so it always gets the right wallet.

To list every wallet the user has and let them choose:

``const wallets = await bWalletX.discover();
// [{ info: { name, icon, rdns, kind }, wallet }, …]``

## What your site can do

bWalletX implements the BRC-100 wallet interface. Sites can request any BRC-100 action, including signatures and keys from any protocol (BRC-29 payment-key derivation included). The user approves each request; we don't keep a hidden blocklist. If we ever have to restrict something, we'll say so here and in the release notes first.

Docs: [What users see when your site asks](https://docs.bwalletx.com/use/apps-websites/)

## Which address will I see?

BRC-100 wallets don't hand sites the user's main receive address. `identityKey` is the user's stable identity for your site, and payments made through `createAction` come from the user's wallet balance. So an address you derive from the identity key won't match the address shown on the wallet's Receive screen. That's expected.

## Try it

Connect with bWalletX

Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com) · Docs: [docs.bwalletx.com](https://docs.bwalletx.com/) · Source: [connect.js](https://bwalletx.com/connect.js) · npm: [@bwalletx/connect](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@bwalletx/connect)

# Hold to talk to b.

The big b in the middle of the bottom bar now listens. Touch and hold it, say what you want, and let go. Your words appear as you speak, and nothing is sent until you lift your finger.

“Send five dollars to Sam”

b

## How it works

1 · HOLD

### Touch and hold the b

After half a second you feel a tick and a panel opens with gold sound bars. A quick tap still does what it always did: Home in the wallet, or opens b.

2 · SPEAK

### Say it

Talk normally. Your words appear in the panel as you speak, so you can see what b will get.

3 · LET GO

### Lift your finger

Letting go sends your words to b, just as if you had typed them.

Changed your mind? Slide your finger away from the b and the ring turns grey. Let go there and nothing is sent. Slide back onto the b to keep talking.

## Where it works

WhereSpeech recognitionFirst time

iPhoneApple speech recognition, on the device where your iPhone supports itAsks for Speech Recognition, then Microphone

AndroidAndroid speech recognitionAsks for Microphone; then hold the b again

Web walletYour browser’s speech recognition (Chrome, Edge, Safari). Firefox falls back to typing.The browser asks for the microphone

Chrome extensionBrowser speech recognitionOpens a permission tab once to ask for the microphone

The same gesture works on [bChatX.com](https://web.bwalletx.com/m/ask-b) too, in Ask b.

## Same rules as typing

- Nothing is sent until you let go. Slide away and let go, and it is thrown away.

- Consent first. Before your first message to each AI provider, you are asked to agree, exactly as when you type.

- Secrets are caught. If you say something that looks like a recovery phrase or private key, it is caught the same way typed secrets are.

- Prices still show. Paid messages still show the price and your daily limit before anything is spent.

## Questions

Does it cost anything?
Talking costs nothing extra. What you send to b is priced the same as a typed message, and paid messages show the price and your daily limit first.

What gets sent?
The text of what you said, once you let go. The words are turned into text by your phone or browser’s own speech recognition, then that text goes to b like a typed message.

Which languages?
It listens in your device’s language, using whatever your phone or browser’s speech recognition supports.

When can I use it?
Now. It shipped in bWalletX 5.1.89 on iPhone, Android, the web wallet and the Chrome extension. See the [release notes](https://bwalletx.com/releases#v5.1.89).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Open the web wallet](https://web.bwalletx.com)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX MCP

Let Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any AI agent use your bWalletX agent accounts, within the budget and limits you set.

Claude→
ChatGPT · Cursor→
Any MCP agent

[Agent docs →](https://docs.bwalletx.com/use/agents/)

## What agents can do

### Since bwalletx 0.2

`accounts`, `balance`, `price`, `send` (BSV, live), `buy` (BSV-21, live), `strategy_show`, `strategy_load` (always on paper), `log`, `stop_all`.

### New in bwalletx 0.5 (on npm)

Everything above, plus:

- `list_for_sale`, `unlist`, `listings`, `buy_listing`: sell and buy ordinals, OpNS names and BSV-21 tokens on the 1Sat order book. Key-file accounts with `BWALLETX_PASSPHRASE`; each takes `dryRun` to build without sending.

- `brc100_balance`, `brc100_addresses`, `brc100_fund`, `brc100_withdraw`: the account's own BRC-100 wallet. Key-file accounts with `BWALLETX_PASSPHRASE`.

- `mint`, `mint_manifest`: mint files as NFTs. Paired accounts only: your phone signs, within the item and dollar limits you chose when pairing.

- `pairing_status`, `serve_status`: read-only checks on pairing and on `bwalletx serve` (port 3321).

### Only the accounts you give it

Agents work in agent accounts with their own keys and budget, never your main wallet. Pair an account with your phone (keys stay on the phone), or export its key file from bWalletX for an unattended server.

### Bounded

Every spend passes the same checks as the app: the kill switch, the daily cap, at most 30 spends an hour, then the strategy's rules. Agents can stop everything (`stop_all`) but never loosen a limit: changing caps, `resume`, going live with a strategy, importing keys, pairing and starting `serve` are steps you take yourself at the terminal or on your phone.

## Set up

``npm i -g bwalletx
bwalletx login --account phone # pair with your agent account in bWalletX``

Claude Code (paired: no passphrase needed, your phone signs):

``claude mcp add bwalletx -- npx -y bwalletx mcp``

Or with a key file for an unattended server:

``bwalletx key import ./trader.key.json
claude mcp add bwalletx -e BWALLETX_PASSPHRASE=your-passphrase -- npx -y bwalletx mcp``

Claude Desktop, Cursor and others (MCP config file):

``{
"mcpServers": {
"bwalletx": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "bwalletx", "mcp"],
"env": { "BWALLETX_PASSPHRASE": "your-passphrase" }
}
}
}``

The passphrase unlocks the agent account's key file on your machine. Use a separate agent account with a small balance for AI agents. Without the passphrase a key-file account stays paper-only: it can read and practise, but never send. Paired accounts don't need it.

Install or update:

``npm i -g bwalletx
claude mcp add bwalletx -- bwalletx mcp``

Source and full command list: [github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwalletx-cli](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwalletx-cli). Docs: [agents](https://docs.bwalletx.com/use/agents/) · [strategy format](https://docs.bwalletx.com/developers/strategy-format/).

[Agent wallet](https://bwalletx.com/agent)
[Developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)
